xVi3bDDDSs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is technically strong, clearly written, and rigorous, with the proportional-regime error characterization and the l1-l_infinity hybrid norm's sharp transition as interesting results.
xVi3bDDDSs.main_concern: The connection to grokking is tenuous: results concern sharp transitions across norms or regularization strength rather than delayed generalization over training time, and the jump partly comes from deliberately chosen norms and the square-root loss.

8c2PxIbnLQ.one_liner: Proves lower bounds and impossibility results showing spectral, random-walk, and adjacency graph tokenizations induce distinct transformer depth regimes.
8c2PxIbnLQ.problem: The choice of graph-to-token map for transformers determines which structural information is exposed, yet its effect on transformer expressivity is not well characterized.
8c2PxIbnLQ.method: They analyze spectral, random-walk, and adjacency tokenizations theoretically, proving which are lossy or ill-conditioned and that limited-depth transformers cannot in general convert between tokenization families, and complement this with controlled experiments.
8c2PxIbnLQ.key_idea: Treat tokenization as part of transformer expressivity and prove depth separations and impossibility results between tokenization families.
8c2PxIbnLQ.evidence: Proofs of lower bounds and impossibility results, plus controlled experiments on synthetic and real-world graph tasks.
8c2PxIbnLQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and timely, the theory covers the three main tokenization classes, and the experiments on synthetic and real graph tasks show differences between tokenizations.
8c2PxIbnLQ.main_concern: Theory and experiments are not tightly linked (unnormalized versus normalized Laplacian), some results match established intuitions, and evidence for combining tokenizations is limited.

owQV3pPODJ.one_liner: Fuses protein sequences and four biomedical knowledge graphs with gated end-to-end learning for cold-start PPI prediction.
owQV3pPODJ.problem: Cold-start PPI predictors use only partial modalities, compute new-to-known protein similarity offline per modality, and give single-modal, feature-oriented explanations.
owQV3pPODJ.method: ECMLF encodes amino acid sequences and four external biomedical knowledge graphs, combines similarity modeling and PPI prediction through an adaptive gated fusion module trained end to end, and adds a dual-pathway explanation mechanism.
owQV3pPODJ.key_idea: An adaptive gated fusion module learns new-to-known protein similarity jointly with PPI prediction, instead of computing similarity offline per modality.
owQV3pPODJ.evidence: Per reviews, protein-held-out splits cover known-new and new-new pairs against selected baselines, with component ablations and explanations scored against annotations; the abstract is cut off before the results.
owQV3pPODJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating on held-out proteins, combining sequence and knowledge-graph modalities with joint optimization, and the dual-pathway explanations.
owQV3pPODJ.main_concern: The method is not shown to be cold-start-specific, and dataset details and robustness to missing or sparse knowledge-graph modalities are not established.

6wpvvIkjeL.one_liner: Proves checkable rank conditions for NTK positive definiteness and finite-width gradient descent convergence for PINNs with linear constraints.
6wpvvIkjeL.problem: NTK analyses of PINNs usually assume the limiting kernel is positive definite without a way to check it for concrete PDE constraints.
6wpvvIkjeL.method: For strong-form, weak-form, and nonlocal linear constraints, shows limiting-NTK positive definiteness is equivalent to a rank condition on a finite coefficient, functional, or moment matrix, then gives width and step-size conditions under which full-batch gradient descent decreases the loss geometrically.
6wpvvIkjeL.key_idea: Reduce NTK positive definiteness to a pre-training rank test on the constraint design matrix that detects structural zero modes, then transfer the kernel gap to finite width.
6wpvvIkjeL.evidence: Theorems for ordinary two-layer PINNs with smooth nonpolynomial activations such as tanh, plus controlled experiments checking the certificates and the finite-width mechanism.
6wpvvIkjeL.claimed_gains: With high probability the empirical NTK keeps at least half the limiting gap and full-batch gradient descent decreases the training loss geometrically at every iteration; no numeric experimental gains stated.
6wpvvIkjeL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find turning an assumed NTK spectral gap into a computable rank condition on the constraints the main contribution, covering vector-valued, weak-form, and nonlocal cases, with sound core logic.
6wpvvIkjeL.main_concern: Applicability is limited to linear constraints and two-layer networks, and experiments do not verify the width and step-size conditions, so the practical usefulness of the quantitative bounds is unclear.

slOOhYwTWQ.one_liner: Risk-Calibrated Negative Suppression attenuates GRPO negative advantages likely to flip sign under later feedback, using retrieval rank as the cue.
slOOhYwTWQ.problem: In RL for generative recommendation, incomplete user feedback means recommendations with negative advantages may still match user interests, so suppressing them can discourage plausible items.
slOOhYwTWQ.method: The paper measures sign conflicts between observed and validation-feedback advantages, finds they are more likely among negative-advantage recommendations with better observed retrieval ranks, and builds RCNS to selectively attenuate such updates. A continuous attenuation function is calibrated against a feedback set.
slOOhYwTWQ.key_idea: Attenuate negative-advantage updates by a rank-based, batch-relative risk score, since better-ranked negatives more often flip sign under later feedback.
slOOhYwTWQ.evidence: Three Amazon Reviews'23 recommendation domains, comparing GRPO and two author-reimplemented HPO variants, plus a diagnostic sign-conflict analysis with fixed rollout groups.
slOOhYwTWQ.claimed_gains: The abstract (cut off before the results) reports that 5.2%--13.1% of negative-advantage recommendations receive positive advantages under validation feedback; RCNS performance numbers are not stated.
slOOhYwTWQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unreliable negative advantages under incomplete feedback is a real, well-diagnosed failure mode and that the rank-based attenuation cue is intuitive and observable during training.
slOOhYwTWQ.main_concern: Evidence is limited to three same-platform Amazon domains with narrow, partly self-implemented baselines and uncertain statistical significance, and calibration still requires an additional feedback set.

PaWTanwG91.one_liner: Flow-matching latent-action policy distilled from a LAM teacher, adapted to new embodiments with a fresh action decoder.
PaWTanwG91.problem: Discrete latent actions create a granularity bottleneck, and continuous alternatives serve as world-modeling proxies that need a further planning step to produce executable actions.
PaWTanwG91.method: UniLAP models latent-action chunks with flow matching, bypassing future frames at inference, and distills a LAM teacher with a flow-adaptive objective. A latent-conditioned motion predictor predicts correspondence-aligned feature changes so latents encode motion from videos; a new robot attaches a fresh action decoder with light finetuning.
PaWTanwG91.key_idea: Distills a LAM teacher's continuous latent actions into a flow-matching policy conditioned only on current observation, with a correspondence-based motion predictor as auxiliary supervision.
PaWTanwG91.evidence: Pretrained on multi-source videos at 1.1B parameters; evaluated on hand pose forecasting, single-arm and humanoid manipulation (including SimplerEnv), and real-world deployment.
PaWTanwG91.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports outperforming latent-action and VLA baselines across hand pose forecasting, single-arm and humanoid manipulation, and real-world deployment, without numeric margins.
PaWTanwG91.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a practical route from action-free video to executable control and broad evaluation across hand-pose forecasting, simulated manipulation, and real-world deployment.
PaWTanwG91.main_concern: The contribution over existing continuous latent-action policies (CLAM, villa-X, LatentVLA) is not isolated, and the correspondence-residual motion supervision is not shown to separate object motion from camera motion.

JDx2HmIm8f.one_liner: Distills heterogeneous DNA language models into one compact agglomerative student, then post-trains it on labeled sequences.
JDx2HmIm8f.problem: DNA language models have complementary strengths with no single model dominating, and deeper layers add little downstream signal, suggesting the capabilities can be consolidated.
JDx2HmIm8f.method: DNA-RADIO distills multiple DNA LM teachers into a single compact student that is 3.24-29.4x smaller than its teachers across two sizes. It then enriches the representations through post-training on large-scale labeled sequences while preserving the distilled knowledge.
JDx2HmIm8f.key_idea: Multi-teacher agglomerative distillation, taken from the RADIO family in vision, applied to DNA language models, followed by labeled post-training that preserves inherited knowledge.
JDx2HmIm8f.evidence: Layer-wise linear probing and CKA analysis of DNA LMs, frozen-feature linear evaluation on held-out sequences, and teacher ablations.
JDx2HmIm8f.claimed_gains: Distillation using only unlabeled sequences improves average performance by 1.0-15.85% over its teachers while the student is 3.24-29.4x smaller, and a single strong teacher alone recovers 87-96% of the improvement.
JDx2HmIm8f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that consolidating complementary DNA models into a compact student is useful and motivated by the layer-wise probing and CKA analysis, with competitive results across task types.
JDx2HmIm8f.main_concern: Key controls are missing: no teacher-free continued-pretraining baseline and no ablation of individual teachers or initialization, so gains cannot be attributed to multi-teacher distillation.

VwjImKfwwW.one_liner: Learns evidence routing for multi-agent LLMs by modeling how sharing value depends on how many agents already hold the evidence.
VwjImKfwwW.problem: In multi-agent search systems, whether evidence is useful to one agent does not determine how widely it should be shared.
VwjImKfwwW.method: MERGE uses paired interventions that differ by one additional agent to learn how the benefit of sharing depends on the current holder count. It combines this with agent-specific usefulness and communication cost and selects routing decisions jointly.
VwjImKfwwW.key_idea: A learned holder-count-dependent group effect, trained from paired one-extra-agent interventions, is combined with per-agent usefulness and cost in a joint routing decision.
VwjImKfwwW.evidence: Nine QA dataset-backbone settings with HotpotQA/Qwen2.5-14B as the primary setting, plus ablations of the group term and joint routing.
VwjImKfwwW.claimed_gains: MERGE achieves the highest mean F1 and EM across nine settings; on HotpotQA/Qwen2.5-14B it reaches 0.716 F1, 2.4 points above the strongest controlled baseline, using 11.8% fewer tokens.
VwjImKfwwW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the holder-dependent view of sharing value is a meaningful distinction and that the multi-dataset, multi-backbone controlled comparisons support it.
VwjImKfwwW.main_concern: The learned group effect may reflect the fixed majority-voting aggregation rather than informational value, and the fixed-team setting and handcrafted features limit the practical case.

nhWwjvB9aj.one_liner: Distills dense traversability and cost-to-go pseudo-labels from static RGB images into a planner-agnostic navigation representation.
nhWwjvB9aj.problem: Monocular RGB navigation needs reliable traversability estimation, but modular approaches depend on extra sensing or interaction-heavy pipelines and end-to-end ones infer structure indirectly from trajectory supervision.
nhWwjvB9aj.method: VGN uses vision foundation models with classical planning algorithms to generate dense traversability and cost-to-go pseudo-labels from static RGB images without trajectory supervision or robot interaction, and trains a student planning representation model on them. The representation plugs into multiple downstream planners.
nhWwjvB9aj.key_idea: Generate traversability and cost-to-go labels from images by combining foundation-model segmentation with classical planning, then distill them into a student network.
nhWwjvB9aj.evidence: Experiments on multiple outdoor datasets, closed-loop simulation environments, and real-world deployment on a Unitree Go2 robot.
nhWwjvB9aj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating dense planning supervision from static images without demonstrations or robot interaction is a practical, scalable idea whose representation works with several downstream planners.
nhWwjvB9aj.main_concern: The learned cost-to-go head shows no clear advantage over traversability plus Dijkstra in the controlled tables, and 2D image-space costs and pseudo-label quality ignore 3D geometry.

vHyTpsgrOW.one_liner: Physics-guided lithography world model using latent flow matching with regional physical gradient correction and difference-preserving self-evolving training.
vHyTpsgrOW.problem: Lithography process responses vary across stages and local regions, which makes reliable multi-stage modeling of the Layout-Mask-Resist Image-ADI pipeline hard.
vHyTpsgrOW.method: Formulates the multi-stage process as latent-space flow matching with process-conditioned velocity fields integrated numerically. A physical dynamics correction evaluates regional response discrepancies with stage-specific approximate physical operators and couples their gradients to correct the latent velocity field, and self-evolving joint training uses paired same-layout supervision across process conditions to guide intermediate-state recomposition and downstream replay.
vHyTpsgrOW.key_idea: Correct latent flow velocities with regional gradients of approximate physical operators, and train with paired same-layout supervision to preserve process-induced differences between stages.
vHyTpsgrOW.evidence: Experiments against lithography baselines such as LMLitho, LithoNet, and LithoDreamer, including an unseen 55 nm process condition, according to reviews (abstract truncated).
vHyTpsgrOW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after 'Experiments show that Flow-Litho'; the TL;DR claims improved fidelity and parameter recovery).
vHyTpsgrOW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a physics-guided world model for multi-stage lithography is meaningful and that the regional physical velocity correction is an interpretable mechanism with gains over baselines, especially on unseen conditions.
vHyTpsgrOW.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to LithoDreamer and existing physics-guided flow methods, and reported metrics are inconsistent (mIoU 96.35% versus mPA 95.23% despite the stated mIoU <= mPA).

ytYtUV701p.one_liner: Builds paired shadow-removal data from shadow image-mask pairs with an agentic workflow of physics-motivated generation, failure detection, retry, and correction.
ytYtUV701p.problem: Paired shadow-removal training data have barely changed in nearly a decade because capturing a shadow-free target requires removing the occluder while keeping scene, camera, and illumination fixed.
ytYtUV701p.method: An offline agentic workflow combining physics-motivated generation, failure detection, feedback-driven retry, candidate selection, and deterministic correction turns existing shadow detection image-mask pairs into image-mask-target triplets, forming AgenticShadow across general scenes, faces, and remote sensing.
ytYtUV701p.key_idea: Generate shadow-free targets for existing shadow-detection images with a generate-detect-retry-select-correct loop built on physical prompts instead of capturing paired photos.
ytYtUV701p.evidence: A 17,138-triplet dataset compared with previous shadow removal work on Color Distribution Difference, and existing shadow removal models retrained on it and evaluated on its test sets and cross-domain.
ytYtUV701p.claimed_gains: The construction workflow reduces Color Distribution Difference by 50.5% over previous shadow removal work, and training existing models on AgenticShadow reduces macro LAB RMSE on its test sets by 19.7-37.5%.
ytYtUV701p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the dataset is larger and broader than prior paired data (faces, remote sensing), that it improves several restoration architectures, and that the appendix gives useful construction statistics and failure analyses.
ytYtUV701p.main_concern: Evaluation relies on references generated by the same pipeline with no human validation or held-out real paired benchmark such as SRD or WSRD+.

C6corWGbYW.one_liner: RMF embeds ranking-based fingerprint probes in task prompts to detect LLM API model substitution at runtime.
C6corWGbYW.problem: Users of third-party LLM aggregation platforms cannot verify which model serves a request, and existing black-box fingerprinting verifies only before deployment, not during actual task execution.
C6corWGbYW.method: RMF builds compact behavioral fingerprints from model-specific preferences over underdetermined ranking tasks and embeds lightweight probes directly in real task prompts. An adaptive probe search framework selects discriminative fingerprints for each task context.
C6corWGbYW.key_idea: Read a model's identity from its preferences on underdetermined ranking questions embedded in the task prompt, with probes chosen by adaptive search per task context.
C6corWGbYW.evidence: Evaluation on 23 frontier LLMs across four real-world application domains in binary verification and multiclass identification settings (fine-grained 20 models and coarse-grained 8 families per reviews), against baselines, with ablations.
C6corWGbYW.claimed_gains: Substantially improves model identification in binary verification and multiclass identification over baselines, with no statistically significant task-performance degradation and negligible token overhead; no figures given in the abstract.
C6corWGbYW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, that verifying the model inside the task request is a sensible direction, and that the method performs well with multiple ablations.
C6corWGbYW.main_concern: No evaluation against an adaptive malicious provider: because the probes are functionally separate from the task, a provider could detect them and route probe and task to different models.

quTM5AcTkn.one_liner: Multi-exit concept bottleneck model with concept-depth-preference distillation for shallow exits and a key-concept-calibrated MaxProb exit rule.
quTM5AcTkn.problem: Concept bottleneck models on heavy vision-language backbones are costly to deploy, and early exiting must preserve concept-level evidence rather than only class labels.
quTM5AcTkn.method: PACE keeps the visual backbone fixed and trains concept exits at intermediate depths. Concept-Preference Guided Distillation builds concept-specific teachers at several depths with fusion-confidence-weighted supervision, and Readiness-Calibrated MaxProb adjusts exit decisions using key-concept support.
quTM5AcTkn.key_idea: Train shallow concept exits with concept-specific multi-depth teachers weighted by fusion confidence, and gate early exits by MaxProb adjusted for key-concept support in the current bottleneck.
quTM5AcTkn.evidence: Per reviews, experiments on five datasets with matched-speedup and forced-exit ablations; the abstract text is cut off before results.
quTM5AcTkn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a meaningful problem (efficient CBM inference that keeps intermediate concept representations) and shows competitive accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across datasets with controlled ablations.
quTM5AcTkn.main_concern: Limited novelty over the preference and multi-layer fusion mechanisms of MVP-CBM, and the preference-specific gain is small because uniform multi-depth supervision already provides most of the improvement.

NoFlLFm4dl.one_liner: Sharp curvature-time risk laws for projected gradient descent via an interaction-dissipation argument with matching upper and lower bounds.
NoFlLFm4dl.problem: Classical stability bounds can overstate the statistical cost of running gradient descent longer on the same finite training sample.
NoFlLFm4dl.method: The paper derives worst-case expected excess-risk laws for projected GD on the unit ball with convex, 1-Lipschitz, L-smooth losses, using an interaction-dissipation principle. It extends beyond convexity with weakly nonconvex instances separating the last iterate, a sampled iterate, and the full average.
NoFlLFm4dl.key_idea: Balance higher-order sample interactions against the stabilizing effect of losses unchanged by sample replacement, instead of accumulating worst-case perturbations round by round.
NoFlLFm4dl.evidence: Theory only: matching upper and lower bounds and explicit constructions; per reviews there are no numerical experiments.
NoFlLFm4dl.claimed_gains: At unit smoothness the worst-case excess risk is Theta(min{1, q^-1 + n^-1/2 + q n^-3/2}), staying at Theta(n^-1/2) at q of order n and reaching constant order only at q of order n^(3/2).
NoFlLFm4dl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cumulative-step-size analysis with matching upper and lower bounds improves on the classical q/n stability rate and clarifies when prolonged training genuinely hurts population risk.
NoFlLFm4dl.main_concern: Restrictive assumptions (projected GD, bounded domain, smooth Lipschitz convex losses) and proofs relegated to a very long appendix, with little main-text intuition and no experiments.

2NzWjWEMPb.one_liner: Rational-function relaxations of sigmoid-like activations, parametric in order k, give sound, convergent, k-complete robustness verification.
2NzWjWEMPb.problem: Verifying sigmoid-like networks needs relaxations that capture transcendental activation relations faithfully while staying efficient to verify, and linear relaxations are loose.
2NzWjWEMPb.method: The authors symbolically derive a family of rational-function relaxations parametric in order k that are sound and convergent, yielding a k-complete procedure that certifies robust instances with strictly positive margin at a finite order. They build a scalable verification method on this family.
2NzWjWEMPb.key_idea: Replace linear bounds on sigmoid-like activations with rational-function bounds derived from truncated exponential expansions, whose tightness increases with relaxation order k.
2NzWjWEMPb.evidence: Image classification experiments (six feedforward networks on MNIST and similar data per reviews) against representative linear-relaxation baselines on certified margin bounds and certified accuracy.
2NzWjWEMPb.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says tighter certified margin bounds and improved certified robustness accuracy than linear-relaxation baselines, without numbers).
2NzWjWEMPb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving beyond linear relaxations to rational ones, with soundness and k-completeness proofs, addresses a timely and under-explored problem for smooth-activation verification.
2NzWjWEMPb.main_concern: Limited scale and benchmarks: only small fully connected networks (at most three hidden layers of 200 neurons) with uniformly sigmoid or tanh activations and 10-second timeouts, with no scaling study.

5kyGbB44F3.one_liner: VDGS ranks 3DGS split candidates by partitioning parent backward signals into two virtual child domains before densifying.
5kyGbB44F3.problem: Fast 3DGS training must improve fidelity under limited densification, but parent-level gradient or error averages hide view frequency and differences between the two sides of a proposed split.
5kyGbB44F3.method: Parent gradient statistics nominate candidates, the prescribed split geometry partitions their pixelwise backward signals into two virtual children, and VDGS combines activity on both sides with the difference in their net gradient directions, accumulated across views, reusing the regular backward pass.
5kyGbB44F3.key_idea: Split-aligned virtual probe: divide a parent's pixelwise gradients by the split geometry and score both sides' activity and gradient-direction difference.
5kyGbB44F3.evidence: Matched growth budgets on nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes (runs averaged per scene) against AbsGS; reviews cite further comparisons with FastGS on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending.
5kyGbB44F3.claimed_gains: Full VDGS gains 0.45 dB in mean PSNR over direct AbsGS, with higher SSIM and lower LPIPS.
5kyGbB44F3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a practical densification-allocation problem with an intuitive, low-overhead probe that reuses existing backward gradients and improves over baselines.
5kyGbB44F3.main_concern: Table 4 shows a simple accumulated parent score already captures most of the gain, so the two-sided scoring adds little (slightly lower PSNR, small SSIM and LPIPS gains), and some baselines are missing.

prPMs3G1Ju.one_liner: Empirical study showing phase-wise full-model experience replay scales VLA continual learning to 125 RoboCasa365 tasks.
prPMs3G1Ju.problem: VLA continual learning beyond a hundred tasks is underexplored, and prior work studies task-wise updates on small task sets.
prPMs3G1Ju.method: Studies phase-wise continual learning, where each update jointly learns a batch of new tasks, on LIBERO and RoboCasa365, comparing full-model experience replay with LoRA variants (rank and learning-rate sweeps), merging, and other methods, and analyzing how LoRA concentrates update energy.
prPMs3G1Ju.key_idea: Phase-wise joint learning of task batches with full-model experience replay on a small replayed fraction of old data, rather than LoRA or one-task-at-a-time updates.
prPMs3G1Ju.evidence: LIBERO and RoboCasa365 with four phases and 125 tasks, matched task sets and training budgets, and LoRA rank and learning-rate sweeps.
prPMs3G1Ju.claimed_gains: Learning larger task groups improves acquisition and retention under matched budgets, and full-model ER continually acquires new capabilities while preserving old ones using only 2% of each old task's data across four phases and 125 tasks.
prPMs3G1Ju.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large-scale, phase-wise evaluation is practically relevant and the analysis of task composition and update granularity is informative.
prPMs3G1Ju.main_concern: It evaluates existing methods rather than proposing one, rests on a single seed, backbone, and task order, fixes the replay configuration (2% memory, 31.25% old-task batch share) without ablation, and cannot predict which support tasks help retention.

6VEed8URmV.one_liner: Lo-GRAD scores tabular anomalies by how poorly a record's local feature representations align with its global representation.
6VEed8URmV.problem: Detecting anomalies in tabular data when only normal records are available for training.
6VEed8URmV.method: A Transformer encoder produces local (per-feature) and global representations trained with a contrastive objective that raises dot-product alignment for local-global pairs from the same record and lowers it across records, plus masked-feature modeling for local and reconstruction for global representations. Records with higher local-global misalignment get higher anomaly scores.
6VEed8URmV.key_idea: Anomalies break the alignment between per-feature local and record-level global representations learned contrastively on normal data, and each local-global pair score gives a feature attribution.
6VEed8URmV.evidence: 26 ADBench datasets per the abstract (a review says 25), with ablations, repeated runs, and comparisons of scoring functions and encoder versus projected spaces.
6VEed8URmV.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off after 'Across 26 ADBench datasets and without'.
6VEed8URmV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clearly explained and intuitive, the paper is well written, and the results are competitive with thorough ablations.
6VEed8URmV.main_concern: It is unclear the gains come from the local-global alignment objective, since the best scores use encoder-space distances while projected-space scores, where the contrastive loss acts, are much worse, and the comparison changes training settings and uses only a benchmark subset.

fO2bvBS5QW.one_liner: AIRGraph accepts a learned partial assignment only when a problem-specific repair credit covers its certified objective-loss bound.
fO2bvBS5QW.problem: Fixing predicted variables in graph optimization can remove every high-quality solution through one wrong decision, and accuracy or confidence do not measure this risk.
fO2bvBS5QW.method: AIRGraph upper-bounds the objective loss of a proposed partial assignment, credits a problem-specific repair, and accepts the proposal only when the credit covers the loss, with an independent fallback preserving the classical approximation factor. It is instantiated for weighted Vertex Cover, weighted Maximum Independent Set, and signed MaxCut/Max-2Lin.
fO2bvBS5QW.key_idea: Augmented-instance regret (AIR): bound the structural objective loss of a commitment before enforcing it and gate acceptance by repair credit.
fO2bvBS5QW.evidence: Exact audits on finite instances found no violations, with experiments on 500 BA-small and 480 BA-large Barabasi-Albert graphs.
fO2bvBS5QW.claimed_gains: On 500 BA-small graphs the flow bound is tighter than the cheap bound on all 2,008 tested proposals, changes 541 gate decisions, and improves 149 returned solutions.
fO2bvBS5QW.reviewer_consensus: Two of three reviewers agree the problem-specific certificates (the Vertex Cover local-LP strengthening and MaxCut flow bound) are substantive and give tighter guarantees without assuming accurate predictions.
fO2bvBS5QW.main_concern: The generic framework is algebraically simple and its practical advantage is unclear, since size rules reproduce the selection frontier and prediction-seeded search beats AIRGraph under matched budgets, and one reviewer found the writing hard to follow.

NDJt8PYdvb.one_liner: A pending excerpt set delays compression until a learned policy commits source-verified facts to bounded memory.
NDJt8PYdvb.problem: Early compression of long-context inputs can discard details whose relevance becomes clear only after later evidence.
NDJt8PYdvb.method: CoEM keeps potentially useful source excerpts verbatim in a pending set and learns to retain, discard, or promote them into committed memory. A frozen verifier checks support for proposed facts, and reinforcement learning combines evidence-level and final-answer rewards.
NDJt8PYdvb.key_idea: Retain unresolved source excerpts and learn when to commit verifier-supported facts as later context clarifies relevance.
NDJt8PYdvb.evidence: Experiments use three Wikipedia-based multi-hop QA benchmarks, include inputs spanning 6,400 documents, and ablate pending retention, verification, rewards, and evidence-gap length.
NDJt8PYdvb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value preserving unresolved evidence verbatim and verifying committed facts to address premature information loss.
NDJt8PYdvb.main_concern: Reviewers find adaptive commitment timing insufficiently isolated from simply retaining more uncompressed evidence under different memory allocations.

JfqIggu4PZ.one_liner: Timestamp-derived Voronoi cell widths weight patch aggregation by physical time while preserving sampling patterns through a separate condition.
JfqIggu4PZ.problem: Equal-weight aggregation in irregular time series measures observation density rather than physical-time coverage when sampling correlates with content.
JfqIggu4PZ.method: VQPatch separates temporal support from aggregation measure and weights each observation by its representative Voronoi cell width. It retains observation-pattern information as a bounded prediction condition.
JfqIggu4PZ.key_idea: Replace unit observation weights with Voronoi temporal-cell widths and route sampling-pattern information through a separate bounded condition.
JfqIggu4PZ.evidence: The paper derives a covariance identity and quadrature approximation guarantee, with four-dataset comparisons, 17 baselines, component ablations, and controlled sampling-shift experiments.
JfqIggu4PZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating patch support from aggregation measure and the simple, theoretically motivated timestamp-based weighting.
JfqIggu4PZ.main_concern: Reviewers find single-seed component and sampling-shift tests insufficient to establish the reliability of small reported effects.

Nw1PoClmkZ.one_liner: Manually designed multi-step world-state tasks test how generative models integrate references, reasoning, and coherent visual prediction.
Nw1PoClmkZ.problem: Generative benchmarks underexplore successive world-state prediction requiring coupled understanding and generation from heterogeneous references.
Nw1PoClmkZ.method: WorldCast organizes capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and constructs multi-step visual prediction cases across eight categories. It evaluates task completion, causal plausibility, and visual consistency.
Nw1PoClmkZ.key_idea: Require successive visual world states from multimodal observations and heterogeneous references, then score completion, causal plausibility, and consistency.
Nw1PoClmkZ.evidence: WorldCast evaluates 12 representative models on 320 manually designed cases across eight categories, with human comparisons, judge checks, and repeated generations noted by a reviewer.
Nw1PoClmkZ.claimed_gains: The GPT-Image-2.5 System scores 72.8 on WorldCast.
Nw1PoClmkZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value multi-step world-state tasks that expose failures beyond static visual quality and cover varied reasoning requirements.
Nw1PoClmkZ.main_concern: Reviewers find the L3/L4 hierarchy insufficiently operationalized to establish a distinct higher-level capability.

7CJ9zfBspD.one_liner: A simulator-trained inverse map restricts Bayesian optimization to a learned search space with a geometry-aware Gaussian process kernel.
7CJ9zfBspD.problem: Black-box optimization can be sample-inefficient when it ignores simulator knowledge and low intrinsic dimensionality.
7CJ9zfBspD.method: The method trains an amortized inverse map of a differentiable mechanistic simulator and searches its learned representation with Bayesian optimization. A Gaussian process kernel preserves awareness of the original parameter-space geometry.
7CJ9zfBspD.key_idea: Amortize simulator inversion into a low-dimensional search representation and evaluate candidates with a kernel reflecting original-space geometry.
7CJ9zfBspD.evidence: Approximation-bias, information-gain, and conditional regret analyses accompany benchmark simulations and synthetic Parkinson's dosing experiments, including simulator misspecification.
7CJ9zfBspD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find simulator-informed low-dimensional Bayesian optimization well motivated and the dosing case study useful.
7CJ9zfBspD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the geometric and uniformly bounded amortization-error assumptions apply to the learned search space in practice.

WGavcJGfuS.one_liner: Shared-prefix continuations receive modality-specific reinforcement credit using sampler-state replay and constrained attention to committed history.
WGavcJGfuS.problem: Clip-level rewards cannot identify which autoregressive audio-video chunks deserve modality-specific credit under a shared generated history.
WGavcJGfuS.method: Fork-NFT branches joint continuations from a common prefix and assigns video credit over full continuations and audio credit over short post-fork windows. Training reuses paired sampler states, rebuilds current-policy causal KV context, and constrains cross-modal attention to committed history.
WGavcJGfuS.key_idea: Compare shared-prefix continuations with distinct video and audio credit windows while replaying sampler states and regularizing attention to historical context.
WGavcJGfuS.evidence: A 22B eight-step autoregressive model is evaluated on short- and long-form audio-video generation against matched-backbone and sampling baselines.
WGavcJGfuS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition into shared history, sampler-aware training, and modality-specific credit well motivated for autoregressive joint generation.
WGavcJGfuS.main_concern: Reviewers find comparisons with close prior methods insufficient to isolate the value of the proposed training components.

8vjsLM4yKd.one_liner: Closed-form quadratic-neuron analysis links feature learning to reduced trigger-strength requirements for backdoors in poisoned Gaussian mixtures.
8vjsLM4yKd.problem: Principled estimates of poison fraction and trigger strength are needed to explain how learning regimes affect backdoor vulnerability.
8vjsLM4yKd.method: The paper analyzes a quadratic neuron trained on a poisoned Gaussian mixture and contrasts lazy and feature-learning regimes. It derives trigger-strength scaling and a quadratic detector's loss margin while tracking clean accuracy.
8vjsLM4yKd.key_idea: Compare linear and quadratic trigger responses in a poisoned Gaussian model to derive how feature learning changes the attack-budget scaling.
8vjsLM4yKd.evidence: Closed-form theory is supported by numerical experiments and supplementary optimization studies in the specified Gaussian quadratic-neuron setting.
8vjsLM4yKd.claimed_gains: With clean accuracy preserved to first order O(π), feature learning changes successful-attack scaling from α ∝ π^{-1/2} to α ∝ π^{-1/4}, with loss margin O(α^4).
8vjsLM4yKd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value an interpretable analytical relationship between poison fraction, trigger strength, and learning regime.
8vjsLM4yKd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the restricted quadratic model and assumed trigger-aligned feature direction justify conclusions about general training dynamics and real networks.

AiXDabF4Km.one_liner: Contrasting successful and failed trajectories yields predicate-checked rules for software agents to reuse across repositories.
AiXDabF4Km.problem: Behaviors observed in successful software-agent trajectories may be incidental and fail to transfer across repositories.
AiXDabF4Km.method: XRepoSkill extracts action-and-condition rules from divergences between successful and failed trajectories and checks them with executable predicates. It retains behaviors associated with success across repositories, consolidates variants, and selects relevant rules for new issues.
AiXDabF4Km.key_idea: Contrast trajectory divergences, test candidate behaviors with executable predicates, and consolidate recurring cross-repository rules.
AiXDabF4Km.evidence: Repository-disjoint evaluations include unseen languages and model vendors, with a repeated DeepSWE experiment supporting improvements from the final rule prompt.
AiXDabF4Km.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the cross-repository evaluation and evidence that the learned rule prompts improve issue resolution.
AiXDabF4Km.main_concern: The rule-verification evidence lacks independent validation of predicate accuracy and protection against confounding in observed success associations.

LjdcKlasnX.one_liner: Spherical rotary embeddings and geometric guidance adapt pretrained diffusion transformers to panoramic image and video generation.
LjdcKlasnX.problem: Pretrained generators fail to satisfy equirectangular topology, while panorama-specific training and iterative optimization incur substantial costs.
LjdcKlasnX.method: SpheRoPE maps low-frequency rotary channels to 3D Cartesian coordinates and quantizes high-frequency channels into periodic harmonics. Semantic Distortion classifier-free guidance steers geometry during inference without training or optimization.
LjdcKlasnX.key_idea: Encode spherical geometry in low-frequency RoPE channels and enforce periodicity in high-frequency channels while guiding denoising toward geometric consistency.
LjdcKlasnX.evidence: Experiments cover panoramic images and videos with backbones including Flux.1, Flux.2, and LTX 2.3, alongside encoding and guidance ablations.
LjdcKlasnX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical inference-time adaptation of existing generators without task-specific training.
LjdcKlasnX.main_concern: Comparisons use different foundation models and fail to isolate the proposed changes from backbone quality.

Ntp6jKwdty.one_liner: A computable blind subspace characterizes what retraining cannot identify in performative reinforcement learning and guides exploration remedies.
Ntp6jKwdty.problem: Repeated retraining may stop visiting informative state-action pairs and converge to a suboptimal policy its own data cannot refute.
Ntp6jKwdty.method: The analysis characterizes identifiable response directions for performative MDPs with exponential-tilt dynamics and computes the remaining blind subspace. It studies optimism, posterior sampling, and minimal probing with regret guarantees.
Ntp6jKwdty.key_idea: Separate unobserved response directions that can change the optimal policy from those that cannot, then explore revealing state-action pairs.
Ntp6jKwdty.evidence: Fisher-information and regret analyses accompany grid-world and small tabular MDP experiments, including benign coverage-loss cases.
Ntp6jKwdty.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between lost coverage and decision-relevant information loss, together with its exploration analysis.
Ntp6jKwdty.main_concern: Restrictive response models with known response shapes and policy triggers limit practical applicability.

da3o1rBgel.one_liner: Pessimistic actor-critic learning jointly fits latent rewards and critics from trajectory outcomes, with sharp sample-complexity guarantees.
da3o1rBgel.problem: Offline RL theory gives limited guidance on when trajectory-level outcomes or preferences suffice for efficient policy optimization.
da3o1rBgel.method: OPAC learns latent per-step rewards and a critic under a pessimistic policy-optimization objective using scalar trajectory labels. The theory extends to pairwise preferences and distinguishes learnable nonlinear aggregations from exponentially hard objectives.
da3o1rBgel.key_idea: Jointly constrain latent rewards and critics with trajectory feedback and optimize pessimistically without requiring unique recovery of per-step rewards.
da3o1rBgel.evidence: Upper and lower bounds match cumulative-return dependence on horizon, coverage, and accuracy, while all-success lower bounds show exponential difficulty for some nonlinear objectives.
da3o1rBgel.claimed_gains: OPAC finds an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy from $\widetilde O(H^4C_{sa}/\varepsilon^2)$ trajectories under single-policy coverage and the stated function-class assumptions.
da3o1rBgel.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theory connecting trajectory-level feedback, policy optimization, and the choice of return objective.
da3o1rBgel.main_concern: Strong and potentially conflicting function-class closure and Bellman-completeness assumptions restrict the generalized guarantees.

P20PXj2iW0.one_liner: Perturbation-based layer profiling and routing-weight prioritization allocate fixed expert budgets for sparse multimodal MoE inference.
P20PXj2iW0.problem: Activating multiple experts across hundreds of visual tokens creates substantial inference overhead in MoE-based multimodal large language models, while uniform capacity reduction ignores layer-wise sensitivity and token-level routing heterogeneity.
P20PXj2iW0.method: M3MoE profiles each MoE layer's sensitivity via output-distribution perturbation to allocate a fixed visual-token expert budget across layers without retraining. Within each layer, it redistributes capacity across visual tokens by prioritizing token-expert pairs with larger routing weights to preserve routing mass.
P20PXj2iW0.key_idea: Profile MoE layer sensitivity via output-distribution perturbation to allocate layer budgets, then prioritize visual token-expert pairs with larger routing weights.
P20PXj2iW0.evidence: Experiments evaluate two MoE-based multimodal LLMs across eight vision-language benchmarks and multiple sparsity budgets with component-wise and calibration ablations.
P20PXj2iW0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-budget layer- and token-level allocation strategy is clearly motivated, requires no retraining, and preserves accuracy at high sparsity with thorough component ablations.
P20PXj2iW0.main_concern: Reviewers find the technical novelty incremental relative to prior layer-adaptive routing and visual-token pruning or skipping methods, while questioning baseline modifications and runtime speedups confounded by custom Triton kernels.

Lb2lOq0RqX.one_liner: Fisher-weighted sparse dictionary factorization and curvature-based allocation compress language-model weights.
Lb2lOq0RqX.problem: Loss-aware compression has largely focused on low-rank factorizations despite sparse dictionaries offering more flexible weight representations.
Lb2lOq0RqX.method: MORS incorporates Kronecker-factored empirical Fisher information into sparse factorization and compression allocation. Activation-metric orthogonality and a diagonal output-curvature surrogate enable decoupled support selection and efficient updates in the original weight domain.
Lb2lOq0RqX.key_idea: Constrain dictionary orthogonality in the activation-curvature metric and use Fisher-weighted objectives to select sparse coefficients and allocate compression.
Lb2lOq0RqX.evidence: Experiments span model families and compression ratios, with reviewers reporting accuracy and perplexity comparisons across 12 model-budget combinations.
Lb2lOq0RqX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent compression improvements and an efficient optimization procedure for the diagonal surrogate.
Lb2lOq0RqX.main_concern: The empirical-Fisher and full-curvature allocation surrogates lack sufficient validation against losses achievable by the deployed diagonal-curvature sparse factorization.

ISpRwLo4Bw.one_liner: A shared SFT–RL inner trajectory and Reptile-style outer update coordinate cross-objective training.
ISpRwLo4Bw.problem: Staged reinforcement learning can overwrite supervised fine-tuning gains, while conflicting gradients complicate joint optimization.
ISpRwLo4Bw.method: The framework places supervised and reinforcement-learning updates on a shared inner optimization trajectory. A Reptile-style outer step implicitly promotes gradient compatibility without explicit second-order gradient computation.
ISpRwLo4Bw.key_idea: Apply a Reptile-style outer update to a trajectory containing both SFT and RL steps so cross-objective interactions enter the update.
ISpRwLo4Bw.evidence: Experiments compare multiple backbones and benchmarks against SFT, RL, staged, and hybrid baselines, including reproduced hybrids with SFT warm-up.
ISpRwLo4Bw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple implementation and concrete shared-trajectory formulation, supported by evaluations across models and benchmarks.
ISpRwLo4Bw.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate gradient alignment as the cause of gains, with training-budget matching and the alignment derivation also needing clarification.

UzoqxX6OCZ.one_liner: A single source attention read supplies cached background context for foreground-only iterative image editing.
UzoqxX6OCZ.problem: Multi-step source inversion and full-image denoising impose unnecessary cost when only a known local region needs editing.
UzoqxX6OCZ.method: FreEdit extracts attention projections from a source image noised at one intermediate timestep. Target denoising updates only masked tokens using stored background keys and values, then combines the foreground with clean source latents; optional QK-CFG supports color and style edits.
UzoqxX6OCZ.key_idea: Cache source attention projections from one network evaluation and reuse background keys and values while iteratively denoising only masked foreground tokens.
UzoqxX6OCZ.evidence: FLUX.1-dev comparisons include a controlled source-inversion replacement, extraction-time studies, and dedicated appearance evaluations, with further results on Klein and Qwen.
UzoqxX6OCZ.claimed_gains: On FLUX.1-dev, FreEdit achieves a 3.58× speedup on the same hardware while improving all six reported mean metrics.
UzoqxX6OCZ.reviewer_consensus: Positive reviews identify the single source read as the concrete contribution and credit the controlled evidence for its efficiency.
UzoqxX6OCZ.main_concern: The advance over KV-Edit remains insufficiently established, particularly without a matched comparison to its inversion-free variant.

omJu0a2qIP.one_liner: Additive log-policy increments reconstruct coalition response scores from singleton alignments for Shapley data valuation.
omJu0a2qIP.problem: Shapley valuation of preference-data sources ordinarily requires an exponential number of separately aligned coalition models.
omJu0a2qIP.method: The method reparameterizes direct alignment algorithms in log-policy-ratio coordinates and analyzes sequential source alignment under exact, identifiable optima. It reconstructs coalition scores from the base policy and one policy per source, up to prompt-dependent normalization.
omJu0a2qIP.key_idea: Sum reference-independent source log-probability increments to reconstruct fixed-response coalition scores without training coalition-specific policies.
omJu0a2qIP.evidence: Theoretical reconstruction results and finite-training experiments across several base models examine response-score agreement and source valuation.
omJu0a2qIP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit reconstruction rule and its reduction of required alignment runs under the stated assumptions.
omJu0a2qIP.main_concern: The theory requires each source to identify relative response scores at every prompt, which heterogeneous sources with missing support or disconnected comparisons may violate.

QCAXD5qKRI.one_liner: Cumulative SVD of upstream attention and MLP weights constructs training-free dictionaries that exactly reconstruct residual activations.
QCAXD5qKRI.problem: Sparse autoencoder dictionaries require activation corpora and training, introduce reconstruction errors, and vary across seeds.
QCAXD5qKRI.method: The method accumulates upstream module outputs and decomposes attention OV circuits and MLP down projections into compact orthogonal read and write channels. These channels form an overcomplete dictionary with exact residual reconstruction.
QCAXD5qKRI.key_idea: Accumulate SVD-derived read and write channels from all upstream attention and MLP modules into a model-intrinsic residual-stream dictionary.
QCAXD5qKRI.evidence: Experiments on Gemma 3 (1B-27B) and Qwen3-8B assess interpretability, semantic coverage, sparse concept prediction, attribute disentanglement, and factual steering.
QCAXD5qKRI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the cheap, deterministic dictionary construction without auxiliary training or corpus dependence.
QCAXD5qKRI.main_concern: Comparisons with SAEs may confound dictionary size and cumulative feature access with SVD's contribution, while weaker raw-feature interpretability complicates the claimed advantage.

buYWiZwoAZ.one_liner: Execution-derived efficiency evidence activates or retires instruction atoms without separate validation rollouts.
buYWiZwoAZ.problem: Skill self-evolution relies on costly validation gates, but removing them can accumulate harmful revisions.
buYWiZwoAZ.method: FreeEvo decomposes skills into task-specific accuracy atoms and a fixed instruction discouraging redundant reasoning. An optimizer attributes errors and unnecessary reasoning to atoms, then accumulates evidence across distinct examples to activate or permanently retire them.
buYWiZwoAZ.key_idea: Use existing execution trajectories to attribute reasoning inefficiency and errors to individual instruction atoms and govern their activation without candidate-validation rollouts.
buYWiZwoAZ.evidence: Experiments span three models and four benchmarks in four domains, with attribution and retirement ablations plus cross-dataset transfer.
buYWiZwoAZ.claimed_gains: FreeEvo matches or outperforms the compared methods while reducing evolution tokens by up to 93.6\%.
buYWiZwoAZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial evolution-cost savings and useful empirical results from reusing execution feedback.
buYWiZwoAZ.main_concern: The attribution mechanism is not convincingly isolated: reasoning length may correlate with harm without causing it, and close itemized-curation methods lack direct comparisons.

vvFCD6b0E5.one_liner: A reinforcement-trained agent selects and cross-checks heterogeneous image detectors using capability profiles.
vvFCD6b0E5.problem: AI-generated image detectors face evolving generators, heterogeneous outputs, costly annotations, and limited extensibility.
vvFCD6b0E5.method: EvoGuard profiles detector capabilities, selects complementary tools per image, and reasons over conflicting or uncertain outputs across multiple rounds. GRPO trains the orchestration policy using binary labels.
vvFCD6b0E5.key_idea: Treat heterogeneous detectors as tools and learn capability-aware selection plus iterative evidence synthesis from low-cost binary supervision.
vvFCD6b0E5.evidence: Experiments compare single detectors, static ensembles, tool-selection variants, and held-out detector additions across benchmarks including LOKI and CommunityForensic-Eval.
vvFCD6b0E5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find dynamic integration of heterogeneous detectors a useful and well-motivated formulation.
vvFCD6b0E5.main_concern: Results do not clearly separate learned orchestration gains from reliance on the strongest detector or ordinary detector complementarity.

cnt2K3pBY7.one_liner: Random-direction-controlled emotion steering separates textual emotion expression from task behavior and long-horizon outcomes.
cnt2K3pBY7.problem: Prior emotion-steering evidence often lacks cross-construct behavioral tests, random controls, and long-horizon evaluation.
cnt2K3pBY7.method: The study compares emotion directions with random directions across static tasks and agent benchmarks. It examines additive versus gain steering, intervention-strength controls, model sensitivity, and intermediate versus final outcomes.
cnt2K3pBY7.key_idea: Compare emotion-vector interventions against random directions on distinct behavioral targets, separating emotional expression from changes in answers or actions.
cnt2K3pBY7.evidence: Evaluation covers four open-weight models, twelve emotions, twelve public cross-construct task categories, and long-horizon agents with statistical controls.
cnt2K3pBY7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad controlled evaluation and statistical analysis of emotion steering's behavioral limits.
cnt2K3pBY7.main_concern: Isotropic random directions may not provide appropriate controls for learned activation directions, leaving emotion-specific effects insufficiently established.

qB5lpaF4rk.one_liner: Low-dimensional cross-group curvature corrections augment tensor-wise preconditioning for joint optimization.
qB5lpaF4rk.problem: Independent parameter-group preconditioning misses coupled directions that can slow convergence or create joint instability.
qB5lpaF4rk.method: CoPEN augments tensor-wise preconditioners with a low-dimensional cross-group curvature model without forming the full Hessian. The analysis studies local convergence and saddle escape, while the practical method uses a positive-semidefinite output-sensitivity surrogate.
qB5lpaF4rk.key_idea: Correct independently preconditioned parameter groups using a projected model of their cross-group interactions.
qB5lpaF4rk.evidence: Local theoretical analyses and controlled experiments accompany full fine-tuning studies of two pretrained vision models on Taskonomy.
qB5lpaF4rk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize cross-group curvature as a meaningful optimization issue and regard low-dimensional corrections as practical.
qB5lpaF4rk.main_concern: True-Hessian saddle theory does not directly characterize the practical positive-semidefinite surrogate, and model-scale controls do not isolate cross-group effects.

5LVAprWOxU.one_liner: Coding agents generate parametric 3D puzzles to test learning unfamiliar physical mechanisms through interaction.
5LVAprWOxU.problem: Embodied agents need evaluation of how efficiently they infer and exploit unfamiliar environments from limited action–perception experience.
5LVAprWOxU.method: Flint uses coding agents to build 3D puzzle rooms and variants that alter their solutions. Other agents adversarially inspect rooms for unintended solutions, alongside automated checks, oracle solutions, and human review.
5LVAprWOxU.key_idea: Generate controlled variants of unfamiliar interactive mechanisms and evaluate whether agents discover and exploit the changes through action–perception feedback.
5LVAprWOxU.evidence: The benchmark contains 283 validated tasks and evaluates frontier multimodal agents with interaction analyses and generous action budgets.
5LVAprWOxU.claimed_gains: Latest frontier agents improve solve rates by 33–52 percentage points over their previous generations under a generous budget.
5LVAprWOxU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the generated puzzle framework, controlled task variants, and evaluation of interactive physical reasoning.
5LVAprWOxU.main_concern: Diagnostic interventions do not adequately separate mechanism discovery from extra attempts, solution-relevant hints, or manipulation difficulty.

yhHaaucuGn.one_liner: Contextual role and induced-action labels distinguish malicious document overreach from superficial injection cues.
yhHaaucuGn.problem: Document safety detectors can miss ordinary-looking attacks and falsely flag benign prompt-like text.
yhHaaucuGn.method: MSO-Bench varies surface cues independently of role mismatch and restricted operations across document types. MSO-Guard trains a 4B model to reason about contextual segment function and induced actions before making document-level safety decisions.
yhHaaucuGn.key_idea: Determine document risk from an out-of-role function combined with a restricted operation while independently varying surface injection cues.
yhHaaucuGn.evidence: The benchmark spans 20 real-world document types with diagnostic type comparisons, model and prompt evaluations, and detector ablations.
yhHaaucuGn.claimed_gains: MSO-Guard achieves a 94.2\% F1 score, outperforming existing dedicated detectors and matching GPT-5 at a fraction of deployment cost.
yhHaaucuGn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the diagnostic separation of surface cues, role mismatch, and restricted operations, supported by extensive experiments.
yhHaaucuGn.main_concern: GPT-5's overlapping roles in data generation, review, training traces, and baseline evaluation risk measuring agreement with its rubric rather than external validity.

rPEZMHotob.one_liner: Global temporal memory and query-retrieved local events feed support-aware routing for irregular time-series forecasts.
rPEZMHotob.problem: Compressed irregular histories can lose predictive local events, while sparse target observations require adaptable information-source selection.
rPEZMHotob.method: SEQNet combines variable-level temporal summaries with retained local events retrieved for the current forecasting query. Its support-aware routing adjusts the use of target history and cross-variable information according to observation availability.
rPEZMHotob.key_idea: Retrieve query-relevant observations alongside compressed temporal summaries and route information according to the target variable's observation support.
rPEZMHotob.evidence: Experiments report MSE over five seeds on four datasets, including PhysioNet and Activity, with event-selection, source-routing, and observation-deletion studies.
rPEZMHotob.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dual-memory and support-aware design well motivated and recognize strong reported forecasting results.
rPEZMHotob.main_concern: Missing recent baselines, uncertain protocol matching, and robustness tests without competitors prevent firm conclusions about comparative benefits under sparse observations.

zt2ptiGCWN.one_liner: A shared future-feature predictor guides independently adapted robot experts for coordinated manipulation.
zt2ptiGCWN.problem: Decentralized robot policies lack global coordination context, while centralized joint-action policies tightly couple individual controllers.
zt2ptiGCWN.method: A shared Brain uses all robot observations and a language instruction to predict collaborative futures through alignment with multi-view 3D features. The frozen Brain provides guidance to independently adapted Action Experts, preserving replaceable robot controllers.
zt2ptiGCWN.key_idea: Learn a shared prediction of future multi-view 3D features and convert it into guidance for separately adapted per-robot policies.
zt2ptiGCWN.evidence: RoboFactory evaluation covers six tasks and demonstrates replacing two experts with GR00T without retraining the Brain or remaining controllers.
zt2ptiGCWN.claimed_gains: The framework achieves an 85.5% average success rate across six RoboFactory tasks.
zt2ptiGCWN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared-prediction and individual-controller separation clear and useful for modular multi-robot coordination.
zt2ptiGCWN.main_concern: Baselines taken from prior papers lack matched pretraining and training protocols, so large gains cannot be attributed confidently to predictive coordination.

KFvo7t3H0P.one_liner: Per-query mixed-integer optimization jointly allocates executor models and paid verification under budget and latency constraints.
KFvo7t3H0P.problem: Task-graph execution needs to balance current model costs against verification that reveals unknown service quality for future allocations.
KFvo7t3H0P.method: JOVE solves per-query mixed-integer linear programs for executor assignment and asynchronous verification. Verification feedback updates task-dependent quality estimates, while an information-gain bonus accounts for learning under long-term budget and per-query latency constraints.
KFvo7t3H0P.key_idea: Jointly select task executors and outputs to verify, using verification-driven quality estimates and an information-gain bonus in constrained allocation.
KFvo7t3H0P.evidence: Sublinear quality-learning regret analysis accompanies four reasoning benchmarks, with random-verification and decomposition ablations.
KFvo7t3H0P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value jointly modeling execution and verification costs with task dependencies, resource constraints, and theoretical guarantees.
KFvo7t3H0P.main_concern: The evaluation does not isolate joint optimization from heterogeneous model-pool advantages, and repeated graphs from the same test samples may contaminate later quality estimates.

MVZPUy7ZW8.one_liner: Validity checks and teacher judgments gate multi-turn distillation, with confidence weighting normalized within each batch.
MVZPUy7ZW8.problem: Dense token-level distillation can penalize valid alternative actions and propagate unreliable supervision on off-distribution agent histories.
MVZPUy7ZW8.method: SAGE-OPD uses pre-execution checks and teacher judgment to select student turns for supervision. Teacher confidence weights selected turns, and batch normalization maintains unit average effective token weight.
MVZPUy7ZW8.key_idea: Apply teacher supervision selectively by response validity and judgment, then allocate normalized supervision weights according to teacher confidence.
MVZPUy7ZW8.evidence: Experiments use Qwen3 students and 8B or 32B teachers on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and SearchQA, with gating, confidence, and normalization controls.
MVZPUy7ZW8.claimed_gains: With a Qwen3-1.7B student and Qwen3-8B teacher, SAGE-OPD raises ALFWorld unseen success from 61.94% to 70.15%.
MVZPUy7ZW8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing acceptable actions from teacher-token matches and appreciate the implementable rule and informative ablations.
MVZPUy7ZW8.main_concern: The added teacher judge lacks a consistently demonstrated advantage over cheaper confidence-only weighting, especially given limited replicated headline experiments.

cHK7M6N4cl.one_liner: Dynamic auxiliary-modality fusion helps classify and localize open-vocabulary video relationship triplets.
cHK7M6N4cl.problem: Visual-only relationship detection cannot reliably disambiguate predicates that differ through audio, text, or 3D context.
cHK7M6N4cl.method: VaM-VidVRD pairs video with heterogeneous, source-dependent auxiliary modalities and relationship annotations. MMSP dynamically fuses available auxiliary inputs into prompts conditioned on subject/object visual streams for relationship prediction.
cHK7M6N4cl.key_idea: Condition relationship prediction on dynamically fused available audio, textual, and 3D evidence to distinguish visually similar predicates.
cHK7M6N4cl.evidence: Reviewers describe 3,600 videos with refined trajectories and category splits, plus vision-only, text-masking, and multimodal baseline comparisons.
cHK7M6N4cl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the multimodal benchmark and controlled evidence that auxiliary cues improve difficult relationship predictions.
cHK7M6N4cl.main_concern: MMSP's contribution beyond existing multimodal fusion and dynamic-prompt methods remains unclear without closely matched comparisons.

A2upKHKbPh.one_liner: Continuity across sampling resolutions characterizes causal maps uniformly approximable by one transformer across arbitrary context lengths.
A2upKHKbPh.problem: Most transformer expressivity results choose separate networks for fixed sequence lengths rather than shared parameters across lengths.
A2upKHKbPh.method: The analysis models sequences as increasingly fine samples of Hölder-regular signals on a fixed normalized horizon. It characterizes cross-resolution continuity, extends approximation to a continuous mean-field limit, and derives quantitative approximation and regression bounds.
A2upKHKbPh.key_idea: Impose a common continuity modulus across token sampling resolutions so a single causal transformer approximates the associated family uniformly.
A2upKHKbPh.evidence: Universality and converse results, approximation and generalization bounds, and finite-bit lower bounds accompany physical-time-series diagnostics.
A2upKHKbPh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified treatment of discrete sequences, shared-parameter approximation across resolutions, and the continuous-time limit.
A2upKHKbPh.main_concern: Smooth resampling of a fixed horizon models time-series refinement rather than text contexts that add information or require isolated-token retrieval.

XOHh3z8FP6.one_liner: Closed-form OOD mixture analysis measures how far source proportions can shift before a detector loses its lead.
XOHh3z8FP6.problem: OOD detector gains can reverse when deployment changes the mixture of unfamiliar input sources.
XOHh3z8FP6.method: The study compares each trained detector against all existing detector–scorer choices, including cross-entropy baselines. Using per-source AUROCs, it computes mixture-shift tolerances and checks predicted source-specific losses across repeated training and evaluation settings.
XOHh3z8FP6.key_idea: Express AUROC over mixtures through per-source scores and compute the mixture perturbation at which a competing detector becomes better.
XOHh3z8FP6.evidence: Four benchmark comparisons and replications span seeds, scoring functions, architectures, and datasets, with new-image tests drawn from already measured sources.
XOHh3z8FP6.claimed_gains: A detector passing every measured-source comparison retains a 9.2-point AUROC lead on new images from two near-OOD sources and halves false acceptances.
XOHh3z8FP6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find mixture-sensitive detector selection meaningful and regard the mathematical comparison as reasonable.
XOHh3z8FP6.main_concern: Robustness depends on already measured sources and chosen mixture shifts, so the evaluation does not establish reliability on unseen OOD sources.

cyQTpX4UIm.one_liner: Self-reflection uncertainty and adapter sensitivity jointly gate the strength of internalized skills for each query.
cyQTpX4UIm.problem: A fixed skill-adapter strength can help some queries while disrupting answers the base model would otherwise get right.
cyQTpX4UIm.method: Query-Adaptive Skill Gating combines predictive uncertainty from self-reflection with adapter sensitivity relative to base computation. These signals regulate each query's skill contribution.
cyQTpX4UIm.key_idea: Set per-query adapter strength by combining self-reflection uncertainty with sensitivity to the skill adapter.
cyQTpX4UIm.evidence: Evaluations span five benchmarks, multiple model scales, component ablations, and comparisons with TextSkill, LatentSkill, and adaptive gating methods.
cyQTpX4UIm.claimed_gains: QASG outperforms the best fixed-strength baseline by 8.1--8.4 points.
cyQTpX4UIm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find per-query skill-strength control well motivated and the reported results supported by ablations.
cyQTpX4UIm.main_concern: The hand-designed combination of uncertainty and sensitivity needs stronger justification and comparisons with alternative gating functions.

n3AelQxx19.one_liner: Pre-video instructions, prescribed responses, and valid response windows make proactive streaming-video behavior programmatically verifiable.
n3AelQxx19.problem: Existing proactive-interaction benchmarks often omit audio or depend on costly open-ended evaluation.
n3AelQxx19.method: PIFBench formalizes Proactive Instruction Following: models receive an instruction before a video, process content incrementally, and remain silent until its condition holds. The benchmark covers visual and audio information with rule-based response verification.
n3AelQxx19.key_idea: Define proactive responses through pre-given conditions, required content, and valid time windows that support rule-based verification.
n3AelQxx19.evidence: PIFBench contains 1,993 items and evaluates mainstream models on incremental visual and audio understanding with proactive responses.
n3AelQxx19.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the streaming-interaction task and scalable, verifiable benchmark design.
n3AelQxx19.main_concern: The paper provides insufficient analysis of streaming behavior, including the cost and evaluation of timely responses.

Q9hnfOoIw4.one_liner: Feature-space reconstruction selects sparse weights to test whether preserving dense-model representations prevents accuracy collapse after pruning.
Q9hnfOoIw4.problem: The mechanism allowing magnitude pruning to preserve accuracy, and causing eventual failure at high sparsity, remains unclear.
Q9hnfOoIw4.method: The paper studies classifiers after a controlled linear embedding and constructs an optimization oracle that reconstructs the dense model's effective feature-space matrix with sparse weights. A sparse autoencoder substitutes for the true embedding when it is unavailable.
Q9hnfOoIw4.key_idea: Choose sparse weights by reconstructing the dense model's effective feature-space matrix rather than ranking individual weight magnitudes.
Q9hnfOoIw4.evidence: Experiments compare pruning under matched retraining budgets on synthetic logic, Digits, UCI datasets, and deeper controlled networks, with sparse-autoencoder variants.
Q9hnfOoIw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled intervention on feature preservation and the sparse-autoencoder extension of the oracle.
Q9hnfOoIw4.main_concern: Small, controlled settings do not establish that the explanation or mixed-integer optimization extends to realistic deep nonlinear models.

RXVGiYTpLD.one_liner: Short auxiliary-model branches redirect target-model rollouts, with policy updates confined to inserted segments using final verifiable rewards.
RXVGiYTpLD.problem: Self-generated reasoning rollouts can become semantically redundant and provide insufficient reward contrast for reinforcement learning.
RXVGiYTpLD.method: W2SPO inserts short segments from a weaker auxiliary model into intermediate target-model trajectories, then lets the target complete them. It restricts policy updates to the inserted segments using final rewards and advantage reweighting.
RXVGiYTpLD.key_idea: Inject short off-policy auxiliary segments into target rollouts and update only those segments according to final verifiable rewards.
RXVGiYTpLD.evidence: Experiments cover mathematical reasoning with 4B-scale models, matched-sampling comparisons against GRPO, a non-Qwen 7B target, and multi-turn tool use.
RXVGiYTpLD.claimed_gains: Compared with vanilla GRPO under the same sampling budget, W2SPO improves Pass@1 from 62.3% to 64.2% with a 3.55× training speedup.
RXVGiYTpLD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find local auxiliary branching a well-motivated response to redundant self-generated reasoning trajectories.
RXVGiYTpLD.main_concern: The experiments insufficiently establish how auxiliary-model quality, diversity, and cost determine the benefits of weak-to-strong exploration.

hnHh4VQL6x.one_liner: Benchmarks style-conditioned and cross-lingual font generation across 920 hierarchical fonts using readability, structure, style, and quality metrics.
hnHh4VQL6x.problem: Existing font generation evaluations rely on narrow font styles, single writing scripts, or pixel-reconstruction metrics that fail to separate glyph readability from typographic style fidelity.
hnHh4VQL6x.method: FontBench curates 920 fonts organized into three main groups and eight subcategories spanning regular to complex artistic scripts for style-conditioned and cross-lingual (English/Chinese) font generation. It evaluates five specialized font generators and seven general image-to-image models across four axes: character readability, structural fidelity, style consistency, and visual quality.
hnHh4VQL6x.key_idea: Organizes 920 fonts into an eight-subcategory complexity taxonomy and evaluates style-conditioned and cross-lingual glyph generation across readability, structure, style, and visual quality.
hnHh4VQL6x.evidence: Evaluated across five specialized font generation models and seven general-purpose image-to-image models on 920 fonts.
hnHh4VQL6x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that expanding font evaluation to complex artistic styles, cross-lingual settings, and both specialized and general-purpose generative models across multiple evaluation dimensions is useful.
hnHh4VQL6x.main_concern: Reviewers question whether general-purpose OpenCLIP features can measure fine-grained typographic style consistency and note that the benchmark provides limited diagnostic insight or near-duplicate screening across font splits.

zjkV9hsOhq.one_liner: Builds a large-scale German pretraining corpus by translating a curated English dataset and filtering with a COMETKiwi-supervised quality proxy.
zjkV9hsOhq.problem: German-language LLM pretraining corpora are smaller, less curated, and less systematically validated through controlled training ablations than English datasets.
zjkV9hsOhq.method: KletterMix translates an English pretraining corpus into German while preserving document boundaries, metadata, and topical structure, and filters the translated text using a scalable proxy model trained on COMETKiwi translation-quality scores. The authors document corpus-level linguistic statistics and validate the dataset via controlled pretraining and annealing runs against native German web corpora.
zjkV9hsOhq.key_idea: Translates a curated English pretraining corpus into German at document level and filters it with a lightweight proxy model distilled from reference-free COMETKiwi quality scores.
zjkV9hsOhq.evidence: Evaluated through corpus-level linguistic analyses and controlled pretraining and annealing ablations at 0.6B and 7B model scales against FineWeb2 and GermanWeb.
zjkV9hsOhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the large-scale engineering effort, thorough corpus documentation, COMETKiwi proxy filtering analysis, and controlled training comparisons across model scales.
zjkV9hsOhq.main_concern: Reviewers point out that downstream gains concentrate on benchmarks that are themselves machine-translated from English (ARC-C and HellaSwag), potentially reflecting translation-artifact alignment rather than native German language and cultural knowledge.

rDDM5SVGUf.one_liner: Optimizes key-value states at inference time using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation to shift multimodal LLM attribution toward perceptual tokens.
rDDM5SVGUf.problem: Multimodal LLMs often hallucinate responses that conflict with visual or audio inputs because decoding relies excessively on text priors over perceptual tokens.
rDDM5SVGUf.method: Learning Inference-time Modality Enhancement (LIME) uses Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) during decoding to measure how much each output prediction relies on visual or audio input tokens versus text tokens. Without modifying model weights or using training data, it performs gradient updates on key-value representations at inference time to increase the relevance score assigned to perceptual tokens.
rDDM5SVGUf.key_idea: Computes Layer-wise Relevance Propagation scores during decoding and iteratively updates KV-cache representations at inference time to maximize relevance attributed to visual or audio tokens.
rDDM5SVGUf.evidence: Evaluated on vision-language and audio-language hallucination benchmarks using models including LLaVA and Qwen2-Audio.
rDDM5SVGUf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation as a training-free inference-time optimization signal across both vision and audio modalities well-motivated.
rDDM5SVGUf.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that running multiple LRP-guided optimization steps during decoding causes a severe ~9x inference throughput slowdown that is relegated to the appendix, alongside weak empirical validation linking LRP scores to hallucination in the main text.

GWjCvZnnIf.one_liner: Preserves pretrained inter-sentence geometry and jointly aligns video-text tokens for bidirectional sign language retrieval.
GWjCvZnnIf.problem: Contrastive sign language retrieval distorts pretrained semantic distances among texts during adaptation and computes local token weights independently, allowing a single video token to spuriously match multiple text tokens.
GWjCvZnnIf.method: SignAlign introduces Text Semantic Structure Alignment (TSSA), which regularizes the adapted text encoder against a frozen pretrained text reference by matching normalized pairwise sentence distances and triplet angles. It combines TSSA with a cross-modal token structure alignment module (CTSA) to jointly align signing video tokens and text tokens.
GWjCvZnnIf.key_idea: Constrains normalized pairwise distances and triplet angles of adapted text embeddings to match a frozen pretrained text encoder while jointly aligning local video and text tokens.
GWjCvZnnIf.evidence: Evaluated on three sign language retrieval benchmarks (Phoenix, How2Sign, and CSL-Daily) with component ablations.
GWjCvZnnIf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written, the geometric preservation and token-alignment modules are well-motivated, and retrieval results improve consistently across three sign language datasets.
