GWjCvZnnIf.main_concern: Reviewers note missing initialization details for the video backbone and pre-extracted features, unanalyzed numerical stability of the normalized angular and distance losses, and incremental scope on established datasets.

wqKUSD7HvK.one_liner: Trains a multi-view context-aware per-view reward model on 48K human preference pairs for view-level RL in 3D texturing.
wqKUSD7HvK.problem: Post-training 3D texture generators with single asset-level rewards obscures quality differences across viewpoints and assigns identical feedback to clean and artifact-heavy views.
wqKUSD7HvK.method: CrediTex constructs a 48K view-level human preference dataset and trains a reward model that takes a target view query alongside the reference image and full multi-view set as context to predict a per-view scalar reward. During reinforcement learning, it computes viewpoint-specific relative advantages across candidates to provide distinct gradient updates to individual views of each 3D asset.
wqKUSD7HvK.key_idea: Evaluates each rendered view conditioned on the full multi-view context to compute view-specific relative advantages for reinforcement learning of multi-view 3D texture diffusion.
wqKUSD7HvK.evidence: Evaluated on reward modeling accuracy and 3D texture generation across multiple diffusion models, automated metrics, and a user study.
wqKUSD7HvK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing coarse asset-level feedback with full-context per-view reward modeling and view-level credit assignment addresses a real limitation in multi-view 3D texturing.
wqKUSD7HvK.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing documentation on preference dataset collection and annotator agreement, lack of empirical comparisons against existing RL-based 3D consistency methods (such as Carve3D), and evaluation restricted to diffusion models.

9LAod6EeXg.one_liner: Allocates RLVR rollout budgets across prompts via a heap-based greedy algorithm maximizing a capability-dependent training-value surrogate.
9LAod6EeXg.problem: Standard GRPO uses a uniform rollout budget across prompts, while instance-level adaptive allocation methods ignore how a model's evolving global capability changes sample training value.
9LAod6EeXg.method: CoBA-RL defines a Capability-Oriented Value function that combines a batch-level model capability indicator with task pass rates and an exponential budget-saturation factor to estimate marginal training gain per additional rollout. At each RL step, a heap-based greedy algorithm distributes the total rollout budget across prompts to maximize this estimated value.
9LAod6EeXg.key_idea: Greedily allocates per-prompt rollout counts using a priority heap scored by a capability-shifted Beta density over prompt pass rates and an exponential rollout-saturation decay.
9LAod6EeXg.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM scales and reasoning benchmarks against uniform GRPO and adaptive budget baselines.
9LAod6EeXg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that dynamically redistributing a fixed per-step rollout count across prompts is practical, easy to integrate into RLVR pipelines, and yields consistent benchmark accuracy gains over uniform GRPO.
9LAod6EeXg.main_concern: Reviewers point out that matching the number of rollout trajectories per step increases total generated tokens and wall-clock GPU time by 38–51% because harder prompts produce longer responses, undermining the compute-efficiency claim alongside a heuristic value function.

ZAfd1HA0cH.one_liner: Grounds multi-turn agentic on-policy distillation in objective interaction states by stripping prior student thoughts from the teacher prefix.
ZAfd1HA0cH.problem: In multi-turn agentic on-policy distillation, conditioning the teacher on the student's accumulated prior reasoning traces distorts teacher supervision at later turns.
ZAfd1HA0cH.method: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation (State-OPD) separates objective interaction states (the task and executed action-observation history) from the student's internal reasoning traces, conditioning the teacher only on the objective interaction state while the student generates from the full history. It also reallocates the sampling budget to draw multiple complete reasoning-action responses at interaction states exhibiting high response entropy.
ZAfd1HA0cH.key_idea: Removes prior-turn student reasoning traces from the teacher's conditioning context while resampling full reasoning-action rollouts at high-entropy interaction states.
ZAfd1HA0cH.evidence: Evaluated on three multi-turn agentic benchmarks (including ALFWorld) with ablations separating teacher-context stripping from entropy-guided resampling.
ZAfd1HA0cH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating objective action-observation history from accumulated student reasoning in the teacher's prompt is a simple and effective insight supported by clear multi-turn empirical gains.
ZAfd1HA0cH.main_concern: Reviewers note that the paper omits the symmetric baseline that also strips prior-turn reasoning from the student's context, does not separate erroneous thoughts from helpful plans, and generates nearly twice as many thinking tokens per turn on ALFWorld.

GrK52SqlB4.one_liner: Proves Markov policies are suboptimal for finite-horizon max@k RL and derives an optimal sample-complexity algorithm via two-statistic state augmentation.
GrK52SqlB4.problem: Although large reasoning models are routinely evaluated and trained under retry-aware max@k metrics across k rollouts, the theoretical planning and sample-complexity foundations of max@k RL are underexplored.
GrK52SqlB4.method: The authors analyze finite-horizon reinforcement learning under the max@k objective, proving that memoryless Markovian policies can be strictly suboptimal and showing that augmenting the state with two scalar statistics—the best return achieved in previous rollouts and the current episode's cumulative reward—restores optimality. They characterize the history-dependence performance gap and provide a reinforcement learning algorithm that achieves the minimax-optimal sample complexity rate.
GrK52SqlB4.key_idea: Augments the MDP state space with the running maximum return across prior attempts and the current trajectory's cumulative reward to recover dynamic programming and optimal sample complexity for max@k RL.
GrK52SqlB4.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs of Markov suboptimality, state-augmentation sufficiency, planning complexity, and minimax sample-complexity bounds.
GrK52SqlB4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing retry-aware max@k RL and proving that two reward statistics suffice to summarize cross-episode and within-episode history is a clear and well-motivated theoretical contribution.
GrK52SqlB4.main_concern: Reviewers identify a mathematical flaw in a lower-bound proof step in the appendix, missing space-complexity analysis for the discretized augmented state space, and insufficient discussion of related risk-sensitive and lookahead RL literature.

AdRhMQz8EP.one_liner: Combines soft-boundary temporal anchoring and shared emotion concept modulation inside non-autoregressive TTS for word-level composable emotion control.
AdRhMQz8EP.problem: Non-autoregressive text-to-speech models lack unified control over word-level emotion placement, continuous intensity scaling, and multi-emotion blending.
AdRhMQz8EP.method: ControlAnything integrates two modules into pretrained non-autoregressive TTS architectures: Soft-boundary Anchor Intervention (SAI), which aligns target text spans to acoustic regions and progressively sharpens temporal boundaries across denoising steps, and Emotion Concept Modulation (ECM), which learns emotion-specific feature transformations that can be scaled for intensity and linearly combined for blended emotions.
AdRhMQz8EP.key_idea: Applies progressive soft-masked temporal anchoring and weighted emotion-specific affine feature modulations within intermediate diffusion transformer blocks of a non-autoregressive TTS model.
AdRhMQz8EP.evidence: Evaluated across pretrained non-autoregressive TTS backbones (including F5-TTS) on emotional speech datasets (including CREMA-D) for word-level localization, intensity control, and emotion composition.
AdRhMQz8EP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical demonstration of simultaneous word-level localization, intensity adjustment, and emotion blending in non-autoregressive TTS, supported by intervention-location ablations.
AdRhMQz8EP.main_concern: Reviewers view the temporal masking and weighted affine modulation mechanisms as incremental, note missing comparisons with matched emotion-conditioned fine-tuning baselines, and point out unaccounted inference latency from multi-pass synthesis and ASR alignment.

9Rxg1AHDrM.one_liner: Accelerates VecSet 3D diffusion via surface-anchor cross-attention token pruning and curvature-adaptive hierarchical volume decoding.
9Rxg1AHDrM.problem: VecSet-based 3D diffusion models suffer from high inference latency during iterative latent denoising and dense volumetric mesh decoding.
9Rxg1AHDrM.method: HGA3D accelerates 3D generation in two stages without retraining: during diffusion, geometry-aware token pruning uses decoder cross-attention from sparse dynamic surface anchors to retain only surface-critical latent tokens; during decoding, curvature-adaptive volume decoding concentrates high-resolution SDF queries near high-curvature surface regions while sparsifying smooth areas.
9Rxg1AHDrM.key_idea: Prunes diffusion latent tokens via cross-attention scores against dynamic zero-level surface anchors and allocates octree volume-decoding queries according to local surface curvature.
9Rxg1AHDrM.evidence: Evaluated on TripoSG and Hunyuan3D-2.0 across 3D generation benchmarks and thin-structure categories.
9Rxg1AHDrM.claimed_gains: Demonstrates total inference speedups of 1.50x on TripoSG and 1.48x on Hunyuan3D-2.0 while preserving 3D generation fidelity.
9Rxg1AHDrM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that accelerating both the diffusion and volume-decoding stages without retraining is practical and achieves consistent ~1.5x speedups on two major 3D backbones.
9Rxg1AHDrM.main_concern: Reviewers note limited technical novelty relative to FlashVDM's attention-based token selection and hierarchical decoding, modest 1.5x overall speedups not compared against simple step-reduction baselines, and missing hyperparameter details.

04AvD0OAzS.one_liner: Learns context-specific Nash equilibria from logged partial relative feedback using doubly robust payoff debiasing and Neyman-orthogonal loss.
04AvD0OAzS.problem: Transitive score-based evaluators like Bradley-Terry fail to capture cyclic collective preferences across heterogeneous human judges, while offline logs only observe partial agent subsets per context.
04AvD0OAzS.method: NashEval formulates contextual agent evaluation as a two-player zero-sum game whose context-dependent Nash equilibrium identifies the winning agent distribution. It constructs doubly robust debiased estimates of the contextual payoff matrix from logged partition feedback and trains a parametric context-to-equilibrium policy using a Neyman-orthogonal loss.
04AvD0OAzS.key_idea: Constructs doubly robust debiased payoff matrices from logged partial rankings and trains a contextual Nash equilibrium mapping via a Neyman-orthogonal objective.
04AvD0OAzS.evidence: Supported by Neyman-orthogonality and exploitability bounds and evaluated on simulated and logged preference datasets including RouterBench, MO-Highway, and LMArena.
04AvD0OAzS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified game-theoretic formulation that handles diverse relative-feedback formats and provides Neyman-orthogonal exploitability guarantees for contextual equilibrium learning.
04AvD0OAzS.main_concern: Reviewers note that intransitive preference cycles are demonstrated primarily on synthetically constructed multi-judge utilities rather than verified on real human preference data, and the debiasing construction relies on standard doubly robust assumptions.

HxNX63Myci.one_liner: Maintains a causal self-expanding geometry-pretrained latent state with KV reference memory for incremental unordered novel view synthesis.
HxNX63Myci.problem: Joint multi-view diffusion and continuous video-based novel view synthesis methods degrade when queried incrementally along unordered camera viewpoints.
HxNX63Myci.method: SEG constructs a Self-Expanding Geometric state from early layers of a pretrained geometric encoder supervised with causal-prefix ground truth so earlier states do not leak future views, paired with a KV reference memory. A causal geometric diffusion model iteratively expands this latent state for new camera queries, and a geometric adapter maps the generated latents to multi-level features for RGB decoding.
HxNX63Myci.key_idea: Supervises a causal geometric diffusion model on prefix-extracted geometric encoder latents stored in an expanding KV cache to synthesize arbitrary successive camera views.
HxNX63Myci.evidence: Evaluated on RealEstate10K and DL3DV under sequential and shuffled viewpoint queries against reconstruction, multi-view, and video-based NVS baselines.
HxNX63Myci.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SEG handles incremental and shuffled camera queries effectively on RealEstate10K and DL3DV while reducing runtime and memory compared to generative baselines.
HxNX63Myci.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing empirical comparisons with closely related causal autoregressive NVS methods (such as CausNVS and Mirage) and a lack of ablations isolating the advantage of geometric latents over standard 2D image latents under the same causal KV cache.

F5n55bk6Vs.one_liner: Crafts black-box adversarial patches against deployed Vision-Language-Action models by attacking visual tokens and instruction grounding on their public ancestor VLMs.
F5n55bk6Vs.problem: Existing adversarial attacks on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robotic models assume white-box access or surrogate VLAs, overlooking whether vulnerabilities inherited from public ancestor VLMs can be exploited black-box.
F5n55bk6Vs.method: The authors optimize adversarial image patches solely on the publicly available ancestor VLM of a target VLA using a two-phase curriculum that combines a vision disruption loss (corrupting projected visual tokens) and an instruction-grounded semantic evidence suppression loss. The resulting patches are applied directly in black-box fashion to downstream derived VLAs.
F5n55bk6Vs.key_idea: Optimizes adversarial patches on a public ancestor VLM to simultaneously corrupt projected visual token features and suppress logit-lens evidence for instruction-grounded concepts before transferring to derived VLAs.
F5n55bk6Vs.evidence: Evaluated across multiple VLA families (including OpenVLA, UniVLA, and pi0.5) on simulated manipulation suites and static real-world images.
F5n55bk6Vs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting publicly known ancestor VLMs as a zero-query black-box supply-chain attack surface against downstream VLAs is practical, realistic, and effective on models like OpenVLA and UniVLA.
F5n55bk6Vs.main_concern: Reviewers note that the approach closely parallels standard backbone-to-downstream transfer attacks, the semantic suppression loss adds only ~2% over visual disruption alone, and explanations for weak transfer to flow-matching VLAs (pi0.5) lack controlled quantitative verification.

IzDTEuEZo8.one_liner: Performs 2-bit quantization-aware training via arithmetic projection onto an implicit E8 lattice codebook with sparse out-of-bounds extension records.
IzDTEuEZo8.problem: Scalar low-bit quantization degrades LLM accuracy, whereas vector quantization with explicit codebooks requires expensive codebook lookup searches during quantization-aware training.
IzDTEuEZo8.method: E8-QAT jointly quantizes 8-dimensional weight groups during QAT via direct arithmetic nearest-point projection onto the E8 lattice, avoiding explicit codebook storage or search in the forward pass. For deployment, it encodes weights using a finite 2-bit core E8 codebook combined with sparse escape records that preserve out-of-range lattice points exactly.
IzDTEuEZo8.key_idea: Projects 8-weight blocks arithmetically onto an unbounded E8 lattice during QAT and exports them into a 2-bit core index plus sparse escape records for out-of-bounds points.
IzDTEuEZo8.evidence: Evaluated on LLMs including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B across four tasks including IFEval and LiveCodeBench against LC-QAT and full-precision BF16.
IzDTEuEZo8.claimed_gains: Adds less than 0.1% to core index storage, outperforms LC-QAT by 2.03 percentage points on IFEval and 1.51 percentage points on LiveCodeBench, reduces peak memory by 80%, supports a 4x larger batch, and reaches 1.97x the decoding throughput of BF16.
IzDTEuEZo8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical combination of search-free arithmetic E8 lattice projection during QAT with an exact 2-bit core-plus-sparse-escape export format that adds under 0.1% storage overhead.
IzDTEuEZo8.main_concern: Reviewers note that the arithmetic E8 QAT projection closely overlaps with a prior CPAL 2026 paper, gains over LC-QAT are confounded by a stronger E8-PTQ initialization, and throughput gains are only measured at enlarged maximum batch sizes without evaluating sparse-escape kernel overhead.

NXnnMHlyYx.one_liner: Detects probability mass shifts among interchangeable top-K candidate tokens and selectively relaxes upper PPO/GRPO clipping for positive updates.
NXnnMHlyYx.problem: Standard token-level importance-sampling clipping in LLM reinforcement learning overly clips positive-advantage tokens whose probability changes merely reflect mass redistribution among contextually interchangeable words.
NXnnMHlyYx.method: The authors define Spurious Policy Shift (SPS) as large token-probability ratios caused by probability mass shifting between the sampled token and interchangeable top-K candidate tokens under the old and new policies. They propose SPS-aware Clipping for Policy Optimization (SCPO), which detects SPS tokens using candidate-set probability mass metrics and selectively relaxes upper clipping thresholds on their positive-advantage updates.
NXnnMHlyYx.key_idea: Measures whether a sampled token's probability increase is offset by probability decreases among top-K old-policy candidates at the same state, relaxing upper IS-ratio clipping when this occurs.
NXnnMHlyYx.evidence: Evaluated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks across two LLM scales (including Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B) on top of GRPO against recent clipping baselines.
NXnnMHlyYx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical diagnosis of which positive-advantage tokens get upper-clipped during GRPO training interesting and appreciate that SCPO plugs in using quantities already available from rollouts.
NXnnMHlyYx.main_concern: Reviewers question whether probability shifts among top-K tokens are truly spurious rather than genuine policy changes, note that simply removing upper clipping achieves nearly identical mean accuracy on Qwen3-4B, and point out unvalidated interchangeability thresholds and single-seed runs.

VTi5wbtgBB.one_liner: Benchmarks next-state image generation from visual arrow-and-line folding instructions on origami tasks using an aspect-wise VLM judge.
VTi5wbtgBB.problem: Existing image editing benchmarks focus on natural-language instructions and lack controlled tests of whether models can interpret diagrammatic visual prompts (arrows, lines, symbols) and generate geometrically accurate state transitions.
VTi5wbtgBB.method: OrigamiGenBench provides current-state origami images overlaid with visual action prompts and auxiliary text instructions, requiring models to generate the resulting one-step-ahead folded state image. It evaluates recent image generation and editing models alongside human-folded references using an aspect-wise VLM-as-a-Judge protocol validated against human ratings.
VTi5wbtgBB.key_idea: Pairs current-state origami images with overlaid diagrammatic folding symbols to test one-step visual state transition generation, scored by an aspect-wise VLM judge.
VTi5wbtgBB.evidence: Evaluated across seven recent image generation and editing models, human-folded reference images, and human correlation studies (35 participants on 360 images).
VTi5wbtgBB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that origami folding provides a well-controlled, geometrically constrained testbed for visual instruction following, strengthened by human-folded upper-bound references and human-judge validation.
VTi5wbtgBB.main_concern: Reviewers note that unedited input images outscore nearly all evaluated models, human-VLM correlation is inflated by pooling low-scoring model outputs with high-scoring human references, and the single-domain origami dataset is small with underspecified construction details.

AYNxoJl3nq.one_liner: Equips each frozen LLM layer with gated matrix cell and hidden memory states connected via depth propagation and gradient feedback.
AYNxoJl3nq.problem: Compact online LLM memory adapters typically use a single persistent state for both history accumulation and attention readout, preventing separate control over what is stored versus exposed.
AYNxoJl3nq.method: LSTMem attaches two matrix-valued states to each layer of a frozen LLM: a gated cell state that accumulates interaction history via input and forget gates, and an output-gated hidden state that corrects backbone attention. It propagates hidden states forward across layers, applies block-end feedback, and uses higher-layer reconstruction gradients to refine lower-layer cell states.
AYNxoJl3nq.key_idea: Separates per-layer matrix memory into input/forget-gated cell states and output-gated hidden states linked across transformer depth by forward propagation and reconstruction-gradient feedback.
AYNxoJl3nq.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-4B-Instruct and additional backbones across MemoryAgentBench, LoCoMo, and HotpotQA against plain backbones and online memory adapters such as delta-Mem.
AYNxoJl3nq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the LSTM-inspired separation of storage cell states and readout hidden states with cross-layer propagation, noting improvements on LoCoMo under matched training.
AYNxoJl3nq.main_concern: Reviewers point out that evaluation retains the full historical KV cache in context—meaning the compact 36 KiB memory is never tested on its own after history eviction—and ablations do not isolate the cell/hidden split from extra trainable adapter parameters.

Gl5qCjakhL.one_liner: Retrofits pretrained LLM attention layers with blockwise local attention and test-time-updated recurrent neural memory modules.
Gl5qCjakhL.problem: Full attention incurs large KV-cache memory costs at long contexts, whereas training recurrent architectures from scratch sacrifices transformer pretraining parallelism and existing pretrained weights.
Gl5qCjakhL.method: Titan-Llama retrofits selected attention layers of a pretrained LLM during post-training by applying a blockwise attention mask that retains full attention over recent tokens while compressing older context into fixed-size recurrent neural memory modules (NMMs) updated at test time. This hybrid design avoids pretraining a new model from scratch.
Gl5qCjakhL.key_idea: Replaces selected pretrained attention layers with blockwise sliding-window attention coupled to fixed-size neural memory modules that update their parameters via test-time training over past blocks.
Gl5qCjakhL.evidence: Evaluated on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on QuALITY, LongHealth, and multi-query retrieval tasks along with prefill/decode latency and memory benchmarks.
Gl5qCjakhL.claimed_gains: Raises accuracy over segmented attention windows on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct from 23.87% to 40.51% on QuALITY and from 14.50% to 40.75% on LongHealth, with >20% faster prefill, 37% faster decode at medium contexts, and 24% lower steady-state decode memory.
Gl5qCjakhL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrofitting pretrained transformers with test-time neural memory modules without training from scratch is practical and substantially outperforms segmented-window attention.
Gl5qCjakhL.main_concern: Reviewers point out that quality experiments convert only 4 of the layers while leaving full attention in the remaining layers (which still access full history), whereas efficiency benchmarks convert more layers without reporting corresponding task accuracy.

soo58PvdjY.one_liner: Aligns dense KV caches across heterogeneous LLM agents using positional disentanglement, KV-group projections, and two-stage reconstruction-then-generation training.
soo58PvdjY.problem: Sparse KV-cache transfer between LLM agents degrades severely when the receiving agent has not observed the sender's source context, and heterogeneous models have incompatible cache geometries.
soo58PvdjY.method: The authors show that cache pruning harms communication when the receiver lacks the sender's input, and propose a dense cross-model KV-cache alignment framework combining positional disentanglement and KV-group transformations. The alignment adapters are trained in two stages: first reconstructing receiver-native KV caches, then optimizing end-to-end downstream generation.
soo58PvdjY.key_idea: Disentangles rotary positional encodings before applying KV-group transformations to dense sender KV caches, trained via receiver-cache reconstruction followed by generation supervision.
soo58PvdjY.evidence: Evaluated across six directed Qwen3 model pairs, three-agent document sharing, and cross-family Mistral-to-Qwen transfer under shared-input and unshared-input settings.
soo58PvdjY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis distinguishing context-aware from context-unaware latent communication and the clear two-stage reconstruction-then-generation training pipeline.
soo58PvdjY.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing module ablations for positional disentanglement, KV-group transformations, and two-stage training, potential unfairness from training the adapter on gold-answer reasoning traces, and omission of actual latency and payload transfer costs.

8KmbGvhpIO.one_liner: Injects multi-interest user themes into a diffusion model via residual preference attention and masked-interest training for generative image recommendation.
8KmbGvhpIO.problem: Standard recommender systems are restricted to fixed item catalogs, while generative recommenders must simultaneously preserve a user's historical preferences and extrapolate to novel items.
8KmbGvhpIO.method: GReCF frames generative recommendation as continuous-space collaborative preference completion and extracts adaptive multi-interest themes for each user, anchoring each image generation on a selected theme via residual preference attention inside a pretrained diffusion model. It combines shared multi-user training with a masked-interest objective that masks the target image's assigned theme so the model reconstructs it from remaining co-occurring themes, and introduces the 1M-interaction synthetic CIGR dataset.
8KmbGvhpIO.key_idea: Conditions a pretrained image diffusion model on clustered user interest themes through residual attention branches and trains it with a masked-theme reconstruction objective across users.
8KmbGvhpIO.evidence: Evaluated across three datasets (including the newly constructed 1M-interaction synthetic CIGR dataset) on ranking, personalization, image quality, coverage, and extrapolation metrics.
8KmbGvhpIO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find extending collaborative filtering to continuous-space image generation via multi-interest theme conditioning and masked-theme training an interesting problem formulation.
8KmbGvhpIO.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the link between the mathematical collaborative-filtering formulation and simply training a shared diffusion model is largely conceptual, noting that ablating masked-interest training actually improves recommendation accuracy and personalization.

ErrPMVCAoa.one_liner: Benchmarks LLMs on 30 constraint-satisfaction and domain-optimization tasks using physics-informed and domain-specific feasibility checkers.
ErrPMVCAoa.problem: Existing LLM reasoning benchmarks rarely test end-to-end optimization under interacting structural, physical, and operational constraints over structured graph and tabular inputs.
ErrPMVCAoa.method: ORC-Bench comprises 30 tasks across ten categories, three difficulty levels, and two modalities (graphs and tables), probing six skills including mathematical formulation and multi-step optimization (such as power-grid topology, contingency analysis, and optimal power flow). Models are scored by domain-specific and physics-informed checkers that measure output validity and constraint-satisfaction rates alongside objective accuracy.
ErrPMVCAoa.key_idea: Evaluates LLM solutions on 30 graph and tabular constrained-optimization tasks using programmatic physics-informed and domain-specific constraint-satisfaction verifiers.
ErrPMVCAoa.evidence: Evaluated across nine LLMs spanning diverse architectures, parameter scales, and reasoning regimes.
ErrPMVCAoa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating LLMs on realistic physical and operational constraint satisfaction over structured graph and tabular inputs fills an important benchmark gap.
ErrPMVCAoa.main_concern: Reviewers identify flawed ground-truth and scoring definitions in several tasks—such as scoring constraint discovery by exact string match when 93–95% of rejected formulas satisfy all data rows, and reporting per-constraint averages rather than joint solution feasibility and optimality gaps in Optimal Power Flow.

7saIJY2rnv.one_liner: Fine-tunes molecular graph diffusion models via forward-process distribution matching against a reward-tilted target over graph size and structure.
7saIJY2rnv.problem: Reinforcement learning methods that fine-tune molecular graph diffusion models along the reverse sampling trajectory suffer from training instability, chemical validity collapse, and fixed graph-size priors.
7saIJY2rnv.method: Graph Forward Distribution Matching (GraphFDM) collects valid generated molecules to define a reward-tilted target distribution jointly over node count (via a Structural Distribution Controller) and molecular graph structure. It then optimizes the diffusion generator through supervised forward-process denoising losses weighted by the reward-tilted target without storing or backpropagating through reverse trajectories.
7saIJY2rnv.key_idea: Reweights forward-process graph denoising losses and adapts the conditional graph-size prior toward an online reward-tilted distribution constructed solely from valid generated molecules.
7saIJY2rnv.evidence: Supported by theoretical target-optimality and improvement proofs and evaluated on multi-conditional polymer and small-molecule (QM9) inverse design benchmarks.
7saIJY2rnv.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest MAE on every target property with reductions of up to 53.0% relative to the strongest baselines and chemical validity above 0.99.
7saIJY2rnv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that converting reverse-trajectory RL into forward-process weighted denoising coupled with adaptive graph-size distribution learning is intuitive and achieves strong validity and property matching.
7saIJY2rnv.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the same random-forest property oracle used to compute training rewards (fitted on all labeled data including the test conditions) is also used as the primary test evaluator, risking reward hacking without independent oracle validation.

2YaCQP8Ceu.one_liner: Calibrates latent-space contrastive alignment perturbations against a refreshed model-state preference-flip threshold to prioritize harm avoidance under goal conflict.
2YaCQP8Ceu.problem: Autonomous LLM agents often fail to prioritize harm-avoidance rules when they conflict with task completion, or else over-apply caution and suppress benign actions.
2YaCQP8Ceu.method: BEHAVE adapts an LLM on 37 constitution-derived contrastive sentence stems by applying latent representation perturbations whose magnitude is calibrated relative to the current model state's preference-flip threshold between compliant and harmful continuations, periodically refreshing this threshold during training. The resulting priority transfer is evaluated on out-of-distribution operational decisions and multi-turn tool selection.
2YaCQP8Ceu.key_idea: Scales latent-space contrastive training perturbations relative to the minimal perturbation norm required to flip the model's log-probability preference on 37 constitutional stems, refreshing this threshold online.
2YaCQP8Ceu.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Ministral-3-14B, and Qwen3.6-27B) on Harm Avoidance, Control Pragmatism, capability/over-refusal benchmarks, and multi-turn tool-use evaluations (PropensityBench).
2YaCQP8Ceu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on principle prioritization under agentic goal conflict, the dual measurement of Harm Avoidance and benign Control Pragmatism, and the transfer from 37 first-person stems to multi-turn tool use.
2YaCQP8Ceu.main_concern: Reviewers note that behavior-relative threshold calibration shows little or no consistent advantage over a tuned fixed-radius latent perturbation baseline (CLPA_C), with confounded training budgets on Qwen2.5-7B and a fixed intervention layer selected only at initialization.

YzIlhcjUs1.one_liner: Splits LLM token watermarking between a public detector key and a private forensic key, detecting adversarial tampering via score-imbalance tests.
YzIlhcjUs1.problem: Releasing an LLM watermark detector publicly lets adversaries use detector feedback to guide watermark removal or forgery edits.
YzIlhcjUs1.method: The authors quantify the incremental removal and forgery risk of public detectors across access levels and propose a split-key watermarking scheme that randomly routes tokens between a public key and a private key. A two-stage private verification pipeline combines the full joint watermark score with a sign-flip permutation statistical test that detects score imbalances between the public and private keys caused by public-detector-guided tampering.
YzIlhcjUs1.key_idea: Embeds watermarks using separate public and private keys across tokens and flags adversarial tampering or forgery by testing for statistical divergence between public and private detection scores.
YzIlhcjUs1.evidence: Evaluated against uninformed and detector-informed watermark removal and forgery attacks across varying edit budgets and detector access levels.
YzIlhcjUs1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that quantifying the marginal risk of public watermark detectors relative to uninformed attacks and leveraging public-private score asymmetry for forensic detection is a timely and well-framed approach.
YzIlhcjUs1.main_concern: Reviewers point out that adaptive and stronger model-based paraphrasing/stealing attacks (such as DIPPER or SIRA) are either not evaluated or still achieve high attack success rates, and the paper lacks empirical comparisons against prior dual-key watermarking schemes like TextSeal.

CRiHNlKJSB.one_liner: Couples VLM semantic grounding with 3D reconstruction to build a 7,000-QA outdoor video spatial benchmark.
CRiHNlKJSB.problem: Existing spatial understanding benchmarks focus on local or indoor scene-level relations, leaving long-horizon spatial integration in continuous outdoor videos underexplored.
CRiHNlKJSB.method: They build SpatialRoute-Bench using an automated pipeline that pairs VLM-based landmark grounding with streaming 3D reconstruction of camera poses, trajectories, and scene geometry. Task-specific generators convert this geometric and semantic evidence into 7,000 multiple-choice QA pairs across perception, reasoning, and decision tasks.
CRiHNlKJSB.key_idea: Derives multiple-choice spatial questions automatically by combining VLM-grounded semantic landmarks with reconstructed 3D camera trajectories and scene geometry.
CRiHNlKJSB.evidence: Evaluated across seven tasks and 7,000 multiple-choice QA pairs on open-source and proprietary VLMs using local/long-range task pairs and frame-order perturbations.
CRiHNlKJSB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the benchmark addresses a meaningful gap in long-horizon outdoor spatial reasoning with a structured three-level task hierarchy and geometry-derived ground truth.
CRiHNlKJSB.main_concern: Reviewers note missing details on video count, duration, and sampled frame counts, alongside limited evaluation of dynamic mobile objects, global map integration, and related outdoor benchmarks.

5U3S6GhIss.one_liner: Uses top-k student-teacher token overlap to reweight rewards and adaptively truncate on-policy distillation rollouts.
5U3S6GhIss.problem: Standard on-policy distillation uses a fixed rollout budget that ignores how well student and teacher predictions match along generated responses.
5U3S6GhIss.method: Prune-OPD measures local student-teacher compatibility via top-k token overlap, reweights rewards after cumulative mismatches, and dynamically updates rollout truncation lengths within configured bounds. This curtails weakly compatible suffixes online without manual per-pair length schedules.
5U3S6GhIss.key_idea: Measures local student-teacher top-k token overlap to reweight rewards after cumulative mismatches and adaptively update rollout truncation length.
5U3S6GhIss.evidence: Evaluated across four student-teacher pairs (including DeepSeek-7B/Skywork-7B) on mathematical reasoning benchmarks AMC, AIME, and HMMT.
5U3S6GhIss.claimed_gains: Reduces reported training time by 37.6%–68.0% across four student-teacher pairs while broadly preserving accuracy on AMC, AIME, and HMMT.
5U3S6GhIss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that dynamically adjusting rollout lengths from student-teacher compatibility feedback is intuitive and yields substantial training-time reductions while preserving accuracy.
5U3S6GhIss.main_concern: Reviewers question the heuristic nature of unweighted top-k overlap and reliability decrements, as well as the evaluation being restricted to mathematical reasoning and relatively weak teachers.

OsJyNOxsWi.one_liner: Initializes flexible scene anchors from a continuous field and compresses multi-view tokens via geometry-grounded attention.
OsJyNOxsWi.problem: Large view synthesis models incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs because scene token counts grow redundantly with reference views.
OsJyNOxsWi.method: GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field to initialize a flexible number of scene anchors matching a target budget, paired with an end-to-end trained condenser that aggregates scene information. The condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression via geometry-grounded attention and enable frustum culling during decoding.
OsJyNOxsWi.key_idea: Combines a continuous anchor-initialization field with a geometry-inferring condenser that compresses multi-view tokens via geometry-grounded attention and frustum culling.
OsJyNOxsWi.evidence: Evaluated on RealEstate10K and DL3DV across multiple reference-view counts and compression ratios against random, K-means, learned pruning, and CLiFT-style condensation baselines.
OsJyNOxsWi.claimed_gains: Reduces scene-token count by 33.4% with a 1.23x rendering speedup at no quality loss, or by 85.5% with a 3.00x rendering speedup under a relaxed quality-loss budget.
OsJyNOxsWi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that consolidating multi-view observations into flexible-budget anchors achieves strong rendering-quality versus token-count trade-offs in controlled comparisons.
OsJyNOxsWi.main_concern: Reviewers state that the claimed emergence of 3D geometry lacks quantitative validation and pretraining controls, and that main speedup numbers omit the overhead of running the condenser.

bEgbKyQyCy.one_liner: Physically measured point-pair distances directly evaluate metric scale in reconstructed geometry across image and video models.
bEgbKyQyCy.problem: Separate depth, camera-intrinsics, and geometric-similarity evaluations do not directly measure physical point-to-point distance estimation.
bEgbKyQyCy.method: Pumpire collects real-world scenes with physically measured point-pair distances and evaluates distance errors from reconstructed geometry. Its unified protocol covers image- and video-level 3D foundation models with or without depth priors.
bEgbKyQyCy.key_idea: Compare distances between reconstructed point pairs against independent physical measurements under a shared cross-model protocol.
bEgbKyQyCy.evidence: The pumpire-6k dataset includes 100 real-world scenes with 64 frames each, totaling 6,400 frames, and experiments evaluate 29 baseline configurations.
bEgbKyQyCy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value direct metric-distance evaluation, physically measured ground truth, and comparisons across 3D model types.
bEgbKyQyCy.main_concern: The benchmark's added value and coverage relative to existing geometry benchmarks are not sufficiently established.

DVoebUQIeI.one_liner: SalTempto pairs action-centric video clips with gaze recordings to test saliency prediction under stronger temporal dynamics.
DVoebUQIeI.problem: Existing video saliency benchmarks may reward static prediction without requiring temporal context.
DVoebUQIeI.method: SalTempto collects gaze recordings for 224 one-minute action-centric HACS-Segments clips and compares static and temporal saliency models. The study also revisits LEDOV with an improved gold standard and recent architectures.
DVoebUQIeI.key_idea: Use action-centric clips and gaze recordings to measure how much saliency information static predictors miss.
DVoebUQIeI.evidence: Comparisons on LEDOV and SalTempto use recent temporal architectures, a fine-tuned static baseline, and gaze recordings from up to 16 subjects.
DVoebUQIeI.claimed_gains: On SalTempto, the fine-tuned static baseline recovers only about 13% of the available gaze information.
DVoebUQIeI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the dataset construction and its usefulness for studying temporal video saliency.
DVoebUQIeI.main_concern: The dataset's limited scale and observer coverage leave the empirical contribution incomplete.

PEuMlzgIoB.one_liner: A transformer uses stimulus-dependent self-attention to probe sparse neural population readout under neuronal and sensory perturbations.
PEuMlzgIoB.problem: Conventional neural decoders reveal available information but provide limited insight into flexible population readout.
PEuMlzgIoB.method: The framework applies self-attention to macaque V1 recordings and analyzes attention relative to neuronal tuning. It removes dominant readout neurons, retrains the model, and tests decoding under reduced contrast and external noise.
PEuMlzgIoB.key_idea: Inspect stimulus-dependent attention weights and their reassignment after neuron removal to probe selective population readout.
PEuMlzgIoB.evidence: Large-scale macaque V1 recordings support analyses of neuronal tuning, neuron-removal retraining, and orientation decoding under contrast and noise perturbations.
PEuMlzgIoB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the macaque population recordings and their relevance to understanding visual neural encoding.
PEuMlzgIoB.main_concern: Sorting neurons by orientation preference before positional encoding introduces potential bias and insufficiently documented train-test independence.

lwoSRI7U8V.one_liner: EduMCTS searches over pedagogical interventions to construct verified interactive reasoning trajectories for language-model training.
lwoSRI7U8V.problem: Reasoning-data augmentation often selects among candidate solutions without actively improving intermediate reasoning during generation.
lwoSRI7U8V.method: EduMCTS makes pedagogical strategies executable tree-search actions and scores reasoning paths using local progress and final-answer correctness. The resulting verified interactive trajectories provide post-training supervision.
lwoSRI7U8V.key_idea: Search over typed teaching interventions at intermediate reasoning states and retain verified trajectories with pedagogical feedback.
lwoSRI7U8V.evidence: Experiments span three LLMs and eleven benchmarks covering seven mathematical and four scientific reasoning tasks, with component ablations.
lwoSRI7U8V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent improvements over reasoning-data augmentation baselines across models and benchmarks.
lwoSRI7U8V.main_concern: Unreported synthesis costs and unmatched search budgets leave the advantage over simpler data-generation methods unclear.

falM6GwzJq.one_liner: DANCE treats continuous EEG decoding as set prediction to jointly locate and classify events without known onsets.
falM6GwzJq.problem: Onset-aligned EEG classification assumes timing information unavailable in continuous monitoring and asynchronous brain-computer interfaces.
falM6GwzJq.method: DANCE combines convolutional processing, Perceiver temporal resampling, and DETR-style set prediction to infer event timing, duration, and class directly from raw unaligned EEG.
falM6GwzJq.key_idea: Predict a set of temporally localized, typed events directly from continuous EEG instead of classifying onset-aligned windows.
falM6GwzJq.evidence: Separate evaluations on ten literature-curated datasets cover cognitive, clinical, and BCI events ranging from milliseconds to minutes, including seizure monitoring.
falM6GwzJq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value onset-free EEG event detection and the breadth of event types and durations covered by one architecture.
falM6GwzJq.main_concern: Baseline event-construction limitations and evaluation choices may explain part of the reported event-level advantage.

5NBFbyOBUZ.one_liner: Pair-aware SCFF adds cross-branch spike correspondence to local goodness functions for unsupervised spiking-network learning.
5NBFbyOBUZ.problem: Activity-only goodness evaluates fused firing strength without testing the relationships used to construct self-contrastive pairs.
5NBFbyOBUZ.method: Pair-aware SCFF measures spike co-activation relative to marginal firing and combines this relational signal with activity-supported pair evidence. Training remains layer-local without class labels or network-wide error propagation.
5NBFbyOBUZ.key_idea: Compare cross-branch spike co-activation with marginal firing activity when assigning local goodness to input pairs.
5NBFbyOBUZ.evidence: Experiments cover six static-image and two event-based datasets, with matched Spiking SCFF comparisons and ablations of goodness and pair-stream propagation.
5NBFbyOBUZ.claimed_gains: Accuracy improves by up to 10.71 percentage points over the matched Spiking SCFF baseline.
5NBFbyOBUZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly measuring pair correspondence addresses a well-motivated mismatch in spiking self-contrastive learning.
5NBFbyOBUZ.main_concern: Baseline coverage and calibration are insufficient to establish the method's advantage beyond the matched Spiking SCFF implementation.

jQ3F4u2t5u.one_liner: TAPER jointly adapts reasoning-length pressure to online accuracy and applies region-specific teacher supervision.
jQ3F4u2t5u.problem: Uniformly shortening reasoning can remove useful computation together with redundant verification and backtracking.
jQ3F4u2t5u.method: TAPER estimates problem-level competence from online samples to adjust a relative-length objective. It jointly optimizes asymmetric teacher supervision with different objectives for reasoning and answer tokens on the same trajectories.
jQ3F4u2t5u.key_idea: Couple accuracy-adaptive trajectory compression with asymmetric token-level teacher objectives for reasoning and answer regions.
jQ3F4u2t5u.evidence: Experiments compare six baselines using Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B on five mathematical, knowledge-intensive, and logical reasoning benchmarks.
jQ3F4u2t5u.claimed_gains: TAPER improves accuracy over GRPO by 1.2–7.9 percentage points while using 18.4%–66.4% fewer thinking tokens.
jQ3F4u2t5u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear presentation and the combination of reasoning-budget control with teacher-guided reasoning behavior.
jQ3F4u2t5u.main_concern: The comparisons do not sufficiently separate the proposed optimization's contribution from the benefit of access to a stronger teacher.

esNaWlyXGa.one_liner: Betting e-processes certify randomized-smoothing robustness under adaptive stopping, with a separate rule for abandoning unlikely certificates.
esNaWlyXGa.problem: Repeated inspection and data-dependent stopping invalidate ordinary fixed-sample Monte Carlo confidence guarantees.
esNaWlyXGa.method: The paper builds bounded predictable witnesses for mean, mean-variance, and discretized-CDF certificates whose betting products form e-processes. Reverse-information-projection guidance refines betting, while a validity-preserving futility rule terminates unlikely certifications early.
esNaWlyXGa.key_idea: Test certificate failure with betting products that retain error control under arbitrary stopping and a separately controlled futility decision.
esNaWlyXGa.evidence: Theoretical guarantees cover multiple certificate types, and CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments ablate witnesses, betting strategies, monitoring, and futility stopping.
esNaWlyXGa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the sequential-validity guarantees and extension of betting methods to multiple robustness certificate types.
esNaWlyXGa.main_concern: The practical advantage over strong certification baselines remains unclear beyond small sampling budgets.

fQTAcmvhbi.one_liner: Activation-space displacements toward helpful-only reference models define a safety-reversion direction tested during benign fine-tuning.
fQTAcmvhbi.problem: Benign post-training can erode safety alignment, but the behavioral relevance of a common reversion direction needs testing.
fQTAcmvhbi.method: The study defines an activation-space direction from aligned models toward independent helpful-only references and measures movement during adaptation. Optimizer-matched blocking and separately stabilized reinforcing objectives test its relationship to harmfulness.
fQTAcmvhbi.key_idea: Define a reference-based activation displacement before fine-tuning, then oppose or reinforce motion along that coordinate during adaptation.
fQTAcmvhbi.evidence: Matched-null trajectory analyses and adaptation interventions cover Llama, Qwen, and Gemma settings from 3B to 14B, with random-direction controls.
fQTAcmvhbi.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a Spearman r=0.958 correlation between directional alignment and harmfulness, without numerical intervention gains.
fQTAcmvhbi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value diagnosing safety degradation during benign fine-tuning and testing the geometric direction across model settings.
fQTAcmvhbi.main_concern: Random-direction blocking also improves safety, so the causal benefit is not specific to the proposed reversion direction.

PNJDdNSYwN.one_liner: PARSEE coordinates token retention with physical page allocation to turn KV eviction into reusable serving memory.
PNJDdNSYwN.problem: Unequal per-head retention and page granularity can prevent logical KV-cache compression from releasing usable GPU capacity.
PNJDdNSYwN.method: PARSEE combines shared semantic and head-specific question evidence through disjoint quotas, then allocates whole pages by marginal utility under a physical budget. Its backend packs retained entries, transfers page ownership, and reclaims dense blocks.
PNJDdNSYwN.key_idea: Coordinate retained counts across page-sharing heads while preserving token identities, then compile selection into reclaimed physical pages.
PNJDdNSYwN.evidence: Experiments cover five Qwen and Llama models with dense, grouped-query, hybrid, and mixture-of-experts architectures, plus SCBench and serving-throughput evaluation.
PNJDdNSYwN.claimed_gains: PARSEE retains near-lossless SCBench performance on Qwen3.8-27B at 90% prefill-context KV compression and achieves up to 5.28× uncompressed-vLLM throughput with its Qwen3-8B backend.
PNJDdNSYwN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing physical storage waste and connecting KV selection to actual memory reclamation and serving concurrency.
PNJDdNSYwN.main_concern: End-to-end efficiency comparisons do not consistently include scoring, selection, and cache-management overheads.

g36UdlaLQn.one_liner: EDDY combines Stein-transformed anti-symmetric particle interactions with a coupled prior for diverse diffusion sampling.
g36UdlaLQn.problem: Repulsive particle guidance can increase diversity by pushing samples away from the data distribution and introducing artifacts.
g36UdlaLQn.method: EDDY constructs drift perturbations from anti-symmetric matrix fields passed through a Stein operator and combines them with a coupled prior preserving initial particle marginals. Finite differences and Hutchinson estimates approximate second-order terms for perceptual kernels.
g36UdlaLQn.key_idea: Pair coupled initialization with Stein-based anti-symmetric interactions whose drift preserves the Fokker–Planck equation under independence.
g36UdlaLQn.evidence: Theoretical analysis studies marginal preservation and dependence, while experiments compare FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.2-klein, and SDXL at matched diversity.
g36UdlaLQn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize encouraging empirical quality and prompt-alignment results relative to particle-guidance baselines.
g36UdlaLQn.main_concern: The method's specific drift construction and its connection to the theoretical results need clearer justification.

QekNiN2I9H.one_liner: BandRider exploits rank-based speculative verification by injecting low-probability commitment tokens from a compromised draft model.
QekNiN2I9H.problem: Speculative-decoding acceptance rules can create a security channel from an untrusted draft into an aligned target's responses.
QekNiN2I9H.method: The study compares probability-checking and rank-based verification, identifies commitment tokens with acceptable rank but negligible probability, and tests sustained draft-only injection. A poisoned draft demonstrates the channel through changed draft weights.
QekNiN2I9H.key_idea: Exploit tokens that pass top-k verification despite negligible target probability to commit subsequent generation toward compliance.
QekNiN2I9H.evidence: Experiments cover seven targets from five model families, four harmful-instruction corpora, several verification rules, and a weights-only poisoned draft.
QekNiN2I9H.claimed_gains: Sustained multi-round injection reaches 74% judged compliance on Llama-3-8B and 80% with a weights-only poisoned draft.
QekNiN2I9H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the security risk of combining an attacker-controlled draft with rank-based verification while leaving the target unchanged.
QekNiN2I9H.main_concern: Evidence of practical applicability is limited because the attack requires draft control and specific verification and target-response conditions.

OWsSUwyLyQ.one_liner: RAQ-MLA fits separate quantization transforms to latent-value error and positional-key score error in MLA caches.
OWsSUwyLyQ.problem: Standard KV-cache quantization overlooks the different roles of compressed latents and positional keys in multi-head latent attention.
OWsSUwyLyQ.method: RAQ-MLA analyzes cache distributions and error propagation, then fits invertible transforms against attention-weighted value error for latents and attention-score perturbations for positional keys.
OWsSUwyLyQ.key_idea: Optimize each cached tensor's invertible quantization transform against the distinct error it contributes to attention output.
OWsSUwyLyQ.evidence: Experiments on GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-5.2, Moonlight, and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite evaluate reasoning, coding, retrieval, and component ablations.
OWsSUwyLyQ.claimed_gains: RAQ-MLA quantizes the full cache to about 2.5 bits per element, yielding a 6.5× increase in theoretical KV-cache capacity.
OWsSUwyLyQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the role-based analysis and the resulting low-bit compression and accuracy trade-off.
OWsSUwyLyQ.main_concern: The MLA-specific role assumptions and transform benefits need stronger isolation and validation under the final low-bit configuration across models.

MwFdOxduVP.one_liner: Readout-to-target norm ratios predict how long early representation collapse persists in dense-target self-supervised regression.
MwFdOxduVP.problem: Target-scale mismatch can induce prolonged representation collapse despite otherwise standard normalized encoder and readout architectures.
MwFdOxduVP.method: The study varies target scale and readout initialization to control their norm ratio, measures collapse and recovery, and decomposes initial gradients to analyze shared input shifts and output shrinkage.
MwFdOxduVP.key_idea: Express target-scale mismatch as the initial readout-output norm divided by target norm and track collapse duration as that ratio changes.
MwFdOxduVP.evidence: Experiments use MelHuBERT on LibriSpeech at nine ratios with three seeds, plus 960-hour training, MAE on ImageNet-100, and a data2vec-style teacher.
MwFdOxduVP.claimed_gains: Collapse lasts 60 to 80 steps at ratio 0.58, about 2,000 at 4.52, and more than 11,000 at 37.3, with 183 of 188 clearly ordered run pairs following ratio order.
MwFdOxduVP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the readout-to-target ratio interpretable and useful as a diagnostic of early representation collapse.
MwFdOxduVP.main_concern: The initialization-gradient analysis does not fully explain why collapse recovery time depends on the ratio.

mF7xMScF25.one_liner: DUDE trains image-dependent tokens through diffusion denoising and progressively aligns neighboring features across visual domains.
mF7xMScF25.problem: Whole-image alignment entangles category-relevant object features with domain-specific styles in unsupervised cross-domain retrieval.
mF7xMScF25.method: DUDE uses a frozen text-to-image diffusion model to train image-dependent object tokens while domain prompts supply style information. It progressively aligns mutual neighbors within and across domains, retaining only the image encoder at retrieval time.
mF7xMScF25.key_idea: Separate image-dependent object tokens from domain prompts during denoising, then progressively align mutual-neighbor object representations across domains.
mF7xMScF25.evidence: Experiments span three retrieval benchmarks and 13 domains, with prompt-swapping examples and representation and alignment ablations.
mF7xMScF25.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find diffusion-guided object-style separation intuitive and appreciate the reported retrieval gains and encoder-only inference.
mF7xMScF25.main_concern: The denoising objective does not enforce object-style disentanglement, and direct evidence that the learned token excludes style remains limited.

RONkIKXtpM.one_liner: StructLFGS derives a shared camera family from angular trajectories to reconstruct light fields with Gaussian splatting.
RONkIKXtpM.problem: Independent camera-pose estimation ignores shared narrow-baseline light-field geometry and can introduce pose drift.
RONkIKXtpM.method: StructLFGS replaces per-view poses with a compact structured camera family whose canonical parameters come from observed angular trajectories. Fixed cameras, trajectory-based initialization, and disparity supervision guide Gaussian geometry.
RONkIKXtpM.key_idea: Infer one shared canonical camera parameterization from angular trajectories and keep it fixed during Gaussian reconstruction.
RONkIKXtpM.evidence: Four light-field benchmarks compare Gaussian-splatting and LF-specific methods, with ablations of camera constraints, initialization, and disparity information.
RONkIKXtpM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the structured-camera formulation and ablations evaluating its reconstruction components.
RONkIKXtpM.main_concern: Different camera information and target-pose procedures across methods complicate fair attribution of the Gaussian-splatting comparison gains.

UhfyCPhNWY.one_liner: SuREST probes hidden-state evidence sufficiency to control retrieval triggering, passage selection, and stopping.
UhfyCPhNWY.problem: Relevant passages can remain insufficient or redundant, while explicit model judgments may miss sufficiency information encoded internally.
UhfyCPhNWY.method: SuREST trains a lightweight probe to recover evidence sufficiency from hidden representations and uses its scores throughout adaptive retrieval, including selecting evidence and deciding when to stop.
UhfyCPhNWY.key_idea: Use a hidden-state sufficiency probe as a shared control signal for acquiring, retaining, and stopping retrieval of evidence.
UhfyCPhNWY.evidence: Evaluation uses four Wikipedia-based multi-hop QA benchmarks, paired sufficiency data, and analyses of evidence redundancy and coverage.
UhfyCPhNWY.claimed_gains: With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SuREST improves macro F1 by 2.36 points over IRCoT while reducing retained passages by 56.7% and end-to-end inference time by 53.6%.
UhfyCPhNWY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing evidence relevance from sufficiency and using internal sufficiency information to guide retrieval.
UhfyCPhNWY.main_concern: The probe requires substantial supervised construction, and supervision-matched controls are missing to isolate the benefit of the latent readout.

I7GxcqXZqx.one_liner: BoundaryMORPH spends limited cross-encoder calls on uncertain top-k membership using a Gaussian-process ranking prior.
I7GxcqXZqx.problem: When reranking budgets are smaller than context capacity, scoring obvious top candidates can miss useful lower-ranked documents.
I7GxcqXZqx.method: BoundaryMORPH treats the dual-encoder ranking as a Gaussian-process structural prior and chooses cross-encoder evaluations near the top-k membership boundary. Each observed score updates predictions for unscored documents.
I7GxcqXZqx.key_idea: Allocate cross-encoder queries to resolve uncertain context-set membership and propagate their scores through a Gaussian-process prior.
I7GxcqXZqx.evidence: Experiments compare multiple models and open-ended retrieval datasets and ablate the ranking prior and boundary-selection rule.
I7GxcqXZqx.claimed_gains: BoundaryMORPH improves nCG@100 by +5.4 pp over the strongest baseline.
I7GxcqXZqx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize retrieval gains and ablation evidence that both the ranking prior and boundary selection contribute.
I7GxcqXZqx.main_concern: Practical end-to-end efficiency remains unclear because sequential scoring and Gaussian-process updates may offset savings from fewer cross-encoder calls.

moVb2UIyYl.one_liner: MUSE generates image-question-conditioned system-prompt embeddings to suppress selected knowledge in a frozen multimodal model.
moVb2UIyYl.problem: Parameter-level multimodal unlearning can require substantial training and storage while struggling to balance forgetting and retention.
moVb2UIyYl.method: A Multimodal Embedding Adapter generates input-conditioned system prompts for a frozen MLLM. An asymmetric dual-space objective constrains both prompt embeddings and internal representations to control selective suppression and preservation.
moVb2UIyYl.key_idea: Condition trainable system-prompt embeddings on each image-question pair and constrain their effects in prompt and representation spaces.
moVb2UIyYl.evidence: MLLMU-Bench experiments on LLaVA-1.5-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B include forgetting, retention, prompt attacks, efficiency comparisons, and component ablations.
moVb2UIyYl.claimed_gains: MUSE achieves up to 4.9× faster training and 74.2% lower GPU memory usage than the strongest baseline.
moVb2UIyYl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate input-specific suppression through an efficient, reversible adapter that leaves the backbone frozen.
moVb2UIyYl.main_concern: Omitted text-only evaluations leave uncertainty about how reliably targeted knowledge remains inaccessible outside the tested multimodal setting.

XSaVOzBlOw.one_liner: Sparse multidimensional comparisons build personalized judgment scales, which SubJudge distills into single-pass continuous scores.
XSaVOzBlOw.problem: Subjective intensity varies by person and is difficult to quantify efficiently for high-traffic applications.
XSaVOzBlOw.method: The framework combines sparse Elo comparisons across cases and profiles with multi-judge voting. SubJudge learns relative rankings through Bradley–Terry-based Batchwise Preference Optimization and reads scores from first-position digit-token probabilities.
XSaVOzBlOw.key_idea: Construct comparative scales from case-person pairs, then train a compact judge to encode continuous scores in digit-token probabilities.
XSaVOzBlOw.evidence: Experiments on PluriHarms and iNews compare 9B models with frontier LLM judges and evaluate inference on an H100 GPU.
XSaVOzBlOw.claimed_gains: Sparse comparisons reduce scale-construction cost from O(N^2) to O(NK), while one forward pass per criterion reduces inference complexity to O(1).
XSaVOzBlOw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value efficient personalized subjective scoring through comparative supervision and smaller learned judges.
XSaVOzBlOw.main_concern: Missing simpler distillation and training baselines prevent attribution of gains to Elo scale construction and Batchwise Preference Optimization.

xpyqgmB13B.one_liner: Relative Density Ratio Optimization bounds preference density ratios by mixing preferred and non-preferred distributions in the denominator.
xpyqgmB13B.problem: Direct density-ratio alignment can become unstable when preferred-to-non-preferred ratios diverge.
xpyqgmB13B.method: RDRO estimates the ratio of preferred data density to a mixture of preferred and non-preferred densities, producing a bounded alignment objective. The paper analyzes its population optimum and convergence behavior.
xpyqgmB13B.key_idea: Replace the ordinary preference density ratio with a bounded relative ratio whose denominator mixes both preference distributions.
xpyqgmB13B.evidence: Theoretical consistency and convergence analyses accompany experiments with Qwen 2.5 and Llama 3, covering four models, two datasets, and three seeds.
xpyqgmB13B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the instability problem well motivated and the bounded relative-ratio formulation theoretically interesting.
xpyqgmB13B.main_concern: The assumptions and finite-sample analysis need stronger justification for the estimator and reference policy used in training.

RUcen8jBUM.one_liner: CENO predicts value functions, constructs consistent mean-field populations, and bounds policy exploitability using Bellman defects.
RUcen8jBUM.problem: Amortized neural mean-field-game solvers can predict policies and populations that fail to form an equilibrium.
RUcen8jBUM.method: CENO predicts candidate values, derives a Gibbs policy, and propagates the population through that policy's dynamics. A Bellman-defect certificate bounds exploitability without a reference equilibrium or extra best-response solve.
RUcen8jBUM.key_idea: Construct policy and population from predicted values, then certify individual optimality using the values' Bellman defect.
RUcen8jBUM.evidence: The paper derives certificates for finite-state, entropy-regularized mean-field games and evaluates three population-level tasks in an open-system simulator.
RUcen8jBUM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a computable equilibrium certificate that avoids an additional best-response solve.
RUcen8jBUM.main_concern: Restrictive finite-horizon assumptions limit how directly the theoretical guarantees support broader games and continuing-horizon experiments.

3y70lKgk9Y.one_liner: Experience Distillation trains agents on experience-conditioned teacher decisions without collecting additional environment interactions.
3y70lKgk9Y.problem: In-context learning benefits from interaction histories disappear when those histories leave the context, while further environment sampling is costly.
3y70lKgk9Y.method: An experience-conditioned teacher generates replacement decisions at recorded histories, and supervised distillation transfers those decisions into student weights. Branch packing supports training without additional environment rollouts.
3y70lKgk9Y.key_idea: Generate teacher action targets at recorded histories using the full experience context, then distill them into a student that does not require that context.
3y70lKgk9Y.evidence: Experiments use 749 curated software-engineering tasks and six text-adventure games, with SFT and RL comparisons, branch-packing ablations, and repeated collect-and-distill cycles.
3y70lKgk9Y.claimed_gains: Experience Distillation retains at least 64.8% of in-context learning gains versus 3.8% for direct SFT and matches classical RL baselines with at least 9.6× fewer environment samples.
3y70lKgk9Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate internalizing useful agent experience without additional environment interactions and the gains over direct SFT.
3y70lKgk9Y.main_concern: Missing comparisons with existing context-distillation and experience-learning methods leave the distinctive contribution insufficiently established.

32TrmcAv3r.one_liner: Distills pre-trained autoregressive driving VLAs into multi-task discrete diffusion models through a three-stage hierarchical adaptation and distillation pipeline.
32TrmcAv3r.problem: Autoregressive driving vision-language-action models suffer from sequential decoding latency and exposure bias, while diffusion policies trained from scratch lack broad visual-linguistic reasoning and face causal-to-bidirectional conversion mismatches.
32TrmcAv3r.method: WAM-Diff2 converts a pre-trained autoregressive VLA into a parallel multi-task discrete block-diffusion model using a three-stage hierarchical strategy: progressive block-wise adaptation, block-wise distillation, and model-wise cross-scale distillation. A single checkpoint supports runtime-adjustable block decoding across driving understanding, perception, and planning tasks.
32TrmcAv3r.key_idea: Bridge causal autoregressive and bidirectional diffusion VLA architectures via progressive block-wise adaptation followed by block-wise and model-wise cross-scale distillation.
32TrmcAv3r.evidence: Evaluated across driving language understanding, perception, and open-loop (NAVSIM v1/v2) and closed-loop planning benchmarks, plus throughput and prefix-perturbation analyses.
32TrmcAv3r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that converting an autoregressive VLA into a single multi-task block-diffusion checkpoint addresses practical inference latency while preserving driving understanding, perception, and planning performance.
32TrmcAv3r.main_concern: Reviewers point out asymmetric system-optimization comparisons where FlashInfer and CUDA Graphs are applied only to the diffusion model, split hardware benchmarking (Ascend 910C NPU vs. CUDA), and underspecified trajectory selection and Stage I contributions.

QiNIjyU0gq.one_liner: Constructs 6,701 deterministic multiple-choice video questions from AVAv2.2 annotations to diagnose five person-centered capabilities in vision-language models.
QiNIjyU0gq.problem: High aggregate scores of video vision-language models on standard benchmarks conceal failures in binding actions, transitions, interactions, and gaze to specific individuals.
QiNIjyU0gq.method: ActionLens deterministically derives 6,701 multiple-choice questions from AVAv2.2's 1.58 million per-second, per-person annotations—refined over 14 rounds of human quality engineering—across five diagnostics: action-transition sensitivity, actor-specific action disambiguation, concurrent action recognition, interaction-role and co-action assignment, and gaze detection. It also includes coordinate-variant ablations replacing visual bounding-box overlays with text coordinates and co-actor binding-trap distractor analyses.
QiNIjyU0gq.key_idea: Deterministically generate person-centered multiple-choice video probes with co-actor binding traps and box-versus-coordinate controls directly from dense per-second human action annotations.
QiNIjyU0gq.evidence: Evaluates 20 vision-language models against human performance across 6,701 questions from 64 AVAv2.2 source videos, including coordinate-grounding ablations and 16-model binding-trap analyses.
QiNIjyU0gq.claimed_gains: Fourteen quality-engineering rounds raised human accuracy from 53% to above 90%, while across 20 VLMs the best open-weight model achieves 68.8% weighted average accuracy against 91.0% for humans (with gaze detection near chance vs. 89.6% human accuracy), text coordinates expose up to a 19.2-point grounding deficit, and 13 of 16 models systematically select the wrong actor's action on D2.
QiNIjyU0gq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deterministic derivation from human annotations without LLM label generation and the co-actor binding-trap design expose genuine person-level grounding failures hidden by aggregate video QA metrics.
QiNIjyU0gq.main_concern: Reviewers show that several diagnostics do not cleanly isolate spatiotemporal binding—some items are solvable without video or from a single frame—and question whether unannotated actions guarantee false distractors.

8Sd5WKVtuH.one_liner: Refines base time-series forecasts by shifting encoded latent states along displacements toward history-predicted future states before residual-adjusted decoding.
8Sd5WKVtuH.problem: Future states predicted directly from encoded history can lie farther from the target representation than an encoded base forecast—a phenomenon termed Predicted State Deviation—making direct latent decoding suboptimal.
8Sd5WKVtuH.method: FUSE encodes a frozen backbone's observation-space base forecast into a latent base state while predicting a future latent state from encoded history, then learns scalar weights to move the base state along or against the displacement vector toward the predicted state. The refined state is decoded back to observation space and combined with an adjusted reconstruction residual without modifying or retraining the forecasting backbone.
8Sd5WKVtuH.key_idea: Shift an encoded base forecast along the latent displacement toward a history-predicted future state and decode with an adjusted reconstruction residual rather than decoding the predicted state directly.
8Sd5WKVtuH.evidence: Evaluated across eight multivariate time-series benchmarks with three backbones (MLP, DLinear, iTransformer) and two frozen foundation models on four ETT datasets, with geometric and decomposition ablations.
8Sd5WKVtuH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using imperfect predicted future states as directional guidance via a lightweight plug-in without retraining the base forecaster is simple, intuitive, and yields consistent gains across backbones.
8Sd5WKVtuH.main_concern: Reviewers note missing citations and baselines from JEPA-style latent forecasting, reliance on global input-shared scalar weights, potential test-set leakage in lookback length selection, and dependence of Predicted State Deviation on autoencoder design.

OiLkn57DoS.one_liner: Benchmarks mobile agents on 122 CLI and hybrid GUI-CLI tasks and pairs verification with continual experience learning in MobiMux.
OiLkn57DoS.problem: Mobile device agents are predominantly built and evaluated for GUI-only interaction, overlooking command-line execution and struggling to coordinate hybrid GUI-CLI workflows.
OiLkn57DoS.method: The authors build MobiCLI, a benchmark of 122 tasks across 18 mobile applications spanning batch operations, file management, computational tasks, data processing, and system operations under CLI and hybrid GUI-CLI settings. They also introduce MobiMux, a mobile agent framework combining task verification with continual experience learning to improve hybrid GUI-CLI execution.
OiLkn57DoS.key_idea: Evaluate mobile agents across CLI and hybrid GUI-CLI tasks while augmenting hybrid agent execution with task verification and continual experience learning.
OiLkn57DoS.evidence: Evaluates general-purpose models and phone-use agents (eight models tested) across 122 tasks and 18 applications in a controlled mobile environment.
OiLkn57DoS.claimed_gains: On MobiCLI the best evaluated model achieves 55.7% success, while MobiMux improves success rates by up to 16.4 percentage points on general-purpose models.
OiLkn57DoS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating shell and hybrid GUI-CLI workflows on mobile devices is well motivated and clearly demonstrates efficiency and capability gains from adding CLI access.
OiLkn57DoS.main_concern: Reviewers note that hybrid tasks do not strictly exclude GUI-only solutions or match task complexity against CLI tasks, obscuring whether lower scores stem from GUI-CLI coordination or task difficulty, alongside unclear training-template overlap in MobiMux.

e2iACCguyD.one_liner: Accelerates diffusion sampling without training by recursively forecasting features via a damped level-trend state inspired by Holt's exponential smoothing.
e2iACCguyD.problem: At high diffusion-sampling acceleration ratios, sparse full-network evaluations make cache-then-forecast feature predictors sensitive to local extrapolation errors.
e2iACCguyD.method: HoltSeer is a training-free cache-then-forecast diffusion accelerator that maintains a smoothed level-trend state—tracking recent cached feature levels, local directional trends, and a trend-scaling damping coefficient—updated across a bounded sequence of recursive forecasts between periodic full network evaluations.
e2iACCguyD.key_idea: Forecast skipped diffusion features via bounded recursive updates of a damped Holt-style level-trend state shared across computed and predicted timesteps.
e2iACCguyD.evidence: Evaluated on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, and Wan2.1 against feature-caching baselines including TeaCache, TC-Padé, and TaylorSeer at large cache intervals.
e2iACCguyD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that HoltSeer is a simple, training-free method that improves generation fidelity over compared caching baselines under high acceleration ratios at matched computation.
e2iACCguyD.main_concern: Reviewers point out that when K=2 the smoothing parameters cancel out into simple damped two-point extrapolation—which outperforms K=3 on FLUX.1-dev—leaving the incremental benefit of exponential smoothing unverified alongside limited baselines.

PfK3qLzHf5.one_liner: Represents dynamical operators as decay-time-ordered nested subspaces (flags) and compares realizations using a gauge-invariant chordal metric.
PfK3qLzHf5.problem: Comparing spectral or modal decompositions of spatiotemporal dynamical systems with Euclidean distances is sensitive to arbitrary basis choices, whereas single-subspace Grassmann distances discard the hierarchy of decay timescales.
PfK3qLzHf5.method: Each dynamical realization is represented as a flag—a nested sequence of subspaces constructed by grouping dynamical modes by spectral modulus and ordering them by decay time—and compared via a gauge-invariant chordal flag distance. The authors prove this distance defines a metric admitting an isometric Euclidean embedding for kernel methods and remains stable under operator perturbations away from decay-time crossings.
PfK3qLzHf5.key_idea: Represent modal decompositions as persistence-ordered flags of nested subspaces grouped by spectral modulus and compare them with a gauge-invariant chordal distance admitting an isometric Euclidean embedding.
