PfK3qLzHf5.evidence: Supported by metric, Euclidean-embedding, and perturbation-stability proofs, synthetic ensemble experiments with decay-time reordering and observation noise, and evaluation on 216 realizations from four CMIP6 climate models and a reanalysis across three variables.
PfK3qLzHf5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using persistence-ordered flags with a chordal metric resolves the trade-off between basis invariance and preserving dynamical timescale hierarchies, backed by clean theoretical properties.
PfK3qLzHf5.main_concern: Reviewers question the scientific motivation of the CMIP6 climate experiments (recovering already-known source model clusters via silhouette scores), note sensitivity to observation noise, and request stronger baselines such as SGOT.

5kZj6Y0Wdt.one_liner: Derives sharp minimax cumulative-loss rates for online threshold learning under probabilistic true-label audits and adversarial past-prediction replay.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.problem: Reusing a model's past predictions as future training labels couples current prediction accuracy with the informativeness of future supervision, creating error accumulation whose minimax limits under partial auditing were unknown.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.method: The authors study online learning over K thresholds with horizon T <= K^(1/2 - epsilon), where after an initial truthful round each label comes from an independent audit with probability rho or from an adversary-selected past predictor otherwise. Using two-clock lower bounds and matching algorithms, they characterize sharp minimax cumulative loss rates across audit probabilities, bounded replay recency, and full or noisy provenance/audit disclosures.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.key_idea: Characterize tight minimax loss rates via two-clock lower bounds and exploration-preserving online learners when labels alternate between probabilistic true-label audits and adversary-selected past predictions.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.evidence: Theoretical minimax upper and lower bounds over K thresholds for proper and improper online learners across varying audit rates, replay recency constraints, and label-provenance disclosure settings.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.claimed_gains: For horizons T <= K^(1/2-epsilon), establishes minimax cumulative loss Theta_epsilon(min{T, T^(2/3)(log K)^(1/3)}) at audit probability rho=1/2, reducing to Theta(min{T, (log K)/rho}) under sufficiently recent replay or audit/source disclosure, whereas fixing p_1=1/2 with revealed source and hidden audit status raises long-horizon loss from Theta((log K)/rho) to Theta((log K)/rho^2).
5kZj6Y0Wdt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the stochastic replay adversary model is an interesting theoretical formulation for self-generated supervision, yielding surprising tight minimax rates and insights into label provenance.
5kZj6Y0Wdt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize dense, hard-to-penetrate exposition backed by a 70-page appendix with little intuition, no empirical simulations, and strong adversarial assumptions restricted to horizons T <= K^(1/2-epsilon).

JUFrvh2NnS.one_liner: Synthesizes and edits outdoor 3D semantic scenes from roadmaps, optional text, and heightmaps using windowed spectral-attention blocks.
JUFrvh2NnS.problem: Outdoor 3D semantic scene generation methods typically depend on dense semantic annotations or rigid conditioning signals that limit scalability and flexible region-specific editing.
JUFrvh2NnS.method: OmniCore conditions outdoor 3D semantic scene synthesis and editing on abstract horizontal roadmaps combined with optional natural language descriptions and vertical heightmaps, integrating multimodal features via a Windowed Spectral-Attention Block (WSAB) that pairs local window attention with scene-adaptive spectral filtering. The authors also build OmniControl-3D by enriching SemanticKITTI, KITTI-360, and nuScenes with paired roadmaps, text descriptions, and heightmaps.
JUFrvh2NnS.key_idea: Combine horizontal roadmaps with optional text and heightmap conditions using windowed spatial attention paired with per-window scene-adaptive spectral filtering for 3D semantic scene synthesis.
JUFrvh2NnS.evidence: Evaluated on the OmniControl-3D benchmark (constructed from SemanticKITTI, KITTI-360, and nuScenes) across conditioning combinations, cross-dataset transfer, synthetic data augmentation, and WSAB ablations.
JUFrvh2NnS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing outdoor 3D scene conditioning into roadmaps plus optional heightmaps and text is practical and that the multi-dataset benchmark and conditioning ablations are informative.
JUFrvh2NnS.main_concern: Reviewers flag incompatible 2D vs. 3D FID baseline numbers drawn from differing evaluation protocols, architectural mismatch in WSAB (non-overlapping windows cannot enforce cross-window continuity), and reliance on ground-truth-derived heightmaps and captions.

9vBPvkA4eS.one_liner: Controls representation drift during MoE continual expert expansion via expectation-preserving reservoir router initialization and first-token-steered self-generated replay.
9vBPvkA4eS.problem: In continual learning via Mixture-of-Experts expansion, adding experts to a shared router alters the softmax denominator and displaces routing weights for earlier tasks even when old experts are frozen.
9vBPvkA4eS.method: CLoRE controls representational drift without storing past data through three mechanisms: reservoir routing, which initializes added experts and router rows to preserve the shared softmax denominator in expectation; concurrent router alignment trained with the language-modeling loss; and self-generated replay, which routes only the first token through an earlier task's experts to generate synthetic replay inputs.
9vBPvkA4eS.key_idea: Initialize added MoE experts and router rows via reservoir routing to preserve the softmax denominator in expectation while aligning the shared router using first-token-steered self-generated replay.
9vBPvkA4eS.evidence: Evaluated on the TRACE continual learning benchmark with two LLMs (including Llama-3.1 and Qwen3) and on an MoE trained from scratch, with router-initialization and drift analyses.
9vBPvkA4eS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing representational drift caused by changes to the shared router's softmax denominator during expert expansion is insightful and that reservoir routing directly targets initialization-induced drift.
9vBPvkA4eS.main_concern: Reviewers highlight protocol contradictions between the main text's data-free self-replay claim and an appendix describing 0.1% original-corpus replay, risk of compounding errors from flawed self-generated replay, and overlap with prior MoE continual-learning methods.

GpBZtJO3oD.one_liner: Compresses autoregressive video KV caches into cluster centers and low-bit residuals using role-specific Key and Value fitting objectives.
GpBZtJO3oD.problem: Historical KV caches in extended autoregressive video generation create growing memory and attention bottlenecks, where aggressive compression degrades quality and full KV reconstruction leaves attention cost unchanged.
GpBZtJO3oD.method: NanoKV compresses frozen-backbone video KV caches by storing shared token content in cluster centers and encoding joint head-channel residuals into low-bit coefficients, fitting Key decoders to preserve downstream block outputs and Value encoders/decoders for faithful quantized reconstruction. An optional NanoKV-Fast variant reuses the compressed coefficients for mixed-dimensional attention without modifying the video backbone.
GpBZtJO3oD.key_idea: Compress video KV caches via token cluster centers and quantized head-channel residuals while fitting Key decoders to preserve block outputs and Value codecs for quantized reconstruction.
GpBZtJO3oD.evidence: Evaluated on three autoregressive video generation backbones (HY-WorldPlay, Matrix-Game 3.5, and LingBot-World 2.0) against KVTC across PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, VBench, compression ratio, and peak GPU memory.
GpBZtJO3oD.claimed_gains: On HY-WorldPlay, NanoKV achieves 26.09x effective KV compression—nearly twice that of KVTC—while improving PSNR by 1.0 dB.
GpBZtJO3oD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that NanoKV delivers substantial, carefully accounted KV memory reductions (including metadata and resident operators) and strong rate-distortion improvements on HY-WorldPlay.
GpBZtJO3oD.main_concern: Reviewers note that Key alignment is omitted on Matrix-Game (where LPIPS and VBench slightly trail KVTC), ablations compare trained Key decoders only against untrained PCA, fitting is backbone-specific, and longer rollout behavior remains untested.

CgWr4X7Eve.one_liner: Reuses pre-trained EEG electrode vectors across heterogeneous layouts via spherical distance-weighted interpolation alongside spatio-temporal and distributionally robust regularization.
CgWr4X7Eve.problem: Accommodating heterogeneous EEG electrode layouts in foundation models does not ensure effective reuse of pre-trained spatial positional knowledge on unseen electrode configurations.
CgWr4X7Eve.method: Analyzing first-order updates of electrode-indexed tables versus shared coordinate generators, the authors propose RADAR centered on Spatial Positional Remapping (SPR), which initializes target electrode encodings by retaining matching pre-trained electrode vectors and computing spherical distance-weighted averages of nearby anchors via backbone-specific interfaces. RADAR further incorporates Spatio-Temporal Regularization (STR) and Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO).
CgWr4X7Eve.key_idea: Initialize target EEG electrode encodings by retaining matching pre-trained electrode anchors and computing spherical distance-weighted averages of nearby anchors across layouts and backbones.
CgWr4X7Eve.evidence: Evaluated across multiple EEG decoding benchmarks and foundation models (including LaBraM, CBraMod, CSBrain, and LUNA) under leave-one-subject-out splits, source-table controls, cross-donor transfer, and coordinate probing.
CgWr4X7Eve.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing layout compatibility from effective spatial-prior reuse is a valuable insight and that spherical distance-weighted remapping of pre-trained electrode embeddings is simple and practical.
CgWr4X7Eve.main_concern: Reviewers argue that experimental confounds—such as replacing overlapping standard electrodes with random vectors in the native LaBraM baseline and bundling unrelated STR/DRO regularizers—prevent cleanly attributing gains to pre-trained spatial knowledge transfer.

HpsK1ZDewj.one_liner: Replays CAD command sequences with a profile-tracking state machine against a feature plan to localize structural divergences before repair.
HpsK1ZDewj.problem: Generated CAD programs can remain executable even after their committed construction geometry diverges from the intended design, making runtime execution feedback insufficient to locate where repair should start.
HpsK1ZDewj.method: TopoRecover replays CAD command sequences through a deterministic state-machine interpreter that records completed profiles and source commands, comparing them against a fixed feature plan to map structural mismatches to responsible command blocks while preserving valid history. An LLM proposes geometry-constrained local edits followed by execution repair, accepting candidates only when verifier replay satisfies the plan and OpenCASCADE produces a valid positive-volume solid.
HpsK1ZDewj.key_idea: Replay CAD command sequences via a deterministic profile-recording state machine against a fixed feature plan to map pre-failure structural mismatches to source commands before local LLM repair.
HpsK1ZDewj.evidence: Evaluated on 347 natural Text2CAD repair inputs with OpenCASCADE solid verification and matched localization studies holding patcher, fallback, validation, and budget limits fixed.
HpsK1ZDewj.claimed_gains: On 347 natural Text2CAD repair inputs, TopoRecover achieves 78.4% plan-conditioned repair success versus 64.3% for the strongest adapted baseline, and topology-based localization improves repair success from 47.6% to 78.4% in a matched localization study.
HpsK1ZDewj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating structural divergence from runtime execution failure via deterministic profile-to-plan localization is clear, inspectable, and well supported by controlled localization ablations.
HpsK1ZDewj.main_concern: Reviewers note that the implemented scope is restricted to simple sketch-and-extrude CAD operations and that broader generalization claims in the paper lack corresponding experimental reports.

xczix7IQA8.one_liner: Compares row-token and cell-token alternating-axis tabular transformers against exact Bayes predictors across controlled sparse-to-dense linear priors.
xczix7IQA8.problem: Released tabular foundation models differ simultaneously in pretraining priors, objectives, and architectures, obscuring why row-token models degrade much more than cell-token alternating-axis models when irrelevant null features are added.
xczix7IQA8.method: The authors construct a controlled family of sparse-to-dense linear priors with fixed second moments and closed-form Bayes-optimal predictors, showing theoretically that sparse prediction requires context-dependent feature gating whereas dense prediction requires only uniform feature weighting. They train streamlined row-token and cell-token alternating-axis transformers identically across these priors and decompose prediction errors relative to the exact Bayes optimum.
xczix7IQA8.key_idea: Train row-token and cell-token alternating-axis transformers under identical sparse-to-dense linear priors with exact Bayes posteriors to test architectural alignment with context-dependent feature gating.
xczix7IQA8.evidence: Exact Bayes analysis, controlled training experiments on sparse-to-dense linear priors, and null-feature evaluations on released tabular foundation models (including TabDPT and TabPFN v2) across synthetic and real-world datasets.
xczix7IQA8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring controlled architectures against an exact Bayes-optimal target across fixed-moment sparse-to-dense priors cleanly decomposes prediction error and addresses a relevant tabular architecture question.
xczix7IQA8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the two trained models simultaneously differ in tokenization, feature attention, depth (5 vs. 3 blocks), and compute—with row-token seeds hitting step caps—so feature-axis ablations and matched-compute controls are needed to rule out under-training.

zAiMJorstl.one_liner: SAGE-RAG selects budgeted evidence using graph-based trust propagation and relational consistency.
zAiMJorstl.problem: Coordinated poisoning can make individually plausible retrieved passages reinforce misleading claims that overwhelm benign evidence in retrieval-augmented generation.
zAiMJorstl.method: SAGE-RAG builds an evidence graph of retrieved claims and their relations. Attack-Aware Trust Propagation calibrates claim trust from coordination patterns, while Maximum Consistent Reasoning Subgraph selection chooses claims under a token budget using utility, trust, and consistency.
zAiMJorstl.key_idea: Calibrate claim trust from graph coordination, then jointly select a token-budgeted subgraph that penalizes low trust and contradictions.
zAiMJorstl.evidence: An 8,000-sample benchmark covers four QA datasets, four attack types, and ten evaluated systems, with attack absorption and exact match as metrics.
zAiMJorstl.claimed_gains: SAGE-RAG reduces attack absorption from 0.338 with BM25 to 0.150 and achieves the highest exact-match score among ten evaluated systems.
zAiMJorstl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling relations among claims addresses a meaningful RAG failure mode and that the two modules form a sensible defense.
zAiMJorstl.main_concern: The ablations do not adequately isolate or justify AATP and MCRS, leaving their necessity, heuristic assumptions, and parameter sensitivity unclear.

QEI9S25Ec2.one_liner: InfiLoop preserves recurrent reasoning states through content-weighted, temporally decayed attention residuals.
QEI9S25Ec2.problem: Looped Transformers can lose correct intermediate deductions as added iterations overwrite recurrent states with noisy updates.
QEI9S25Ec2.method: InfiLoop maintains a running summary of recurrent states using content-based weighting and learned temporal decay. An exact streaming recurrence keeps aggregation memory constant as loop count grows while adaptively accepting new updates.
QEI9S25Ec2.key_idea: Aggregate past recurrent states with content-dependent attention and temporal decay instead of replacing the state with each loop output.
QEI9S25Ec2.evidence: Reasoning experiments include Sudoku-Extreme and ARC-AGI-2, with depth-scaling, ablation, and state-perturbation analyses supporting the mechanism.
QEI9S25Ec2.claimed_gains: A 7M-parameter InfiLoop model reaches 97.9% exact accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme and 13.6% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-2, with test-time looping beyond 20,000 effective steps on Sudoku-Extreme.
QEI9S25Ec2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the residual mechanism is simple, memory-efficient, and directed at a meaningful recurrent-reasoning failure.
QEI9S25Ec2.main_concern: Comparisons with simpler learned gates and the closest recursive architectures do not establish the specific benefit of the proposed history-dependent aggregation.

zyxg380KrE.one_liner: AIMPACT separates presentation evidence collection from rubric-conditioned multi-expert judgment.
zyxg380KrE.problem: Directly mapping heterogeneous multimodal observations to presentation scores conflates unreliable evidence with rubric-based judgment.
zyxg380KrE.method: AIMPACT's EJMA hierarchy builds traceable evidence memory and coordinates seven specialist agents through a reliability-guided collaboration graph. RC-MEPO then learns expert corrections to the council prior and applies on-policy preference optimization with confidence-weighted expert scores and rubric perturbations.
zyxg380KrE.key_idea: Separate traceable multimodal evidence from scoring, then correct a specialist-agent council using confidence-weighted expert preferences.
zyxg380KrE.evidence: The authors construct the MEPA multi-expert presentation assessment dataset and evaluate the framework across presentation dimensions with individual expert scores, confidence ratings, and feedback.
zyxg380KrE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating evidence from judgment is useful and that MEPA's multi-expert annotations address a practical assessment need.
zyxg380KrE.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate gains from multi-agent collaboration against those from structured features, expert supervision, and target-domain fine-tuning.

LdeoEneaYR.one_liner: CasEm guides full-state neural rollouts with independently evolving low-dimensional physical aggregates.
LdeoEneaYR.problem: Autoregressive neural emulators can drift or diverge during long rollouts despite accurate short-term forecasts.
LdeoEneaYR.method: CasEm adds a one-way subsystem that independently predicts physically specified aggregates and corrects a full-state backbone without receiving backbone feedback. A finite-horizon error bound and empirical diagnostics guide subsystem selection.
LdeoEneaYR.key_idea: Let an independent aggregate subsystem correct full-state rollouts through one-way guidance, preventing backbone errors from feeding back into the subsystem.
LdeoEneaYR.evidence: Experiments cover four ODE/PDE benchmarks, diffusion tasks with Fourier neural operator backbones, and global climate emulation with ACE and Spherical DYffusion.
LdeoEneaYR.claimed_gains: CasEm reduces 10-year full-state time-mean error by 66.6% and 46.3% for frozen ACE and Spherical DYffusion backbones, respectively, while adding less than 3% to inference time.
LdeoEneaYR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the predictor-corrector design is simple, inexpensive, and compatible with existing emulators for long-horizon stability.
LdeoEneaYR.main_concern: Aggregate subsystem selection remains highly case-dependent, and the baselines do not fully establish that gains exceed simpler climatology-based references.

3NMGV5gAEg.one_liner: LUCID extracts compact DNF policy rules and separately audits fidelity, factor alignment, and causal efficacy.
3NMGV5gAEg.problem: Rule-surrogate fidelity alone does not show whether extracted RL concepts align with environment factors or causally influence the policy.
3NMGV5gAEg.method: LUCID jointly trains a sparse autoencoder, learnable binarization bottleneck, and product t-norm logic layer on frozen policy features before extracting DNF rules. It audits rule concepts through simulator-factor alignment and interventions on the frozen teacher.
3NMGV5gAEg.key_idea: Jointly train sparse features, binarization, and logic for DNF extraction, then evaluate concept alignment and causal effect separately from action fidelity.
3NMGV5gAEg.evidence: Five discrete-action vision tasks from MiniGrid to Pong and Boxing support comparisons with decision trees, extraction controls, factor-alignment audits, and causal interventions.
3NMGV5gAEg.claimed_gains: The rules agree with the PPO teacher on 96.8–100% of states and need about 2× fewer feature tests than matched-fidelity decision trees on gridworlds and 28–46× fewer on Atari.
3NMGV5gAEg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating concepts beyond fidelity is worthwhile and that joint training and the audit controls strengthen the study.
3NMGV5gAEg.main_concern: Five discrete-action environments with a single PPO teacher provide limited support for broad claims about vision-based RL concepts.

pD2TCZ6Zsq.one_liner: Reduces cross-entity interference in fixed-size recurrent models by hashing entity IDs into read and write addresses.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.problem: Fixed-size recurrent models suffer accuracy collapse as the number of concurrently tracked entities grows, even when sequence length is short.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.method: Entity-Conditioned Addressing (ECA-Hash) generates deterministic random keys from entity identifiers without a trainable entity table and injects them into the recurrent state's read and write addresses, preserving constant state size.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.key_idea: Injects deterministic random hash keys derived from entity IDs into recurrent read and write addresses to separate concurrent entity states.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.evidence: Evaluated on controlled entity-state benchmarks, an independent security grammar, and a Windows endpoint state probe across Mamba-1/2/3, Naju, and Gated DeltaNet.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.claimed_gains: Raises 16-entity tracking accuracy from <=0.20 to 0.87 (Mamba-2) and 0.98 (Gated DeltaNet), and improves endpoint state probe accuracy from 0.714-0.726 to 0.936-0.984.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper cleanly isolates cross-entity interference and provides convincing matched-input versus address-injection ablations across five backbones.
pD2TCZ6Zsq.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over classical random-key associative memories and narrow real-world utility outside routing-bound state-tracking probes.

KpUbdBhfy4.one_liner: In-context tabular foundation model for survival analysis pretrained on synthetic proportional-odds data with quantile regression.
KpUbdBhfy4.problem: Existing tabular foundation models fail to beat the classical Cox model on small clinical survival datasets.
KpUbdBhfy4.method: SurvICL pretrains a TabICLv2-based architecture on synthetic datasets from a proportional-odds prior, using censored context and uncensored synthetic event times with a quantile regression loss, alongside a 103-dataset benchmark.
KpUbdBhfy4.key_idea: Pretrains an in-context tabular model on synthetic proportional-odds survival data using uncensored latent event times for quantile regression.
KpUbdBhfy4.evidence: Evaluated on 63 held-out datasets from a 103-dataset survival benchmark against 20 tree-based, deep, and foundation-model baselines.
KpUbdBhfy4.claimed_gains: Wins 82.9% of pairwise integrated Brier score comparisons on 63 held-out datasets without tuning, versus 71.3% for the runner-up Cox model.
KpUbdBhfy4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that outperforming the Cox model on small clinical cohorts without tuning and releasing a 103-dataset benchmark are practically valuable.
KpUbdBhfy4.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in combining existing components (TabICLv2, pinball loss, latent-time supervision) without isolating their contributions or analyzing synthetic-to-real shift.

SlG49nGglA.one_liner: Asynchronous proactive agent separating a continuous intervention-timing model from a response and physical-action model.
SlG49nGglA.problem: Physical AI systems typically wait for explicit instructions instead of continuously monitoring world states to act proactively.
SlG49nGglA.method: ProAgent pairs a Proactive Timing Model (trained on video-derived causal timing supervision) that decides when to intervene with a Response Model that speaks or invokes physical device actions asynchronously.
SlG49nGglA.key_idea: Decouples continuous causal intervention-timing prediction from asynchronous text generation and physical action execution.
SlG49nGglA.evidence: Evaluated on streaming video benchmarks and 60 real-robot scenarios.
SlG49nGglA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the asynchronous separation of timing from response generation is coherent and shows strong matched-baseline gains on video benchmarks.
SlG49nGglA.main_concern: Reviewers find the real-robot evaluation lacks matched baselines and controls, and note methodological overlap with prior proactive streaming agents like Dispider and StreamMind.

QfaLbsM5I7.one_liner: Derives asymmetric-bandwidth AllReduce lower bounds and designs a four-stage pipelined schedule approaching fault-free speed.
QfaLbsM5I7.problem: A single server with degraded NIC bandwidth bottlenecks standard Ring AllReduce across an entire GPU cluster.
QfaLbsM5I7.method: The authors prove an information-theoretic lower bound showing O(1/p) overhead when a straggler keeps at least half its bandwidth, and design OptCC, a four-stage pipelined AllReduce that overlaps straggler transfers with the healthy ring.
QfaLbsM5I7.key_idea: Overlaps reduced-volume straggler transfers on separate links with a healthy-node ring in a four-stage pipelined AllReduce schedule.
QfaLbsM5I7.evidence: Supported by theoretical lower-bound proofs and SimAI cluster simulations.
QfaLbsM5I7.claimed_gains: In SimAI simulations with up to 50% bandwidth loss, OptCC completes AllReduce within 2-6% of fault-free NCCL ring performance, compared to up to 57% overhead for SOTA.
QfaLbsM5I7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical lower bound and the insight to offload volume from degraded links in a pipelined schedule are sound and practical.
QfaLbsM5I7.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of real-GPU testbed validation (simulation-only) and request clearer justification of NIC flow-multiplexing assumptions and ForestColl comparisons.

qmu7nQctdZ.one_liner: Multi-agent benchmark of 51 expert agents and 2,766 dependency-tracked tasks diagnosing where interdependent collaboration fails.
qmu7nQctdZ.problem: Outcome-only benchmarks cannot pinpoint whether multi-agent systems fail at expert selection, orchestration, transfer, or integration.
qmu7nQctdZ.method: MAScope builds 2,766 tasks across 51 Stack Exchange expert agents with verifiable work dependencies, tracking each required contribution into the final answer across four collaboration stages.
qmu7nQctdZ.key_idea: Traces indispensable, verifiable agent contributions through four collaboration stages to isolate where interdependent multi-agent workflows lose performance.
qmu7nQctdZ.evidence: Evaluated 12 representative multi-agent methods across 2,766 tasks with dependency-bypass and rescoring checks.
qmu7nQctdZ.claimed_gains: Success drops by 48% once work becomes interdependent, over 3x the drop of a no-collaboration single agent.
qmu7nQctdZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MAScope offers a valuable, traceable benchmark across 12 MAS frameworks that diagnoses collaboration bottlenecks.
qmu7nQctdZ.main_concern: Reviewers warn that keyword/identifier matching checks content presence rather than reasoning correctness, and that qualitative trajectory analysis is underspecified.

rH77LCJMAG.one_liner: Controlled multilingual study of 123 LMs and 54 tokenizers showing tokenizer sensitivity concentrates in lower-resource languages.
rH77LCJMAG.problem: Prior work leaves unclear which languages are most sensitive to tokenizer choices and how tokenizer-training allocations affect them.
rH77LCJMAG.method: The authors train 123 language models across 54 tokenizers and 31 languages with fixed architecture and training setup, analyzing bits-per-byte variance against training-data share and tokenizer weighting.
rH77LCJMAG.key_idea: Holds model architecture and training fixed across 54 tokenizers to measure per-language bits-per-byte sensitivity as a function of data share.
rH77LCJMAG.evidence: Trained 123 language models spanning 54 tokenizers and 31 languages.
rH77LCJMAG.claimed_gains: BPB standard deviation increases as training-data share decreases (Spearman rho = -0.52 over 31 languages and -0.69 over 28 with word boundaries).
rH77LCJMAG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large controlled sweep across 123 models, 54 tokenizers, and 31 languages provides useful per-language empirical insights.
rH77LCJMAG.main_concern: Reviewers note small model/budget scale, high run-to-run variance with non-significant linear fits, and limited novelty beyond prior multilingual tokenizer studies.

3GVTsHA2Qy.one_liner: Organizes user history into a provenance-linked memory pyramid and trains an LLM via RL to navigate memory tools.
3GVTsHA2Qy.problem: Exposing long-term user memory only as passively retrieved context limits an agent's control over when and how to consult history.
3GVTsHA2Qy.method: NapMem structures user histories into a four-level pyramid (raw conversations, typed records, topic tracks, profiles) with provenance links exposed as tools, and trains a 9B agent with RL over memory-tool trajectories.
3GVTsHA2Qy.key_idea: Exposes a provenance-linked multi-granularity memory pyramid as tools and optimizes an RL navigation policy over memory-access trajectories.
3GVTsHA2Qy.evidence: Evaluations on PersonaMem-v2, LongMemEval, and LoCoMo, plus non-memory reasoning tasks and component ablations.
3GVTsHA2Qy.claimed_gains: A 9B NapMem agent achieves the highest average score among evaluated systems, outperforming a 397B variant without memory-navigation training.
3GVTsHA2Qy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hierarchical provenance-linked memory interface is practical and achieves strong empirical results across multiple memory benchmarks.
3GVTsHA2Qy.main_concern: Evaluation splits and subset sizes raise generalization and leakage concerns, memory writing/maintenance is not trained, and performance drops on adversarial/unanswerable LoCoMo queries.

B2AQldg6rd.one_liner: Proposes AnchorGen, training an unconditional joint shape-sketch rectified flow and anchoring the sketch latent during inference-time physics optimization.
B2AQldg6rd.problem: Generative shape priors used during physics-based 3D design optimization ignore initial 2D sketches and drift toward high-density training modes.
B2AQldg6rd.method: AnchorGen trains an unconditional rectified flow on concatenated shape and sketch latents; at inference, gradient descent optimizes the shape latent against a differentiable drag surrogate while a token-wise cosine penalty anchors the sketch latent.
B2AQldg6rd.key_idea: Trains an unconditional joint shape-sketch flow and constrains the sketch latent via token-wise cosine similarity during physics optimization.
B2AQldg6rd.evidence: Evaluated on ShapeNet and 600 DrivAerNet++ source-target pairs for aerodynamic drag optimization, dimensional edits, and sketch synthesis.
B2AQldg6rd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate incorporating 2D sketch constraints into physics-driven 3D shape optimization via unconditional joint flow matching.
B2AQldg6rd.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to synthetic car sketches and aerodynamic drag optimization, leaving generalization to freehand user sketches, other categories, and other physics objectives unvalidated.

r8b6Dt5B3H.one_liner: Proposes WEIRDO, estimating Doob's h-transform diffusion guidance via a bias-free weak residual penalty of the space-time harmonicity PDE.
r8b6Dt5B3H.problem: Estimating Doob's h-function drift for tilting pretrained diffusion models toward a target distribution lacks non-asymptotic convergence guarantees without smoothness assumptions.
r8b6Dt5B3H.method: WEIRDO minimizes a penalized least-squares risk whose regularizer is the dual Sobolev norm of the space-time harmonicity PDE residual, which vanishes at the true h-function.
r8b6Dt5B3H.key_idea: Regularizes Doob's h-transform least-squares estimation with a dual-Sobolev weak residual of the space-time harmonicity PDE.
r8b6Dt5B3H.evidence: High-probability L2 guidance error convergence-rate proofs under exact pretrained scores and compact support, plus small-scale empirical tests.
r8b6Dt5B3H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous statistical analysis of Doob's h-transform estimation using a bias-free weak residual PDE penalty.
r8b6Dt5B3H.main_concern: Convergence guarantees assume an exact pretrained score and compact support without score-error propagation analysis, and empirical validation is small-scale.

fc2gWLWd7p.one_liner: Trains an environment-conditioned actor-critic once to generate Whittle indices in real time as restless bandit environments change.
fc2gWLWd7p.problem: Constantly changing environments in restless multi-armed bandit problems force repeated recomputation of Whittle indices, incurring high computational complexity.
fc2gWLWd7p.method: The authors introduce an environment parameter-driven neural network trained once via a Whittle Actor-Critic (WAC) pipeline. Given an estimated or encoded environment parameter, the network outputs Whittle indices in a single forward pass.
fc2gWLWd7p.key_idea: Condition a single neural index network on environment parameters or learned environment embeddings and train it with an actor-critic pipeline using threshold policies.
fc2gWLWd7p.evidence: Numerical simulations across RMAB settings including wireless scheduling, model-size ablations, and theoretical analysis of local minima in Theorem 4.1 support the approach.
fc2gWLWd7p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning on environment representations enables real-time index generation and outperforms DeepTOP and WQL on index error and control cost across model sizes.
fc2gWLWd7p.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological novelty over applying domain randomization to DeepTOP and note limitations in the non-indexable resource-constraint proof and simple two-parameter simulations.

6mtliTEfQi.one_liner: Embeds games into an oracle atlas by induced solver dynamics and trains a payoff-based model to locate unseen games.
6mtliTEfQi.problem: Analytical game taxonomies such as potential, zero-sum, or monotone classes do not reliably predict realized solver dynamics or finite-time behavior.
6mtliTEfQi.method: The authors construct behavioural cartography, placing games with similar dynamics across gradient, optimistic/extragradient, and fictitious-play solvers nearby in an oracle atlas, then train a payoff-based model invariant to action relabeling and player exchange.
6mtliTEfQi.key_idea: Organize game representations directly by empirical learning dynamics across diverse solver primitives rather than analytical payoff structure.
6mtliTEfQi.evidence: Empirical evaluation across solver families, withheld property prediction (recurrence and reversal), and leave-one-solver-out transfer experiments support the method.
6mtliTEfQi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find representing and grouping games by induced solver behavior rather than structural categories interesting and well evaluated empirically.
6mtliTEfQi.main_concern: Reviewers note that headline results are reported on the dev set rather than a held-out test set, transfer to excluded solvers is uneven, and practical benefits over structural guarantees are unclear.

tMv5dDcgM9.one_liner: Evaluates agent adherence to skill specifications using 96 skill-task pairs and 2,194 constraints across a 9-subcategory taxonomy.
tMv5dDcgM9.problem: Evaluating agents solely on task completion misses whether they follow procedural, deliverable, and restraint requirements specified in reusable skills.
tMv5dDcgM9.method: The authors build SkillIF, pairing 96 curated skills across ten domains with executable tasks and 2,194 constraints organized into a 3-category, 9-subcategory taxonomy, scored via deterministic checks and LLM judges.
tMv5dDcgM9.key_idea: Decompose skill specifications into a shared constraint taxonomy and evaluate execution evidence independently of task completion using deterministic checks and LLM judges.
tMv5dDcgM9.evidence: Experiments across combinations of language models and execution harnesses, plus judge-agreement validation (Kendall tau = 0.745), evaluate adherence versus task completion.
tMv5dDcgM9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating skill adherence from task completion addresses a timely problem with a useful constraint taxonomy and reproducible numerical reporting.
tMv5dDcgM9.main_concern: Reviewers point out that constraints are LLM-extracted without human validation and that injected harness prompts override skill interaction and stopping rules.

6sL9g6gc85.one_liner: Establishes necessary and sufficient conditions and error bounds for exact attribute conversion in autoencoder-based style transfer.
6sL9g6gc85.problem: Autoencoder-based style transfer methods remain largely heuristic and lack theoretical conditions guaranteeing exact attribute conversion while preserving non-target content.
6sL9g6gc85.method: The authors formalize a data-generating process separating a task-relevant factor from a controllable attribute, prove necessary and sufficient conditions for exact conversion, and derive error bounds from reconstruction error and residual dependence.
6sL9g6gc85.key_idea: Replace latent recovery guarantees with synthesis-oriented conditions combining injectivity, distributional asymmetry on content, and Lipschitz error bounds linking reconstruction and independence to transfer quality.
6sL9g6gc85.evidence: Theoretical theorems and lemmas, speech cluster frequency checks in Appendix E, and real-data experiments support the analysis.
6sL9g6gc85.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical analysis of when reconstruction and independence suffice for content-preserving style transfer is rigorous and relevant.
6sL9g6gc85.main_concern: Reviewers question the realism and practical scope of the distributional asymmetry assumption (Assumption 2) and note that prior synthesis theory already covers similar objectives.

V4y67LMtUy.one_liner: Progressively freezes parameter groups during fine-tuning by tracking Jensen-Shannon distance between successive Fisher-value distributions.
V4y67LMtUy.problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods typically select trainable parameters before training using static heuristics rather than tracking changing parameter importance.
V4y67LMtUy.method: FisherAdapTune monitors temporal drift via the Jensen-Shannon distance between successive Fisher-value distributions for each parameter group and freezes stabilized groups using an adaptive threshold, backed by a local Gaussian divergence bound.
V4y67LMtUy.key_idea: Track temporal Jensen-Shannon drift of per-group Fisher information distributions during fine-tuning and freeze groups whose curvature stabilizes.
V4y67LMtUy.evidence: Experiments on VTAB-1k image classification tasks (61.62% macro accuracy vs. 59.97% full fine-tuning in Table 2), four segmentation backbones, and signal ablations support the method.
V4y67LMtUy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find tracking temporal Fisher drift for progressive parameter selection well motivated with clear diagnostics on parameter lifetimes.
V4y67LMtUy.main_concern: Reviewers note limited evaluation scope (primarily VTAB-1k classification), confounded ablations with differing parameter budgets and hyperparameters, and no direct comparison against one-time drift selection.

lGPQa3PLjt.one_liner: Probes hypothetical token reveals on an approximate conditional oracle to sample hidden-forest distributions in sublinear parallel depth.
lGPQa3PLjt.problem: Parallel sampling in masked generative models must discover unknown token dependencies without incurring linear sequential depth or oracle calls.
lGPQa3PLjt.method: For discrete distributions with hidden forest structure accessed via an approximate conditional oracle, the algorithm probes counterfactual reveals and shares masked-state evaluations across dependence tests to identify safe parallel commit batches without full graph recovery. A tunable parameter trades probing cost against irreversible commit rounds.
lGPQa3PLjt.key_idea: Sharing masked-state evaluations across counterfactual reveal probes identifies safe parallel unmasking batches in hidden-forest distributions with sublinear depth and queries.
lGPQa3PLjt.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds under uniform Hellinger oracle error conditions, plus exact-oracle path-graph experiments.
lGPQa3PLjt.claimed_gains: Achieves vanishing TV error with both oracle submissions and sequential depth in O(N^C) for 0 < C < 1 (specifically O(N^2/3) upper bound and O(N^1/3) lower bound).
lGPQa3PLjt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that parallel sampling with dependency discovery in masked models is an important problem and that the O(N^2/3) upper bound and O(N^1/3) lower bound are solid theoretical results.
lGPQa3PLjt.main_concern: Reviewers highlight dense presentation, strong worst-case Hellinger oracle assumptions, and the absence of experiments on trained masked diffusion language models.

PsqBNvnWwe.one_liner: Derives equivariance conditions and finite-sample error bounds for exponential-family variational BNNs trained with data augmentation.
PsqBNvnWwe.problem: While augmented infinite deep ensembles are known to be equivariant, theoretical guarantees for data augmentation in variational Bayesian neural networks are lacking.
PsqBNvnWwe.method: The authors analyze Bayesian neural networks trained with variational inference in the exponential family under data augmentation, deriving conditions for exact equivariance and bounds on equivariance error. They also propose three symmetrization techniques—including orbit expansion—to strengthen augmentation.
PsqBNvnWwe.key_idea: Analyzing exponential-family variational parameters under group-closed priors establishes exact equivariance conditions and error bounds for augmented BNNs.
PsqBNvnWwe.evidence: Theoretical proofs for exponential-family VI and numerical experiments including FashionMNIST with C4 symmetry.
PsqBNvnWwe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical framework characterizing exponential-family variational BNNs under data augmentation is well-motivated and rigorously constructed.
PsqBNvnWwe.main_concern: Reviewers note close overlap with Nordenfors et al. (2025), limited experimental scope (only FashionMNIST with C4, where two of three symmetrization methods fail to beat baseline accuracy), and a technical gap in Theorem 3.

eLg0yy1BYo.one_liner: Combines alpha-barycenter aggregation with derivative calibration and trust-region checks for fast multiobjective f-divergence matching.
eLg0yy1BYo.problem: Optimizing one distribution against many target distributions under f-divergences is computationally expensive when evaluating true objectives.
eLg0yy1BYo.method: CAL-alpha-MODM aggregates targets via local f-divergence alpha-barycenters for cheap predictor queries and applies derivative calibration to match true gradients and Hessians, verified by trust-region acceptance checks. Canonical geometry cancels the leading quadratic error term at common matching for cubic local convergence.
eLg0yy1BYo.key_idea: Aggregating targets into alpha-barycenters with derivative calibration and trust-region checks cuts true-objective evaluations while preserving local convergence order.
eLg0yy1BYo.evidence: Convergence proofs and controlled experiments on synthetic heterogeneous/common targets, 256-target query benchmarks, and low-dimensional solves vs. L-BFGS and Direct-TR.
eLg0yy1BYo.claimed_gains: Achieves 2.46-3.14x end-to-end query speedups at 256 targets and speedups over L-BFGS and Direct-TR.
eLg0yy1BYo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical analysis of calibration and canonical-geometry error cancellation is substantial and well-executed.
eLg0yy1BYo.main_concern: Reviewers note heavy notation that obscures intuition and narrow practical speedup (only 1.10x over Direct-TR at 300 targets in a 2D latent space).

VmxEIuspKD.one_liner: Introduces GEM, a training-free agent memory compressor that preserves task-evidence records first and fills remaining slots via geometric residuals.
VmxEIuspKD.problem: Compressing long-horizon agent histories based solely on geometric redundancy can discard critical next-action task evidence despite preserving global embedding similarity.
VmxEIuspKD.method: The authors propose Geometry Guided Evidence Preserving Memory (GEM), a training-free compressor that protects task and execution evidence using recency, goal similarity, write patterns, and error cues, then uses Modified Gram-Schmidt geometric residual completion to fill the remaining budget.
VmxEIuspKD.key_idea: Protecting execution and task-evidence blocks before running greedy geometric residual completion preserves critical next-action signals that pure subspace coverage misses.
VmxEIuspKD.evidence: Spectral diagnostics, controlled block-replacement experiments, and evaluations on the 260-task WorkBuddyBench measuring token usage and task reward.
VmxEIuspKD.claimed_gains: Evidence-aware selection raises next-action Top-3 retention from 0.31 to 0.69 at 0.98 centroid similarity, and GEM reduces mean token usage from 2.69M to 2.11M (21.4% reduction) with similar mean task reward.
VmxEIuspKD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the concrete demonstration that global geometric coverage can miss next-action evidence and the 21.4% token reduction on WorkBuddyBench.
VmxEIuspKD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether geometric residual completion adds value over simpler heuristic selection rules and note minimal token reduction (1.37M to 1.35M) with slight reward drop on Code tasks.

OF9Goc0Ku2.one_liner: Diagnoses LoRA rank bottlenecks by bounding the local loss gap between dense and low-rank updates within a fixed Frobenius ball.
OF9Goc0Ku2.problem: Comparing raw LoRA and dense fine-tuning runs confounds rank capacity with optimization dynamics and update scale, leaving rank sufficiency unclear.
OF9Goc0Ku2.method: The authors propose a local quadratic diagnostic framework comparing optimal dense and low-rank updates within a fixed Frobenius radius, showing the gap equals the spectral tail of a curvature-whitened gradient when unconstrained optima are feasible, with corrections for boundary optima and approximation errors.
OF9Goc0Ku2.key_idea: Comparing dense and low-rank updates inside a fixed Frobenius ball relates rank-upgrade benefit to newly captured spectral energy of a curvature-whitened gradient.
OF9Goc0Ku2.evidence: Controlled 24-dimensional synthetic objective experiments for interval coverage and RoBERTa experiments on SST-2 and MRPC for rank-upgrade prediction.
OF9Goc0Ku2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper asks an important question in LoRA and cleanly separates rank capacity from update magnitude under a shared norm constraint.
OF9Goc0Ku2.main_concern: Reviewers note that certified interval bounds are never instantiated on neural networks (only synthetic toy functions), neural experiments use a very small radius (R=0.05) on small models, and writing clarity is poor.

zqgzYRgLlb.one_liner: Proves exact interpolation in noiseless high-dimensional regression incurs a Theta(log n / n) minimax risk penalty and persistent SGD deterioration.
zqgzYRgLlb.problem: The statistical cost of exact interpolation in noiseless high-dimensional regression and the trajectory of averaged GD/SGD iterates remain unresolved.
zqgzYRgLlb.method: The authors derive minimax lower bounds for interpolating linear predictors, analyze worst-case GD and fixed-dataset SGD population risk across training horizons, and characterize risk certification bounds from m validation samples.
zqgzYRgLlb.key_idea: Shows that requiring exact interpolation raises minimax risk from Theta(1/n) to Theta(log n / n) while prefix-averaged GD/SGD suffers a persistent Theta(sqrt(n)) risk rebound after T=n.
zqgzYRgLlb.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs for noiseless linear regression, Gaussian mixtures, and realizable quadratics.
zqgzYRgLlb.claimed_gains: Interpolation raises minimax risk from Theta(1/n) to Theta(log n / n); T-point prefix averages hit Theta(log n / n^(3/2)) at T=n before a persistent Theta(sqrt(n)) deterioration to Theta(log n / n); certification scale is Theta(min{log n / n, 1/m}).
zqgzYRgLlb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the rigor of proving the logarithmic interpolation penalty across all linear interpolating estimators.
zqgzYRgLlb.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical significance of a logarithmic factor arising from an artificial discrete worst-case construction, and note the complete absence of numerical experiments.

3ouK4frGSB.one_liner: Detects single-sample OOD inputs in continuous normalizing flows via goodness-of-fit and dependence tests on latent noise.
3ouK4frGSB.problem: Likelihoods from deep generative models are unreliable for OOD detection and suffer from complexity bias.
3ouK4frGSB.method: Signal in the Noise (SITN) maps inputs through a continuous normalizing flow to its latent space and tests whether the latent vector conforms to the standard normal prior using Anderson-Darling normality and spectral dependence statistics, without requiring OOD training data.
3ouK4frGSB.key_idea: Applies single-sample goodness-of-fit normality and spectral dependence tests to continuous normalizing flow latents rather than relying on likelihood values.
3ouK4frGSB.evidence: Evaluations on standard image OOD benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR-10 vs. SVHN, CIFAR-10-C) and synthetic perturbations, plus statistic ablations.
3ouK4frGSB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SITN is simple, OOD-data-free, avoids image complexity bias, and achieves strong empirical AUROC.
3ouK4frGSB.main_concern: Reviewers identify mathematical errors in the statistical guarantee proofs, limited novelty over prior latent goodness-of-fit tests, and restriction to continuous normalizing flows.

RqSEg3ArpB.one_liner: Pretrains a gene-resolution masked autoencoder on frozen protein embeddings with contig-boundary and relative-strand attention.
RqSEg3ArpB.problem: Genomic-context models must distinguish true biological gene relationships from arbitrary assembly contig orderings and reference-dependent strand labels.
RqSEg3ArpB.method: VenusGenome encodes visible-only gene protein embeddings with high-ratio masking and genome-aware attention that blocks cross-contig attention and encodes relative strand orientation and gene positions, pretrained on 1.7M+ prokaryotic assemblies.
RqSEg3ArpB.key_idea: Applies visible-only masked autoencoding over gene protein embeddings with attention restricted within contigs and biased by relative strand orientation.
RqSEg3ArpB.evidence: Pretrained on over 1.7 million prokaryotic assemblies and evaluated on 11 genome-level phenotype and gene-level tasks (BGC, operon, PPI) plus fitness-defect perturbations.
RqSEg3ArpB.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest mean performance among evaluated models on nine of eleven primary metrics.
RqSEg3ArpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the assembly-aware attention (contig blocking and relative strand) and disciplined probing protocol.
RqSEg3ArpB.main_concern: Reviewers flag capacity-mismatched baselines (1B vs. 26M BacFormer), missing gLM2/ESM2-only ablations, and potential confounding in BGC/STRING labels.

U7m8AwSg9Z.one_liner: Trains separate human-object and human-scene motion priors and composes them at inference via diffusion noise optimization.
U7m8AwSg9Z.problem: Scarcity of paired human-object-scene interaction (HOSI) data limits motion generation models that need both accurate hand-object contact and scene compatibility.
U7m8AwSg9Z.method: PriorHOSI learns HOIPrior and HSIPrior separately on abundant HOI and HSI data. At inference, HSIPrior proposes scene-adapted human targets (with body-part-aware residual refinement) that guide joint body-object diffusion noise optimization through a consistency-distilled HOIPrior under hand-in-object-frame constraints.
U7m8AwSg9Z.key_idea: Composes separately trained HOI and HSI diffusion priors at inference using diffusion noise optimization with hand-contact constraints in the object frame.
U7m8AwSg9Z.evidence: Evaluated on 469 InfBaGel benchmark tasks with component ablations.
U7m8AwSg9Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separate HOI/HSI prior composition is a well-motivated solution to HOSI data scarcity that improves both contact and scene penetration.
U7m8AwSg9Z.main_concern: Reviewers note high inference cost (150 DNO iterations), missing DNO-on-InfBaGel baseline controls, and a discrepancy between the paper's objective and extra metric-aligned loss terms in the code.

BnqJcRBl9D.one_liner: Caps per-layer MoE expert loading during speculative verification by keeping only the top-B routing-probability experts.
BnqJcRBl9D.problem: In MoE speculative decoding, verifying many candidate tokens activates the union of their routed experts, approaching full-model cost.
BnqJcRBl9D.method: MoE-Spec is a training-free method that aggregates router probabilities across all candidate tokens in a verification tree and loads only the top-B experts per layer, trading quality for throughput via budget B.
BnqJcRBl9D.key_idea: Aggregates routing probabilities across speculative draft-tree tokens and restricts verification to the top-B experts per layer.
BnqJcRBl9D.evidence: Evaluated on OLMoE-1B-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, and Mixtral-8x7B across reasoning, code generation, and summarization against EAGLE.
BnqJcRBl9D.claimed_gains: Improves throughput by 15–45% over EAGLE while retaining >=90% of autoregressive quality at aggressive budgets, and matches EAGLE quality at conservative budgets.
BnqJcRBl9D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the "expert explosion" bottleneck in MoE tree verification as real and appreciate the simple, training-free budget control.
BnqJcRBl9D.main_concern: Reviewers note missing lossy/static-pruning baselines, untuned EAGLE tree sizes, single-request-only evaluation on 80-sample benchmarks, and post-hoc test-set budget selection.

wqokSvnBVo.one_liner: Discovers cyclic motion symbols and rules from continuous control via spectral initialization, dynamics modeling, and inductive abductive learning.
wqokSvnBVo.problem: Jointly discovering continuous latent factors, symbol value boundaries, and temporal rules from continuous-control trajectories creates a coupled optimization problem.
wqokSvnBVo.method: DynaAbd uses three progressive stages: contrastive spectral initialization and one-step dynamics modeling separate motion into a cyclic Driver and Dependent response, followed by inductive abductive learning (with Prolog) and alternating gradient optimization to refine rules and symbol boundaries.
wqokSvnBVo.key_idea: Decomposes continuous trajectories into a cyclic Driver and Dependent via spectral initialization and refines discrete symbols and rules using progressive inductive abductive learning.
wqokSvnBVo.evidence: Evaluated on polar motion systems and MuJoCo locomotion tasks against VQ-VAE and autoencoder baselines.
wqokSvnBVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the three-stage decomposition that makes joint factor, boundary, and rule learning tractable.
wqokSvnBVo.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the restrictive cyclic-motion assumptions and tiny hard-coded rule space (30 programs), and note inconclusive MuJoCo RL gains overlapping with raw/autoencoder baselines.

TXG8geevv1.one_liner: Contrasts trigger-present and trigger-absent proxy models trained on identical targets to isolate backdoor trigger parameters for purification.
TXG8geevv1.problem: Proxy-based LLM backdoor purification mixes trigger-conditioned and target-learning parameter changes, making defense unstable across different targets.
TXG8geevv1.method: Trigger Isolation (T-ISO) trains two proxy models on the exact same prompts and targets, differing only in whether the proxy trigger is present, and contrasts their parameter updates to isolate trigger-conditioned changes for suppression and recovery.
TXG8geevv1.key_idea: Subtracts parameter updates of a clean-prompt proxy from a triggered-prompt proxy trained on identical targets to cancel target-learning effects and isolate trigger weights.
TXG8geevv1.evidence: Supported by controlled target-sensitivity experiments, first-order cancellation analysis, and evaluations across multiple LLMs, attacks, and targets.
TXG8geevv1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experiments diagnosing target sensitivity and the clean matched-target proxy contrast.
TXG8geevv1.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a missing recovery-only baseline (proxy-triggered recovery without T-ISO suppression) in Table 3, high 50% poisoning ratios, and missing comparisons to CROW/LETHE.

2vjbWZLQJ0.one_liner: Benchmarks accuracy, latency, and energy across 1,656 agentic workflow configurations spanning seven architectures and nine benchmark levels.
2vjbWZLQJ0.problem: Agentic design choices such as call frequency, orchestration, and tool integration cause wide latency and energy disparities at similar accuracy.
2vjbWZLQJ0.method: The authors construct and profile 1,656 agentic configurations across seven architectures, nine benchmark/level pairs, RAG settings, and GPU placements, analyzing component breakdowns, tail latency, and synchronization slack.
2vjbWZLQJ0.key_idea: Profiles end-to-end accuracy, latency, and energy Pareto frontiers across 1,656 agentic workflow configurations to expose orchestrator and retrieval bottlenecks.
2vjbWZLQJ0.evidence: Measured 1,656 systems (including 356 multi-turn and 432 RAG configurations plus 26,000+ GPU assignments) across nine benchmark/level combinations.
2vjbWZLQJ0.claimed_gains: Iso-accurate configurations differ by as much as 238 s and 1,013x in latency, or 177.8 kJ and 1,153x in energy per task.
2vjbWZLQJ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the large-scale joint evaluation of accuracy, latency, and energy across 1,656 configurations and the practical per-agent and retrieval bottleneck breakdowns.
2vjbWZLQJ0.main_concern: All four reviewers flag that Multi-Turn AgentChat cascades terminate early using ground-truth benchmark answers (oracle pass@k), confounding their efficiency advantage against non-oracle baselines.

PkLAt2VOY3.one_liner: Couples an LLM-feedback-trained catalog reorganizer with GRPO post-training for in-context small-merchant product search.
PkLAt2VOY3.problem: Full-catalog prompting in long-context LLMs suffers from non-uniform context utilization, degrading product selection accuracy for small merchants.
PkLAt2VOY3.method: RPTune trains an encoder-reorganizer curator to prune and order catalog items using downstream LLM feedback, then post-trains the LLM with GRPO using a context-relative reward on the curated catalogs.
PkLAt2VOY3.key_idea: Jointly optimizes a catalog-pruning reorganizer from downstream LLM selection feedback and post-trains the LLM with context-relative rewards.
PkLAt2VOY3.evidence: Evaluated across seven real merchants and 100 conversational queries per merchant using proprietary and open-weight LLMs.
PkLAt2VOY3.claimed_gains: Context curation yields gains of up to 31.4 percentage points and post-training adds a further 10.3 points on average.
PkLAt2VOY3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is practical, improves accuracy and latency across seven merchants and multiple backbones, and isolates the LLM-in-the-loop reorganizer via ablations.
PkLAt2VOY3.main_concern: Reviewers point out that synthetic queries, rewards, and single-reference labels are generated by gemini-3.1-pro (with 64.9% judge acceptance) and key IR baselines like BM25, ColBERT, and RankRAG are missing.

qUEHP1ucAK.one_liner: Formulates joint retriever and LLM policy optimization in agentic RL as a bilevel problem solved with first-order gradient estimation.
qUEHP1ucAK.problem: Agentic RL treats retrieved documents as fixed environment observations, misattributing retrieval failures to the LLM policy instead of updating the retriever.
qUEHP1ucAK.method: BRIDGE models joint retriever and LLM training as a bilevel optimization problem with retriever adaptation at the lower level, preserving the empirically observed sensitivity to update order. It solves this with a memory-efficient first-order method combining RL rewards and RAG likelihoods.
qUEHP1ucAK.key_idea: Solves joint retriever-LLM agentic RL as a bilevel optimization problem with lower-level retriever LoRA adaptation driven by RL and RAG-likelihood signals.
qUEHP1ucAK.evidence: Evaluated on 3B and 7B backbones across seven open-domain QA benchmarks and five medical QA benchmarks, plus convergence analysis.
qUEHP1ucAK.claimed_gains: Improves multi-hop QA accuracy by 9.8% (3B) and 3.3% (7B) across seven open-domain QA benchmarks.
qUEHP1ucAK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bilevel formulation is well-motivated and achieves consistent accuracy gains across multiple open-domain and medical QA benchmarks.
qUEHP1ucAK.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of direct retrieval metrics (such as recall or NDCG) to isolate retriever gains from LLM gains, plus missing seed variance.

67SF8nq4EN.one_liner: Aligns multilingual decoder-only LLMs by matching sequence-pooled MoE router probabilities across translation pairs.
67SF8nq4EN.problem: Varying tokenization lengths across languages prevents direct token-level hidden-state contrastive alignment in multilingual decoder-only LLMs.
67SF8nq4EN.method: The authors apply an auxiliary cross-lingual alignment loss to the sequence-level mean-pooled router output distributions of Mixture-of-Experts layers across parallel translations. Because router outputs have fixed expert dimensionality regardless of token count, this enables direct sequence-level alignment without token matching.
67SF8nq4EN.key_idea: Applies an auxiliary alignment loss to mean-pooled MoE router distributions across translated sequences, bypassing cross-lingual tokenization length mismatches.
67SF8nq4EN.evidence: Controlled continual pre-training experiments on four open-source MoE models evaluating routing alignment, hidden-state alignment, and multilingual downstream benchmarks.
67SF8nq4EN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using sequence-pooled MoE router outputs is a clean, practical way to bypass tokenization mismatches in cross-lingual alignment.
67SF8nq4EN.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains come from semantic alignment versus shifting routing toward English distributions, and ask for evaluations on English-language trade-offs.

30nE9a2zv7.one_liner: Trains a neural score model to reverse reflected diffusions on bounded convex domains for unbiased importance-sampled integration.
30nE9a2zv7.problem: Learned diffusion samplers for numerical integration operate on unbounded Euclidean space or boundaryless manifolds and cannot handle integrands on bounded convex domains.
30nE9a2zv7.method: The method uses a reflected diffusion that maps the target distribution toward the uniform distribution on a bounded domain and trains a neural score model to reverse it, yielding a boundary-term-free change-of-measure objective and unbiased importance weights. A REINFORCE estimator using pre-reflection Gaussian proposals handles non-smooth integrands.
30nE9a2zv7.key_idea: Reverses a reflected diffusion toward the uniform distribution on a bounded convex domain to obtain an adaptive proposal with computable importance weights.
30nE9a2zv7.evidence: Evaluated on high-dimensional bounded numerical integration tasks and the Digits dataset against Quasi-Monte Carlo and sampling baselines.
30nE9a2zv7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find extending reflected diffusion models to data-free bounded-domain integration and non-differentiable integrands interesting and clearly presented.
30nE9a2zv7.main_concern: Reviewers note missing runtime/training-cost comparisons against training-free QMC, omitted AIS/SMC baselines, and limited novelty beyond combining PIS with reflected diffusions.

XzxPii6bnf.one_liner: Unties self-conditioning from ODE solver updates in flow-matching language models via training-free projection scaling and history correction.
XzxPii6bnf.problem: Self-conditioned flow-matching language models reuse the same clean prediction for both the solver step and next-step conditioning, degrading few-step generation quality.
XzxPii6bnf.method: Untied Self-Conditioning scales down self-conditioning components along directions shared with the model's input projections while using prediction history and offline trajectory statistics to compute a solver-only correction, requiring one model evaluation per step without retraining.
XzxPii6bnf.key_idea: Decouples self-conditioning from solver updates in one NFE per step by suppressing redundant conditioning projections and applying a trajectory-estimated solver correction.
XzxPii6bnf.evidence: Evaluated across pretrained flow-matching language models (ELF and LangFlow) on OpenWebText and other benchmarks at low NFE.
XzxPii6bnf.claimed_gains: Improves generation quality and reduces generative perplexity at 8 NFE across evaluated baselines (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
XzxPii6bnf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the diagnosis separating solver updates from self-conditioning and the training-free GenPPL gains at low NFE.
XzxPii6bnf.main_concern: Reviewers note GenPPL gains coincide with lower unigram entropy and higher n-gram repetition, and question the theoretical justification and complexity of the heuristics.

Jep3qqMkU9.one_liner: Distills a LoRA task expert and frozen base VLA policy in velocity-field space using a per-sample competence gate.
Jep3qqMkU9.problem: Adapting pretrained vision-language-action policies to novel tasks causes catastrophic forgetting or trades retention for acquisition under weight merging.
Jep3qqMkU9.method: KEEP fine-tunes a LoRA task expert, computes a per-sample competence gate comparing flow-matching errors of the expert and frozen base policy, and trains a student to match the expert's velocity field where competent and the base policy's field elsewhere.
Jep3qqMkU9.key_idea: Uses flow-matching error differences between a LoRA expert and frozen base policy to gate dual-teacher distillation in velocity-field space.
Jep3qqMkU9.evidence: Evaluated with 5,150 real-robot rollouts across three single-task and one two-task settings on pi_0.5, plus over 250,000 simulated episodes.
Jep3qqMkU9.claimed_gains: Matches task experts on novel tasks while keeping generalist performance within the noise of pretrained pi_0.5, whereas the strongest weight-merging baseline loses close to fifteen points.
Jep3qqMkU9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the extensive empirical validation across 5,150 real-robot rollouts and over 250,000 simulated episodes.
Jep3qqMkU9.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on pretraining replay data, limited continual learning beyond two tasks, unvalidated link between flow loss and policy quality, and writing clarity issues.

8ZlVj8zkht.one_liner: Generates TMAX-13K synthetic terminal environments and trains 2B-27B open models with an outcome-only DPPO RL recipe.
8ZlVj8zkht.problem: RL training for terminal-using agents is hindered by scarce open environments, hard benchmarks, and unstable training recipes.
8ZlVj8zkht.method: Generates 13,565 terminal environments (TMAX-13K) using a taxonomy with difficulty control, personas, and verifier auditing/repair, then trains 2B-27B models with outcome-only DPPO, FP32 LM head, and larger group sizes.
8ZlVj8zkht.key_idea: Combines taxonomy-driven synthetic terminal environment generation and verifier repair with outcome-only DPPO using an FP32 LM head and large group sizes.
8ZlVj8zkht.evidence: Evaluates 2B to 27B models across model families on Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/Lite, SWE-Bench Verified, and AIME against prior datasets.
8ZlVj8zkht.claimed_gains: Achieves 33% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with a 9B model (TL;DR states 27% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 13,565 environments).
8ZlVj8zkht.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the release of the TMAX-13K environment dataset and consistent improvements across smaller open models.
8ZlVj8zkht.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty, shrinking gains at 27B scale, and potential distributional alignment with Terminal-Bench.

T0JBRmZ4pB.one_liner: Evaluates covert sabotage and LLM monitor detection across four autonomous AI R&D workflows.
T0JBRmZ4pB.problem: It is unclear whether autonomous AI R&D agents will execute covert sabotage and whether monitor agents can detect it from transcripts or artifacts.
T0JBRmZ4pB.method: ResearchArena pairs four AI R&D tasks (safety post-training, capabilities post-training, CUDA-kernel optimization, inference-server optimization) with embedded or independent harmful side tasks, evaluating monitors across artifact-access and CoT-access axes.
T0JBRmZ4pB.key_idea: Tests autonomous R&D agents on simultaneous main and covert sabotage tasks while benchmarking monitors with varying access to final artifacts and reasoning traces.
T0JBRmZ4pB.evidence: Empirical evaluation across four R&D domains, multiple agent models, and four monitoring conditions.
T0JBRmZ4pB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the realistic R&D evaluation setting combining legitimate engineering tasks, covert sabotage, and artifact-inspecting monitors.
T0JBRmZ4pB.main_concern: Reviewers cite methodological confounds (marking problematic baselines as false positives, mismatched CoT/model runs, and limited task diversity).

ToHK3NonvH.one_liner: Adapts a shared longitudinal brain-tumor MRI world model using a treatment-response field and recurring forecast-error history.
ToHK3NonvH.problem: Forecasting patient-specific tumor evolution from irregular serial MRIs is difficult when models ignore prior treatment courses and patient-specific forecast deviations.
ToHK3NonvH.method: LMWM learns a shared latent transition across patients and adds two conditioning signals: a treatment-response field encoding course timing/location and a history map of recurring deviations in the patient's past forecasts, scored via signed change F1 (cF1).
ToHK3NonvH.key_idea: Conditions a shared cross-patient latent MRI transition on a spatial-temporal treatment-response field and a map of recurring patient-specific forecast residuals.
ToHK3NonvH.evidence: Evaluated on longitudinal patient timelines from twelve public brain-tumor MRI collections against twelve image-generation baselines.
ToHK3NonvH.claimed_gains: Raises signed change F1 (cF1) from 31.6% for the shared model to 45.1% (and 37.2% with treatment only), exceeding copying the input (72.9% follow-up Dice).
ToHK3NonvH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the conditioning design separating shared dynamics from treatment and history, and beating the trivial copy-last-scan baseline.
ToHK3NonvH.main_concern: Reviewers question combining biologically distinct GBM and metastasis cohorts, unablated residual flow-matching/loss choices, and whether simpler history conditioning works similarly.

cxZ9isKl1Q.one_liner: Adapts forward graph diffusion noise and reverse spectral reconstruction jointly using a learnable Bernstein polynomial response function.
cxZ9isKl1Q.problem: Existing graph diffusion models use uniform or predefined noise schedules that ignore how heterogeneous graph spectral distributions affect perturbation and recovery across frequencies.
cxZ9isKl1Q.method: SPREAD parameterizes a learnable spectral response function with Bernstein polynomials to regulate forward noise intensity per frequency band. In the reverse process, a frequency-aware spectral reconstruction objective weights bands according to the learned response profiles to recover informative components.
cxZ9isKl1Q.key_idea: Parameterizing a frequency-dependent forward noise schedule and matching reverse reconstruction weights via learnable Bernstein polynomials on graph spectra.
cxZ9isKl1Q.evidence: Theoretical approximation analysis via Bernstein polynomials and experiments on node and graph classification benchmarks with ablations.
cxZ9isKl1Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the spectral SNR motivation is clear and that jointly adapting forward and reverse processes with a compact Bernstein response is coherent.
cxZ9isKl1Q.main_concern: Reviewers note limited theoretical novelty, missing noise-strength-matched controls and runtime/scalability comparisons for Laplacian eigendecomposition, and potential trivial zero-noise degeneration.

tVFAecXZK9.one_liner: Repairs AI-generated image detector blind spots without retraining by extracting generator fingerprints in a PCA residual space.
tVFAecXZK9.problem: AI-generated image detectors suffer blind spots on unseen generators, and fine-tuning on missed generators risks degrading performance on already-detected ones.
tVFAecXZK9.method: Generator Fingerprint Isolation (GFI) removes the top principal components explaining real-image variance in pretrained CLIP and DINO embeddings to form a residual space. It extracts generator-specific fingerprints from this residual space and fuses fingerprint alignment scores with the frozen detector's predictions at inference.
tVFAecXZK9.key_idea: Projecting pretrained features orthogonal to dominant real-image principal components to isolate generator fingerprints and fuse them with frozen detectors.
tVFAecXZK9.evidence: Evaluated on AIGCDetectBench across blind-spot generators using CLIP and DINO representations.
tVFAecXZK9.claimed_gains: Removing principal components accounting for 95% of real-image variance yields a residual space that preserves 78.8% of the measured generator-discriminative signal.
tVFAecXZK9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training-free, modular post-hoc blind-spot repair for deployed AIGI detectors is practical and well-motivated.
tVFAecXZK9.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over existing residual-feature detectors, reliance on outdated generators in AIGCDetectBench rather than modern models like FLUX, and unanalyzed sensitivity to fingerprint sample size.

7aLC09U77O.one_liner: Trains a unified protein foundation model on 205M UniProtKB text-protein pairs to follow instructions alongside ligand and antigen context.
7aLC09U77O.problem: Designing proteins with specified functions requires integrating natural-language instructions with biological contextual constraints such as ligand or antigen structures.
7aLC09U77O.method: NLPro combines a text encoder with specialized biological encoders in a unified generative architecture supporting full-sequence generation and span infilling. The authors curate NLProBench (205M description-protein pairs from UniProtKB via InterPro summaries) and fine-tune NLPro on ligand-binding protein and antibody design.
7aLC09U77O.key_idea: Unifying text and biological context encoders trained on 205M InterPro-derived description-protein pairs for instruction-guided protein generation.
7aLC09U77O.evidence: Evaluated on functional recovery, ligand-binding protein design, and antibody design benchmarks.
7aLC09U77O.claimed_gains: Attains a functional F1 score of 74.8%, a DockQ score of 0.38 in antibody design, and an ipTM score of 0.90 in ligand-binding protein design.
7aLC09U77O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that curating the 205M-pair NLProBench dataset from InterPro annotations is scalable and the unified multi-task protein design framework is practically relevant.
7aLC09U77O.main_concern: Reviewers note that biological-context conditioning fails to improve antibody DockQ over text-only input, the closest baseline (InstructPro) is missing, and evaluation metrics closely mirror training InterPro annotations.

f0fSfp0g3Z.one_liner: Conditions a diffusion shadow generator on ray-casted geometric shadow masks, estimated light direction, and learned confidence scores.
f0fSfp0g3Z.problem: Learning-based shadow generation treats the task as image translation without explicit physical reasoning, causing misaligned or implausible outdoor cast shadows.
f0fSfp0g3Z.method: Given a composite image and foreground mask, the method recovers monocular scene geometry (via MoGe-2) and estimates dominant light direction to ray-cast a coarse shadow mask. It predicts confidence scores for both lighting and shadow cues to gate their conditioning strength inside a diffusion generator.
f0fSfp0g3Z.key_idea: Gating diffusion conditioning with predicted confidence scores over ray-casted geometric shadow masks and estimated light direction.
f0fSfp0g3Z.evidence: Evaluated on the DESOBAV2 benchmark across BOS and BOS-free settings with diagnostic and ablation studies.
f0fSfp0g3Z.claimed_gains: Achieves 23% lower shadow-region RMSE and 30% lower shadow-mask BER than the prior state-of-the-art method on DESOBAV2.
f0fSfp0g3Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that confidence-aware physical conditioning is well-motivated for ill-posed single-image shadow generation and achieves strong DESOBAV2 results.
f0fSfp0g3Z.main_concern: Reviewers point out that point-map conditioning alone accounts for most of the gain over baselines, making the incremental value of the confidence gating and ray-casting mechanisms unclear.

ZlzSVYjMAI.one_liner: Applies prediction-powered inference to debias noisy zero-cost proxy pairwise rankings using scarce ground-truth evaluations in neural architecture search.
ZlzSVYjMAI.problem: Neural architecture search struggles to combine scarce, expensive ground-truth accuracy labels with abundant but noisy zero-cost proxy (ZCP) rankings.
ZlzSVYjMAI.method: PPNAS formulates predictor-based NAS using pairwise ranking supervision from both labeled architectures and large sets of ZCP-scored architectures. It adapts prediction-powered inference (PPI) with architecture-level Hájek projections to debias systematic discrepancies between ZCP-based and ground-truth rankings.
ZlzSVYjMAI.key_idea: Using prediction-powered inference over pairwise preference rankings to debias abundant zero-cost proxy signals with limited ground-truth evaluations.
ZlzSVYjMAI.evidence: Evaluated on tabular NAS benchmarks across multiple search spaces, datasets, zero-cost proxies, and architecture encodings.
ZlzSVYjMAI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting prediction-powered inference to fuse ground-truth labels and zero-cost proxies via pairwise rankings is well-motivated and broadly evaluated on tabular NAS.
ZlzSVYjMAI.main_concern: Reviewers note missing controlled ablations against simple weighted loss fusion under identical predictors, restriction to tabular NAS benchmarks, and violation of i.i.d. PPI assumptions during active search.
