kZ6GdwbHqK.one_liner: Constructs finite-sample view-level conformal RGB prediction intervals for 3D Gaussian Splatting by factorizing spatial shape and view difficulty.
kZ6GdwbHqK.problem: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting uncertainty heatmaps only rank risky pixels and cannot guarantee what fraction of pixels in a novel view falls inside calibrated RGB intervals.
kZ6GdwbHqK.method: View-Structured Conformal Prediction (VSCP) factorizes pre-calibration scale into a renderer spatial shape and a transferable view-difficulty predictor, then applies a held-out quantile over views (View-CP) to guarantee with probability at least 1−α that RGB boxes cover at least 1−β of pixels in a new view.
kZ6GdwbHqK.key_idea: Factorizes pixel uncertainty into a renderer spatial map and a predicted view-difficulty multiplier, calibrated with a view-level held-out quantile for finite-sample view-event coverage.
kZ6GdwbHqK.evidence: Theoretical excess-width decomposition and experiments across 13 real scenes comparing against pixel-pooled calibration, constant scales, and ten-model ensembles.
kZ6GdwbHqK.claimed_gains: Across 13 real scenes at a 90% target, View-CP achieves 91.7–92.0% view-event coverage (vs. 61.4% for pixel-pooled calibration), and VSCP cuts width by 22.1% over a constant scale, matching a ten-model ensemble's 21.0% reduction using one model and four rather than ten rasterization passes.
kZ6GdwbHqK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a genuine blind spot between marginal pixel coverage and view-level coverage, backed by clean factorization and empirical contrast.
kZ6GdwbHqK.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical motivation and evaluation protocol, noting that interleaved holdouts only test interpolation, the writing is dense, and the learned view factor beats a simple per-view mean only marginally.

l7GtgaeX0B.one_liner: Introduces a 416K-frame visually grounded driving reasoning dataset and curriculum SFT linking decision-critical objects to trajectory planning.
l7GtgaeX0B.problem: Existing autonomous driving datasets offer limited supervision connecting decision-critical visual elements to causal reasoning and trajectory planning in long-tail scenarios.
l7GtgaeX0B.method: AnchorReasoning annotates WOD-E2E frames with visually grounded chains-of-thought (VG-CoT) linking object localization, attributes, rationale, and trajectory planning, paired with curriculum supervised fine-tuning and an object-size-aware grounding metric.
l7GtgaeX0B.key_idea: Organizes long-tail driving frames into hierarchical visually grounded chains-of-thought from critical-object localization to trajectory planning and trains VLMs via curriculum SFT.
l7GtgaeX0B.evidence: Dataset of 416,119 frames and 395,379 elements evaluated across eight general-purpose, embodied-AI, and AV-specific VLM backbones on trajectory prediction, RFS, and grounding.
l7GtgaeX0B.claimed_gains: Reduces ADE@5s by 11.9% on Alpamayo-R1 and 15.8% on Alpamayo-1.5 while using 18.5 fewer reasoning tokens and 0.32 s/frame lower inference latency.
l7GtgaeX0B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the large-scale decision-focused annotations on WOD-E2E, clear presentation, and broad evaluation across eight model backbones.
l7GtgaeX0B.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to prior grounded driving-reasoning datasets (DriveLM, DriveCoT, nuReasoning, AutoDrive-P³), note reliance on VLM/GPT-5.5 annotation and evaluation, and lack of closed-loop safety validation.

CzVkRf2QVu.one_liner: Samples implicit perceptual priors of MLLMs directly via Gibbs sampling over diffusion-generated stimuli steered along interpretable slider axes.
CzVkRf2QVu.problem: Fixed-stimulus behavioral probes and internal mechanistic probes cannot reconstruct the implicit visual prior distribution an MLLM expects over high-dimensional image spaces.
CzVkRf2QVu.method: The authors steer a diffusion generator along controllable semantic PCA slider axes and run Gibbs sampling (with Barker acceptance) using the target MLLM as a pairwise judge to sample directly from its perceptual prior over concepts such as face trustworthiness or art cheapness.
CzVkRf2QVu.key_idea: Uses the target MLLM as a pairwise judge inside a Gibbs sampler over diffusion-generated images steered along controllable semantic slider directions.
CzVkRf2QVu.evidence: Applied across multiple MLLMs, visual domains, and target concepts to recover canonical and unexpected perceptual priors.
CzVkRf2QVu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find extending human Gibbs-sampling prior elicitation to MLLMs with interpretable diffusion controls conceptually engaging and broadly tested.
CzVkRf2QVu.main_concern: Reviewers raise severe statistical concerns: the required Bradley-Terry global utility consistency is unverified, MCMC chains show poor convergence (high split-R-hat and low acceptance rates), and 10 fixed PCA sliders restrict bias discovery.

jnJ31akuq6.one_liner: Guides image editing from target-viewing EEG via dual-path cross-attention and time-gated residuals, introducing the Neve benchmark.
jnJ31akuq6.problem: Translating visual-perception EEG into precise semantic and appearance image edits while preserving unrelated source content lacks both aligned mechanisms and paired benchmarks.
jnJ31akuq6.method: EEGRAFT aligns neural and visual representations so source-conditioned visual states query EEG summary and unpooled features via separate attention pathways with time-gated residual updates, requiring only a source image and target-viewing EEG at inference. The Neve benchmark provides 29,275 source-target pairs and 2.71M EEG trials by generating synthetic source images from viewed targets.
jnJ31akuq6.key_idea: Queries aligned EEG summary and unpooled features via dual cross-attention pathways with time-gated residual updates conditioned on the source image.
jnJ31akuq6.evidence: Evaluated on the Neve benchmark (29,275 pairs, 2.71M EEG trials) against six baselines across six aggregate metrics plus fixed-editor mismatched-EEG controls.
jnJ31akuq6.claimed_gains: Reduces C-LPIPS by 22.7% and increases R-Edit from 0.386 to 0.585 relative to the strongest baseline for each metric.
jnJ31akuq6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the inverted Neve dataset construction avoiding synthetic EEG, strict concept-disjoint splits, and change-region evaluation metrics.
jnJ31akuq6.main_concern: Reviewers point out that EEGRAFT with null/mismatched EEG already beats all external baselines due to its stronger OmniGen2 backbone and synthetic-to-natural domain gap, confounding the headline gains.

GbSSGmkvqL.one_liner: Uses dynamic programming to let an implicit-CoT student select an ordered, non-reusing teacher KV supervision path without extra parameters.
GbSSGmkvqL.problem: Implicit chain-of-thought distillation selects informative teacher KV states globally without determining which specific teacher state best supervises each student latent step.
GbSSGmkvqL.method: SPIRE uses the student's current representations to score a compact pool of teacher KV states and solves an exact dynamic program to assign a distinct, order-preserving teacher target to each active student step. It adds no trainable routing parameters and leaves inference unchanged.
GbSSGmkvqL.key_idea: Solves an exact dynamic program over student-teacher similarity scores to assign an ordered, non-reusing teacher KV supervision path per student step.
GbSSGmkvqL.evidence: Stability analysis under score noise plus experiments across three arithmetic reasoning benchmarks and three model backbones.
GbSSGmkvqL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clearly framed student-step supervision allocation problem and the lightweight, parameter-free training-time mechanism.
GbSSGmkvqL.main_concern: Reviewers question the motivation study and cosine-similarity proxy for cross-entropy utility, note confounded candidate-pool sizes (18 vs 12) in ablations, and observe sensitivity to pool size.

qp6WwtHd1J.one_liner: Separates selective visual-block refinement from lightweight query-guided visual access with cross-layer priority feedback for long-video LLMs.
qp6WwtHd1J.problem: Long-video MLLMs waste compute updating redundant visual tokens at every layer, yet standard pruning or skipping discards evidence still needed for answering.
qp6WwtHd1J.method: AdaDPC splits computation on a shared visual state sequence into a Selective Refinement Path (full attention and FFN on chosen visual blocks) and a Query-Guided Access Path (low-cost text-query retrieval from remaining blocks). Cross-Layer Priority Feedback uses evidence discovered during access to guide subsequent-layer refinement.
qp6WwtHd1J.key_idea: Combines selective block-wise full refinement with low-cost query-guided cross-attention over skipped visual tokens and cross-layer priority feedback.
qp6WwtHd1J.evidence: Evaluated across eight long-video benchmarks (including MLVU Dev and TimeScope) on Qwen2.5-VL-3B.
qp6WwtHd1J.claimed_gains: Improves MLVU Dev from 65.3 to 69.7 (+4.4 points) and TimeScope from 76.3 to 81.9 (+5.6 points) over the dense model while reducing FLOPs by 55.5%.
qp6WwtHd1J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the conceptual separation between updating visual states and keeping skipped tokens readable by the query.
qp6WwtHd1J.main_concern: Reviewers note unfair comparisons against training-free baselines without matched FLOPs or trained MoD baselines, incomplete end-to-end latency/memory reporting, and evaluation limited to Qwen2.5-VL-3B.

Ns3mHOVa2R.one_liner: Benchmarks AI agents on open-ended LLM inference server deployment and latency/throughput optimization on one H100 within 2 hours.
Ns3mHOVa2R.problem: Existing R&D agent benchmarks constrain agents to narrow action spaces, obscuring whether agents genuinely optimize systems or reproduce known solutions.
Ns3mHOVa2R.method: InferenceBench tasks agents with deploying an OpenAI-compatible server on one H100 GPU within a 2-hour budget to optimize time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, request throughput, or a combined objective. The benchmark evaluates 42 agent configurations against default engines and matched-budget hyperparameter search.
Ns3mHOVa2R.key_idea: Evaluates open-ended agent systems engineering on real LLM serving throughput and latency under a fixed 2-hour single-H100 budget against matched-budget search.
Ns3mHOVa2R.evidence: 504 scored runs across 42 agent configurations, matched-budget random/Bayesian hyperparameter search, and warm-start/forced-engine ablations.
Ns3mHOVa2R.claimed_gains: 30 of 42 agents exceed default vLLM (4.05x over naive PyTorch), while matched-budget vLLM hyperparameter search reaches 11.53x, beating all agents except Claude Opus 5.5 (12.08x).
Ns3mHOVa2R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical end-to-end systems task, extensive 42-agent evaluation, and matched-budget hyperparameter search baseline.
Ns3mHOVa2R.main_concern: Reviewers question practical validity due to small 7B/8K-token settings that avoid memory bottlenecks, forced EOS-ignoring decode workloads, and potential max-over-dev selection bias.

kFGHs4vhnw.one_liner: Learns diffusion perturbation laws via Bayesian nonparametrics and a corrected denoising score matching risk for finite-resource learners.
kFGHs4vhnw.problem: Diffusion models typically fix a Gaussian perturbation law, and raw denoising score matching cannot fairly compare alternative perturbation distributions due to an irreducible perturbation-dependent term.
kFGHs4vhnw.method: The authors formulate a Bayesian nonparametric (BNP) diffusion model that learns the perturbation distribution via generalized Bayesian inference using a corrected DSM criterion. They prove consistency for finite-resource score risk, posterior concentration, and reverse-process error control.
kFGHs4vhnw.key_idea: Subtracts the perturbation-dependent irreducible DSM term to perform generalized Bayesian nonparametric inference over diffusion perturbation laws.
kFGHs4vhnw.evidence: Theoretical consistency, concentration, and reverse-error bounds plus controlled synthetic experiments and evaluations on CIFAR-10 and HRRR.
kFGHs4vhnw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the principled corrected-DSM formulation for comparing perturbation laws and the theoretical guarantees.
kFGHs4vhnw.main_concern: Reviewers note mixed real-data results with missing generative quality metrics (e.g., FID/CRPS), observe that the scalar noise-scale construction reduces to noise-schedule selection, and flag unclear notation.

ElNbbliNdP.one_liner: Models and benchmarks GPU energy versus latency and FLOPs across sequential and parallel test-time scaling configurations.
ElNbbliNdP.problem: Test-time scaling laws rely on FLOPs or GPU-hours as proxies, poorly quantifying real-world inference energy costs across sequential and parallel scaling.
ElNbbliNdP.method: The authors build an analytic task-performance model for sequential and parallel test-time scaling and empirically measure GPU power and latency across Qwen3 models, budgets, sample counts, and three GPU platforms to identify energy-optimal configurations.
ElNbbliNdP.key_idea: Combines an analytic performance model with direct GPU power measurements to optimize sequential versus parallel test-time compute for energy.
ElNbbliNdP.evidence: Empirical GPU power/latency benchmarks on Qwen3 dense and MoE models across AIME, MATH-500, coding, and GPQA on three GPU platforms.
ElNbbliNdP.claimed_gains: Energy-optimal configurations on Qwen3 reduce inference energy use by 22% compared to latency-optimal selections and by 242% compared to FLOPS-optimal selections.
ElNbbliNdP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find studying real GPU energy trade-offs in test-time scaling important and practically relevant.
ElNbbliNdP.main_concern: Reviewers note the savings rely on underutilized single-query serving ignoring system/idle power, findings vary across a single model family (Qwen3), and one reviewer reported a corrupted manuscript PDF.

8YIs6ENyBk.one_liner: Characterizes partial neural state tracking on finite groups algebraically via subgroup cosets, contrasting Transformer abelianization with recurrent non-normal cosets.
8YIs6ENyBk.problem: Aggregate accuracy on sequence state-tracking tasks does not reveal what intermediate algebraic state a partially accurate neural network actually represents.
8YIs6ENyBk.method: The authors analyze Transformers and recurrent networks trained on finite-group running products, showing partially accurate models track exact subgroup cosets and predict uniformly within each class. They prove optimal order-blind accuracy converges to the reciprocal abelianization class size and probe low-dimensional recurrent state subspaces on A5.
8YIs6ENyBk.key_idea: Identifies partial neural state tracking as exact subgroup-coset tracking, proving order-blind Transformers stop at normal abelianization while recurrent models track non-normal right cosets.
8YIs6ENyBk.evidence: Theoretical order-blind accuracy bound plus empirical census across Transformers and parameter-matched recurrent networks on finite groups including A5.
8YIs6ENyBk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algebraic coset explanation of partial state tracking and the Transformer-versus-recurrent contrast insightful and compelling.
8YIs6ENyBk.main_concern: Reviewers question the actionable implications for practical LLM architecture design and criticize opaque presentation of experimental recipes.

SB9MyQ9sAX.one_liner: Aligns multi-objective self-supervised EEG pretraining losses via a closed-form loss-statistics weighting rule without per-objective gradient computation.
SB9MyQ9sAX.problem: Multi-objective self-supervised pretraining of EEG time-series foundation models suffers from gradient-magnitude disparities that let one objective dominate optimization.
SB9MyQ9sAX.method: MAPE introduces a loss-based adaptive weighting framework with a closed-form rule derived from pretraining loss statistics to balance multiple self-supervised objectives in a single pipeline without computing separate per-objective gradients.
SB9MyQ9sAX.key_idea: Computes closed-form adaptive multi-objective pretraining weights directly from normalized loss statistics instead of explicit per-objective gradients.
SB9MyQ9sAX.evidence: Empirical study across three encoders (one general time-series and two EEG-specific models) comparing MAPE against single-objective and unaligned multi-objective pretraining.
SB9MyQ9sAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the lightweight gradient-free weighting mechanism and multi-architecture EEG evaluation.
SB9MyQ9sAX.main_concern: Reviewers question whether small gains exceed standard-deviation noise, lack a normalized-loss fixed-weight baseline, and note missing handling of potentially negative weights or gradient-direction conflict checks.

0OQQhoUHkA.one_liner: SVD-structured disentangled category transformations decouple update direction and amplitude for incremental vision-language object detection.
0OQQhoUHkA.problem: Incremental vision-language object detection suffers from inter-category homogenization when coupled update matrices are overwhelmed by shared generic gradients, and intra-category drift across recurring tasks.
0OQQhoUHkA.method: CADT introduces Disentangled Category-Aware Transformation (DCT), which uses an SVD-like structure to decouple category update direction and amplitude on a frozen shared anchor. It pairs these parameter-efficient category cores with consistency constraints for recurring categories across continual tasks.
0OQQhoUHkA.key_idea: Decouple category-specific update directions and amplitudes via SVD-structured low-rank cores on a frozen anchor while applying consistency constraints to recurring categories.
0OQQhoUHkA.evidence: Evaluated on incremental vision-language object detection benchmarks (including ODinW-O and ZCOCO) with component ablations and parameter-efficiency analyses.
0OQQhoUHkA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear decomposition into inter- and intra-category interference, parameter-efficient category cores, and extensive ablation studies.
0OQQhoUHkA.main_concern: Theoretical analysis assumes strictly orthogonal SVD factors whereas the implementation uses only soft orthogonality regularization, alongside internal numerical inconsistencies across reported tables.

4I2qS5Edtg.one_liner: Path-value estimator P-DC-SCTR models current state, local transitions, and remaining tasks to predict continual fine-tuning safety.
4I2qS5Edtg.problem: Continual fine-tuning on benign tasks exhibits path-dependent terminal safety degradation where one-step local safety effects fail to predict final safety after remaining tasks.
4I2qS5Edtg.method: The authors formulate continual task ordering as terminal path-value estimation and introduce P-DC-SCTR, which jointly models the current model state, local task transition effects, and the remaining adaptation path. They enumerate all task orders under fixed data and budgets to compare local monitoring against trajectory-level prediction.
4I2qS5Edtg.key_idea: Estimate terminal safety from joint representations of current state, local one-step transition effects, and the remaining task sequence rather than isolated one-step updates.
4I2qS5Edtg.evidence: Controlled experiments enumerating all 24 permutations of four benign tasks (qa, code, math, summarization) on a LoRA-anchored 0.6B model across multiple continual fine-tuning settings.
4I2qS5Edtg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled experimental design isolating task order effects and the authors' transparency about the limits of their estimator.
4I2qS5Edtg.main_concern: The small 0.6B model with shallow LoRA alignment limits external validity, and assuming known reorderable future tasks resembles curriculum design rather than realistic continual learning.

sENe8VBeGG.one_liner: Loss-expansion leading-support signatures classify five extreme learning regimes of large weight-tied linear autoencoders onto a triangular prism.
sENe8VBeGG.problem: Theoretical analyses of gradient descent typically study isolated limiting regimes rather than systematically classifying all qualitatively distinct extreme learning regimes of a model.
sENe8VBeGG.method: The authors analyze formal loss expansions of large weight-tied linear autoencoders parameterized by input dimension, latent dimension, initialization scale, and dataset size, mapping five basic extreme regimes to the 2-faces of a triangular prism. For four regimes (large-data, small-data, mean-field, narrow-latent), they derive limiting training and population-loss dynamics with convergence guarantees.
sENe8VBeGG.key_idea: Classify extreme gradient-flow regimes by mapping leading-support monomials of formal loss expansions to the faces of a triangular prism.
sENe8VBeGG.evidence: Theoretical derivations of limiting dynamics and convergence bounds on logarithmically growing time intervals, paired with numerical experiments on linear autoencoders.
sENe8VBeGG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the leading-support prism classification mathematically explicit, principled, and interesting for organizing parameter scalings.
sENe8VBeGG.main_concern: The formal Taylor-expansion classification at initialization does not guarantee exhaustion of full dynamical trajectories, and practical relevance beyond weight-tied linear autoencoders is unclear.

OIX56pKbrH.one_liner: Self-supervised dynamic graph transformer STAGE prunes cross-channel edges and occludes nodes for real-time time-series anomaly attribution.
OIX56pKbrH.problem: Multivariate time-series anomaly detectors face a trade-off between interpretable graph methods with lower accuracy and expressive deep models that lack real-time explanations.
OIX56pKbrH.method: STAGE represents time-series dimensions as vertices in a dynamic graph, prunes edges via multi-head attention to isolate cross-channel dependencies, and scores anomalies using a permutation-invariant readout. For post-hoc explainability without retraining, it occludes individual dimension nodes in a batched forward pass to measure anomaly-score shifts.
OIX56pKbrH.key_idea: Combine attention-pruned dynamic channel graphs with single-pass leave-one-node-out occlusion scoring for zero-retraining anomaly attribution.
OIX56pKbrH.evidence: Evaluated against 30 baselines across 180 multivariate time series on TSB-AD-M-Eval, plus attribution quality and speed tests on CoMuT and SMD.
OIX56pKbrH.claimed_gains: Achieves a VUS-PR of 0.44 on TSB-AD-M, matching the best baseline out of 30 and outperforming the runner-up by 12%.
OIX56pKbrH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clean architectural integration, competitive accuracy across 30 baselines on TSB-AD-M, and practical batched node-occlusion interface.
OIX56pKbrH.main_concern: Comparing STAGE's batched node occlusion against SHAP on competing detectors confounds detector and explainer speed, omitting cheaper residual or channel-masking attribution baselines.

B9a221JXqo.one_liner: Curated VenusRX-Bench dataset and two-stage pretrained encoder-decoder VenusRX jointly model reactants, products, and Enzyme Commission annotations.
B9a221JXqo.problem: Organic reaction models fail to capture the coupling between molecular structure and catalytic function in enzymatic reactions, and prior evaluations suffer from fragmented datasets and inconsistent splits.
B9a221JXqo.method: The authors build VenusRX-Bench, a 126,361-reaction benchmark with EC annotations, atom-atom mappings, and leakage-controlled splits across forward prediction, single-step retrosynthesis, and EC prediction. They also train VenusRX, a T5-style encoder-decoder pretrained in two stages on template-expanded reactions with EC conditioning.
B9a221JXqo.key_idea: Pretrain an EC-conditioned encoder-decoder in two stages on template-expanded enzymatic reactions and evaluate across unified leakage-controlled biochemical tasks.
B9a221JXqo.evidence: Evaluated on VenusRX-Bench (126,361 curated enzymatic reactions) across forward reaction prediction, single-step retrosynthesis, and EC-number prediction against chemical and enzymatic baselines.
B9a221JXqo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified multi-task biochemical benchmark with EC labels, atom mappings, and shared generalization splits.
B9a221JXqo.main_concern: Comparisons are confounded because VenusRX trains on millions of extra template-expanded reactions and multiple R-SMILES views unavailable to baselines, with limited modeling novelty beyond standard T5.

9WM5OmcrkZ.one_liner: Hierarchical page-store and RL-trained Researcher construct query-conditioned agent memory contexts at runtime via Memory-Gym.
9WM5OmcrkZ.problem: Ahead-of-time agent memory systems compress interaction histories before queries arrive, discarding fine-grained details needed for later requests.
9WM5OmcrkZ.method: JAM pairs a Memorizer that keeps full raw histories in a hierarchical page-store with compact navigational summaries and a Researcher that iteratively retrieves and integrates evidence at query time. The Researcher is trained on Memory-Gym, a synthesized dataset across nine task types and six domains, via verified-trajectory SFT followed by Hint-guided GRPO.
9WM5OmcrkZ.key_idea: Retain raw histories in a summarized hierarchical page-store and train an iterative runtime Researcher via verified-trajectory SFT and Hint-guided GRPO.
9WM5OmcrkZ.evidence: Evaluated across four public agent-memory and long-context QA benchmarks with ablations and efficiency analyses, trained on Memory-Gym.
9WM5OmcrkZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deferring memory extraction to query time is well motivated and that JAM achieves strong results across four benchmarks with a reusable Memory-Gym pipeline.
9WM5OmcrkZ.main_concern: Methodological novelty over multi-turn agentic RAG is unclear, comparisons lack controlled backbones and training data, and experiments cover only QA rather than continual agentic workflows.

zLC0A6UKiS.one_liner: Counterfactual likelihood-drop supervision trains a relational scorer to prune joint history-block sets under risk constraints.
zLC0A6UKiS.problem: Independent importance scoring for long-horizon agent history pruning ignores interactions, redundancies, and cumulative harm when deleting multiple blocks together.
zLC0A6UKiS.method: DRSR generates offline supervision by jointly deleting protocol-valid history blocks and measuring the change in teacher-forced likelihood of the recorded next output. A lightweight relational scorer predicts set-level deletion risk from pre-action state and pairwise block interactions, enabling online pruning of the largest feasible set under risk, recency, and budget gates.
zLC0A6UKiS.key_idea: Train a relational set-risk scorer on offline counterfactual teacher-forced likelihood drops to prune the largest risk-safe block subset online.
zLC0A6UKiS.evidence: Evaluated across four long-horizon agent domains and an Eval40 suite, plus empirical analysis of set-level interaction residuals.
zLC0A6UKiS.claimed_gains: Across four long-horizon agent domains, DRSR increases mean reward from 0.699 to 0.802 while reducing total model tokens by 20.82%.
zLC0A6UKiS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear theoretical and empirical argument for set-level deletion risk and the low-cost counterfactual supervision signal.
zLC0A6UKiS.main_concern: Direct pruning accounts for under 4% of total token savings on Eval40 while most savings and reward gains stem from unexplained trajectory shifts, and teacher-forced NLL change is not validated against task reward.

4iblWKVTlY.one_liner: Shortest-path flow matching with a learnable condition-dependent mixture base distribution improves conditional generation under distribution shift.
4iblWKVTlY.problem: Conditional flow-matching models fit training conditions well but struggle to extrapolate to unseen interventions such as held-out drugs or genetic perturbations.
4iblWKVTlY.method: SP-FM conditions both a learnable mixture base distribution and the transport vector field on the input condition, training the flow via shortest-path flow matching. Adapting the starting mixture per condition reduces source-target mismatch to support smoother interpolation and extrapolation.
4iblWKVTlY.key_idea: Condition a learnable mixture base distribution alongside the vector field in shortest-path flow matching to adapt the transport starting distribution per condition.
4iblWKVTlY.evidence: Theoretical transport analysis and experiments on synthetic data, single-cell transcriptomics perturbation prediction, and microscopy-based drug screening.
4iblWKVTlY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view conditioning the base distribution as an intuitive, easily integrable extension to flow matching tested across diverse synthetic and biological modalities.
4iblWKVTlY.main_concern: Unseen condition descriptor construction and test-split PCA leakage undermine generalization claims, alongside missing global-GMM ablations and theory-implementation gaps.

GliI8fGM76.one_liner: Topology-aware search ATLAS splits prompt injections into semantic atoms placed across multi-agent communication graphs with terminal closure.
GliI8fGM76.problem: Existing prompt-injection attacks on LLM multi-agent systems optimize inputs or exploit topology without modeling how adversarial intent converts and propagates across inter-agent traces.
GliI8fGM76.method: From trace-level security analysis identifying node-level conversion and semantic propagation as key drivers, ATLAS decomposes an injection into coordinated semantic atoms. It jointly searches injection locations and propagation paths over the communication topology and enforces terminal semantic closure to recover full attack intent.
GliI8fGM76.key_idea: Decompose indirect prompt injections into coordinated semantic atoms, search optimal injection nodes and propagation paths over the agent graph, and close intent at the target.
GliI8fGM76.evidence: Evaluated across three MAS security benchmarks (including TAMAS) and ten victim models with component ablations.
GliI8fGM76.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of inter-agent communication security and note consistent ASR gains across three benchmarks and ten models.
GliI8fGM76.main_concern: ATLAS assumes unrealistic full attacker knowledge of MAS topology and interfaces, compares mainly against weak original injections rather than strong multi-point baselines, and relies on an unvalidated LLM evaluator.

Car2Mw6Pnm.one_liner: Information-asymmetric client simulation and turn-level lookahead GRPO train PSYCHO-R1 for proactive multi-turn psychological counseling.
Car2Mw6Pnm.problem: LLM counselors struggle to proactively guide multi-turn therapy because they fail to infer hidden client states under information asymmetry and receive only coarse trajectory-level RL rewards.
Car2Mw6Pnm.method: PSYCHO-R1 is trained in an information-asymmetric environment with a private-profile client simulator and a turn-level reward evaluator. It links explicit client-state inference to hierarchical inquiry-or-intervention decisions and uses critic-free local lookahead returns to compute turn-level group-relative advantages.
Car2Mw6Pnm.key_idea: Train a state-inferring counselor policy in a hidden-profile client simulator using critic-free turn-level GRPO advantages derived from local lookahead returns.
Car2Mw6Pnm.evidence: Evaluated across 11 counselor, client, and therapeutic alliance dimensions on 150 PsyQA-seeded interactive cases against general and specialized mental-health LLMs.
Car2Mw6Pnm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers endorse framing counseling as sequential decision-making under hidden client state and appreciate the turn-level lookahead credit assignment over trajectory-level GRPO.
Car2Mw6Pnm.main_concern: Evaluation relies entirely on simulated LLM clients and GPT-5.5 judging—the same model family used for SFT data—with zero human or clinician validation on a small 150-case set.

jgkJnTg5O8.one_liner: Activation analysis links computer-use agent loops to absorbing regions, mitigated by R3 context reset, reroute, and restore.
jgkJnTg5O8.problem: Computer-use agents exhibit inertia, repeatedly executing ineffective actions even after explicitly acknowledging that those actions failed.
jgkJnTg5O8.method: The authors analyze high-dimensional model activations during repeated desktop actions, finding stale activation states resistant to linear steering. To escape this absorbing region, they propose R3 (Reset, Reroute, Restore), which temporarily clears the agent's context trajectory to trigger a new action and then restores the prior history.
jgkJnTg5O8.key_idea: Interrupt computer-use action loops by temporarily resetting the context trajectory to displace stale activations, rerouting the action, and restoring prior history.
jgkJnTg5O8.evidence: Cross-model activation analysis, linear readout and steering replay tests, and desktop task evaluations measuring recurrence and task scores.
jgkJnTg5O8.claimed_gains: R3 yields 17–55% lower measured inertia across models relative to unmodified agents.
jgkJnTg5O8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the inertia phenomenon practically relevant and value the repeatable screen-action recurrence metric and thorough activation diagnostics.
jgkJnTg5O8.main_concern: Reducing inertia with R3 does not improve actual task completion scores, the absorbing-region causal claim is underdetermined, and simple prompt-based anti-repetition baselines and closely related prior work are missing.

z5rJIBKibk.one_liner: Weight-sharing supernet FetNAS adds an elastic input-feature dimension to progressive shrinking for joint feature and architecture search.
z5rJIBKibk.problem: Resource-constrained tabular deployment requires minimizing both sensor input features and model size, whereas NAS fixes input features and feature selection fixes the architecture.
z5rJIBKibk.method: FetNAS extends progressive shrinking in a single over-parameterized supernet by making input-feature count an elastic dimension alongside depth and width, selecting top-ranked features via gradient-based importance. Multi-objective evolutionary search then extracts Pareto-optimal subnetworks over accuracy, parameter count, and feature count without retraining.
z5rJIBKibk.key_idea: Add a gradient-ranked elastic input-feature prefix stage to progressive-shrinking weight-sharing NAS and run multi-objective evolutionary search over the supernet.
z5rJIBKibk.evidence: Evaluated across 51 TabArena datasets (38 classification and 13 regression) with five cross-validation splits.
z5rJIBKibk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing feature count and model size for resource-constrained tabular learning is practical and broadly evaluated across 51 TabArena datasets.
z5rJIBKibk.main_concern: Restricting all architectures to prefixes of one fixed feature ranking limits true joint optimization, technical novelty over progressive shrinking is incremental, and training/search compute costs are unreported.

e2LH2NCbRs.one_liner: Multiscale Transformer neural operator uPDEt uses 3D RoPE and ball-tree local attention for unstructured steady and transient PDEs.
e2LH2NCbRs.problem: Neural operators on large unstructured 3D meshes incur high memory and compute overhead and are frequently restricted to steady-state predictions.
e2LH2NCbRs.method: uPDEt integrates ball-tree spatial partitioning, multiscale local attention with a 3D generalization of RoPE, attention-based pooling/unpooling, and queryable decoding into a Transformer neural operator. It supports both steady-state field prediction and autoregressive rollouts for transient physics.
e2LH2NCbRs.key_idea: Combine ball-tree multiscale local attention, 3D rotary position embeddings, and attention pooling/unpooling for compute-efficient steady and transient unstructured-mesh PDE surrogates.
e2LH2NCbRs.evidence: Evaluated under compute-matched comparisons on complex 3D unstructured benchmarks including DrivAerML and SHIFT-Wing against baselines such as SMART, AB-UPT, and GeoTransolver.
e2LH2NCbRs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight uPDEt's strong throughput and low GPU memory footprint while maintaining competitive accuracy on large-scale 3D meshes.
e2LH2NCbRs.main_concern: Accuracy comparisons are unfair because uPDEt receives extra geometric inputs (face normals and cell areas) omitted from coordinate-only baselines SMART and AB-UPT, and architectural details lack formal clarity.

lneAO3HEg9.one_liner: Federated NVS framework couples a server-side image-conditioned model with private client neural fields via local pseudo-view updates.
lneAO3HEg9.problem: Training large novel view synthesis models centrally violates scene privacy, while local sparse-view neural fields lack geometric supervision and cannot be shared without exposing renderable scenes.
lneAO3HEg9.method: Each client keeps raw images and its personalized neural field local, rendering nearby pseudo-target views to fine-tune a trainable subset of a server-side large NVS model and sending only parameter updates. The aggregated server model is returned to clients to regularize local neural fields via consistency supervision in a mutual-reinforcement loop.
lneAO3HEg9.key_idea: Use private client neural fields to render local pseudo-views that fine-tune a shared server NVS model, then return the aggregated server model to supervise local fields.
lneAO3HEg9.evidence: Experiments with 5,000 scene-level clients (plus 75,000 public scenes) and ablations comparing against reduced LVSM and FrugalNeRF on Objaverse.
lneAO3HEg9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent mutual-reinforcement mechanism bridging a global image-conditioned NVS model with private local neural fields without transmitting renderable weights.
lneAO3HEg9.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not match data, supervision, or compute budgets—especially given heavy server-side public-data training—and privacy tests do not evaluate leakage from individual client updates.

oGWaGHIPWm.one_liner: Training-free ThunderWorld repairs W4A4 world-model quantization error using budget-capped, structure-selected dense FP4 residual GEMMs.
oGWaGHIPWm.problem: Four-bit floating-point (W4A4) inference degrades generative world-model fidelity, while sparse or reordering-based mixed-precision fixes underutilize native dense FP4 Tensor Cores.
oGWaGHIPWm.method: ThunderWorld keeps base W4A4 attention blocks intact and adds block-aligned dense FP4 matrix products computed from quantization residuals under a compute budget. It uses offline-calibrated, structure-informed tile selection to allocate residual repair without training, sparse instructions, or channel reordering.
oGWaGHIPWm.key_idea: Correct W4A4 quantization error via dense FP4 residual GEMMs selected with structure-informed block-aligned policies under a fixed matrix-work budget.
oGWaGHIPWm.evidence: Evaluated on Cosmos3 Edge and Nano across RBench and PAI-Bench-G (~1,700 scenes per model) with end-to-end throughput measured on RTX PRO 6000 and Jetson AGX Thor.
oGWaGHIPWm.claimed_gains: At 2× base W4A4 matrix work, stays within 0.08 RBench points and 0.37 PAI-Bench-G percentage points of BF16, reduces LPIPS by 3.3–7.8% over ARCQuant (2.0), and achieves 1.17–1.88× its throughput.
oGWaGHIPWm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the hardware-friendly dense FP4 residual design, careful paired-seed evaluation, and fidelity/throughput gains over adapted FP4 baselines.
oGWaGHIPWm.main_concern: The paper omits end-to-end latency comparisons against BF16 and native FP8, even though 2× FP4 work roughly matches native FP8 compute while trailing FP8 in fidelity.

7C0ANUZ1Fp.one_liner: Policy-conditioned bottleneck ACB modulates visual tokens via scaling, channel reweighting, and rank-limited correction to isolate MLLM capabilities.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.problem: Collaborative MLLM inference transmits visual representations that let remote models exercise unauthorized capabilities, which standard reconstruction-focused privacy defenses do not selectively control.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.method: The authors formulate authorization-conditioned capability isolation and propose the Authorization-Conditioned Bottleneck (ACB), which transforms shared visual features without modifying the remote MLLM. ACB applies policy-conditioned token scaling, channel reweighting, rank-limited correction, and fixed-representation off-target preservation, evaluated on a 13-capability benchmark (AuthCap).
7C0ANUZ1Fp.key_idea: Apply policy-conditioned token scaling, channel reweighting, and rank-limited correction to shared visual embeddings to suppress denied capabilities toward No-Image performance while retaining off-target utility.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.evidence: Evaluated on the constructed 13-capability AuthCap benchmark across vision-language backbones including Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Molmo2-O-7B.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.claimed_gains: On AuthCap, ACB achieves 0.8194 authorized utility, reduces denied target capability to within 0.0007 of the No-Image reference, and improves unrelated capability retention from 0.1400 to 0.5479.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the request-level capability isolation framing over generic reconstruction privacy and note that ACB works without modifying the cloud MLLM.
7C0ANUZ1Fp.main_concern: Ablations fail to isolate each module (especially rank-limited correction) or compare against concept-erasure baselines, while evaluation is limited to single-capability policies on largely synthetic tasks with uneven cross-backbone retention.

w3zAs5rvZZ.one_liner: Pesto aligns separate modality embedding spaces through distributions over a shared topology-preserving 2D prototype grid.
w3zAs5rvZZ.problem: Projecting heterogeneous modalities into a single shared vector space imposes a common geometry that can discard modality-specific structure and hinder inference under missing modalities.
w3zAs5rvZZ.method: Pesto gives each modality its own encoder and prototype matrix but links them via a shared 2D self-organizing prototype grid so paired samples map to similar grid locations and similar instances cluster in neighboring cells. Joint training backpropagates a neighborhood loss through the encoders and prototypes, allowing any modality subset at inference without imputation or retraining.
w3zAs5rvZZ.key_idea: Align distinct modality-specific embedding spaces by matching their affinity distributions over a shared 2D topology-preserving prototype grid.
w3zAs5rvZZ.evidence: Evaluated across three multimodal datasets (including MM-Fi and sleep data) under full and missing-modality subject-wise protocols.
w3zAs5rvZZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like decoupling multimodal alignment from shared vector dimensionality via a 2D prototype grid and note competitive missing-modality results.
w3zAs5rvZZ.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the benefit of grid topology against an unstructured prototype baseline, and the paper omits critical details on how downstream classifiers handle missing-modality shift.

lXIB72o5CP.one_liner: Bidirectional teacher-student distillation on benign reasoning data measures behavioral safety imprinting and tests token-masking and rewriting mitigations.
lXIB72o5CP.problem: Knowledge distillation on task-focused teacher outputs can inadvertently transfer unintended behavioral or safety dispositions from teacher to student models.
lXIB72o5CP.method: The authors create harm-accepting and harm-avoiding variants of a base teacher, generate responses to ordinary reasoning and knowledge prompts unrelated to safety, and distill them into different student backbones. They then evaluate behavioral shifts and test mitigations including masking sparse divergence tokens, response rewriting, and post-distillation preference optimization.
lXIB72o5CP.key_idea: Distill benign reasoning outputs from opposing harm-accepting and harm-avoiding teachers into student models to isolate behavioral imprinting and test divergence-token masking.
lXIB72o5CP.evidence: Experiments across multiple teacher-student model families, safety and capability benchmarks, and three mitigation strategies (divergence-token masking, rewriting, SFT/DPO).
lXIB72o5CP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean bidirectional capability-controlled setup, cross-architecture experiments, and honest reporting of negative findings.
lXIB72o5CP.main_concern: Novelty relative to prior subliminal trait-transfer and divergence-token distillation studies is not cleanly isolated, and the manipulation relies on 22 hand-written scenarios without proving harm-specificity.

571ctY7Tob.one_liner: Pixel Contrast Flow integrates calibrated log-contrast increments via pixel-local exponential updates for threshold-consistent event camera representations.
571ctY7Tob.problem: Event-camera recognition models that rely on raw event counts degrade when sensor contrast thresholds change event multiplicity and timing for the same underlying motion.
571ctY7Tob.method: Pixel Contrast Flow (PCF) integrates calibrated log-contrast quanta into pixel-local states before spatial readout, using an exponential state update controlled by incoming contrast at each pixel and polarity. This update composes exactly when a contrast increment splits into simultaneous increments of equal total mass.
571ctY7Tob.key_idea: Applies pixel-local exponential state updates driven by calibrated contrast mass that compose exactly under threshold-induced event splitting.
571ctY7Tob.evidence: Evaluated on paired simulated Caltech101-CT event streams regenerated at different thresholds and a simulated ramp calibration test across 13 perturbation settings.
571ctY7Tob.claimed_gains: On paired simulated Caltech101-CT streams, PCF achieves 0.215 RelL2 feature drift, approximately 69% lower than Mass-GRU's 0.691, and 39.13% mean classification accuracy across 13 perturbation settings within 0.02 percentage points of generating-threshold accuracy.
571ctY7Tob.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that threshold-consistent event representation is a practical, well-motivated problem and that the semigroup exponential update and paired-threshold evaluation are well-principled.
571ctY7Tob.main_concern: All experiments rely solely on synthetic Caltech101-CT simulations without real event-camera recordings, non-classification tasks, or comparisons against standard event representations.

j8WfDtbimf.one_liner: VESTA constructs executable API environments and turn-level state-transition contracts to supervise SFT filtering and RL for tool-use agents.
j8WfDtbimf.problem: Supervising stateful tool-use agents via final outcomes alone misses intermediate execution errors, while tool-call matching alone fails to verify actual environment state changes.
j8WfDtbimf.method: VESTA builds executable environments from API specifications and synthesizes tasks executable-first, recording reference tool calls and expected environment states at each turn as state-transition contracts. These contracts drive SFT trajectory selection, policy-conditioned RL task selection, and RL reward computation without learned or LLM reward judges.
j8WfDtbimf.key_idea: Records turn-level reference tool calls and expected environment states as executable contracts for unified SFT filtering and judge-free RL rewards.
j8WfDtbimf.evidence: Evaluated across three Qwen3 model scales on BFCL-v3 Multi-Turn, ACEBench-Agent, and tau^2-Bench.
j8WfDtbimf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusable, execution-grounded state-transition supervision without LLM judges is well-engineered and shows consistent gains across model scales and benchmarks.
j8WfDtbimf.main_concern: Reviewers note limited differentiation from prior synthetic executable environment pipelines, manually templated workflow structures, and missing controls isolating joint state-transition supervision from SFT distillation or outcome-only filtering.

OT3ZbA1N3U.one_liner: Graph deep learning framework trains spatiotemporal forecasters across multiple sampled aggregation hierarchies as multi-task regularization.
OT3ZbA1N3U.problem: Existing hierarchical spatiotemporal forecasting architectures train on a single fixed aggregation structure, causing over-specialization and limiting generalization across hierarchies.
OT3ZbA1N3U.method: The authors propose a graph deep learning framework that samples and jointly trains across multiple aggregation hierarchies as multi-task regularization to learn representations shared across structures. They also pair this with an approach to handle the computational cost of enforcing coherence across sampled hierarchies.
OT3ZbA1N3U.key_idea: Jointly trains a graph spatiotemporal forecaster across multiple sampled aggregation hierarchies as multi-task regularization.
OT3ZbA1N3U.evidence: Evaluated on standard spatiotemporal forecasting benchmark datasets, measuring performance as the number of training hierarchies varies.
OT3ZbA1N3U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find multi-hierarchy training for spatiotemporal forecasting an interesting idea that empirically improves accuracy as more training hierarchies are sampled.
OT3ZbA1N3U.main_concern: Reviewers question the framing and evaluation, noting missing standard hierarchical forecasting datasets, limited separation from HiGP and forecast averaging, and unclear fairness when averaging across 20 hierarchies versus a single fixed hierarchy.

msOhhRrOJW.one_liner: MyPCBench evaluates computer-use agents as personal assistants across 184 tasks in a persona-seeded Linux desktop with 17 web apps.
msOhhRrOJW.problem: Existing computer-use benchmarks test agents in impersonal environments and cannot evaluate logged-in web workflows requiring personal context and historical user data.
msOhhRrOJW.method: MyPCBench provides a Linux desktop populated with 17 simulated real-world web applications and a full desktop stack seeded for one persona (Michael Scott), with 184 tasks drawn from OpenClaw community requests. Task completion is graded by an LLM-as-a-Judge using 1,191 rubric items.
msOhhRrOJW.key_idea: Constructs a densely populated, persona-seeded Linux desktop and 17 simulated logged-in web apps with 184 cross-application tasks graded by rubric-based LLM judges.
msOhhRrOJW.evidence: Benchmarks ten closed- and open-weight models using shared computer and shell tools, with human validation of the rubric judge.
msOhhRrOJW.claimed_gains: The highest perfect rate is 58.2% (Claude Opus 4.6) followed by GPT-5.6-sol at 55.4%, and the rubric judge agrees with human grading on 94.5% of sampled rubric items.
msOhhRrOJW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the densely populated, internally consistent cross-application desktop environment with historical dependencies is a well-crafted resource.
msOhhRrOJW.main_concern: Reviewers question whether a single persona truly measures personalization rather than long-horizon data lookup, cite limited differentiation from prior benchmarks like iOSWorld, and note limited judge calibration and inter-annotator statistics.

bD9XDliNAm.one_liner: RewardFlow aligns flow-matching models to reward-induced trajectory distributions using a prompt-conditioned partition function and step-wise KL constraints.
bD9XDliNAm.problem: GRPO-style scalar reward maximization in flow-based text-to-image post-training concentrates policies on few samples, hurting diversity, unseen-metric generalization, and multi-reward stability.
bD9XDliNAm.method: RewardFlow forms a reward-induced distribution over sampled denoising trajectories and aligns the flow policy to this distribution so multiple high-quality trajectories receive positive signal. It stabilizes training with a warm-started learnable prompt-conditioned partition function for reward calibration and a step-wise KL constraint to preserve the pretrained flow prior.
bD9XDliNAm.key_idea: Matches the flow policy to a reward-induced trajectory distribution calibrated by a learnable prompt-conditioned partition function and step-wise KL regularization.
bD9XDliNAm.evidence: Evaluated on SD3.5-M and FLUX.1-dev under single-reward and heterogeneous multi-reward settings, measuring in-domain and held-out preference metrics.
bD9XDliNAm.claimed_gains: Under multi-reward training on SD3.5-M, RewardFlow improves HPS-v2.1 from 0.326 to 0.362 and unseen Aesthetic Score from 6.226 to 6.470 over Flow-GRPO.
bD9XDliNAm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that RewardFlow achieves strong empirical gains on SD3.5-M and FLUX.1-dev, especially in multi-reward alignment and held-out preference metrics.
bD9XDliNAm.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the reward-tilted target distribution is equivalent to KL-regularized reward maximization / FlowRL / GFlowNet-TB, and that practical modifications depart from the stated theoretical objective.
